figma-design-to-code.title: Figma (design-to-code)
figma-design-to-code.content:
## Overview Emergent can convert your Figma designs directly into working code. Share a Figma URL in chat and the platform will analyze the design, extract components, styles, and layout structure, then generate production-ready React code that matches your mockup. This guide walks you through importing a Figma design and refining the generated implementation. Figma-to-code works for both web and mobile designs. The platform auto-detects the design type (viewport, frame names, component structure) and generates the appropriate stack. ## Before you start - **Figma file permissions**: Your design must be shared with "Anyone with the link can view" or public. Private files will return a permissions error. - **Frame structure**: Organize your design into clearly named frames (e.g. `Homepage`, `Dashboard`, `Mobile - Login`). Emergent treats each top-level frame as a candidate page or screen. - **Design system**: If your design uses Figma components, variants, and auto-layout, the generated code will reflect that structure with reusable React components. ## How to convert a Figma design In Figma, click **Share** → **Copy link**. Ensure the file is publicly viewable or set to "Anyone with the link." In your Emergent workspace chat, paste the Figma URL and describe what you want: ``` https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/My-Design Build the homepage from this design ``` You can reference specific frames by name: ``` https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Mobile-App Implement the "Onboarding Flow" screens ``` Emergent will: - Parse the Figma file structure (frames, layers, text, styles) - Extract colors, typography, spacing values - Identify interactive elements (buttons, inputs, nav) - Generate React components with Tailwind CSS (web) or React Native (mobile) - Create placeholder logic for any buttons or forms This typically takes 30–90 seconds depending on design complexity. The generated app opens in the preview pane. Compare it side-by-side with your Figma design to catch layout differences, missing elements, or styling mismatches. Describe any changes: ``` The hero image should be full-width Move the CTA button to the right Use the exact blue from the design: #3B82F6 ``` Emergent will adjust the code and refresh the preview. You can iterate as many times as needed. ## What gets converted | Design element | How it's handled | |----------------|------------------| | **Frames** | Top-level frames → pages or screens; nested frames → layout sections | | **Text layers** | `

`, `

`, `` with font family, size, weight, color preserved | | **Images** | `` tags with placeholder `src` (you can swap in real assets later) | | **Buttons** | `

what-is-emergent.title: What is Emergent?
what-is-emergent.content:
## Welcome to Emergent

Emergent is an **agentic vibecoding platform** where you describe what you want to build in natural language, and AI agents handle the rest—writing code, running tests, and deploying your application.

Instead of writing code line-by-line, you chat with Emergent about your vision. The platform's AI agents translate your intent into working software, manage the technical details, and get your app live.

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Describe your idea">
    Tell Emergent what you want to build in plain language. No technical knowledge required—just explain the problem you're solving or the experience you want to create.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="AI agents build it">
    Emergent's agents write the code, set up databases, configure APIs, and handle deployment. They work autonomously, making technical decisions and implementing features based on your description.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Test and iterate">
    Review the working app, provide feedback, and refine. The agents respond to your notes and requests, making changes until the app matches your vision.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Deploy and scale">
    Your app goes live with hosting, authentication, databases, and infrastructure managed by the platform. Focus on users and features, not DevOps.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Vibecoding vs. traditional development

<Columns cols={2}>
  <Card title="Traditional coding" icon="code">
    - Write every line of code yourself
    - Configure build tools, dependencies, environments
    - Manually test across devices and scenarios
    - Set up hosting, CI/CD, monitoring
    - Debug infrastructure issues
    - Weeks or months to first version
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Vibecoding with Emergent" icon="sparkles">
    - Describe what you want in chat
    - AI handles implementation details
    - Automated testing and quality checks
    - Instant deployment and scaling
    - Infrastructure managed for you
    - Working apps in hours or days
  </Card>
</Columns>

<Tip title="Focus on what, not how">
Vibecoding means focusing on *what* you want your app to do, not *how* to implement it. Describe features, user flows, and goals—the agents handle the technical execution.
</Tip>

## What you can build

Emergent supports a wide range of applications, from simple prototypes to production-ready products:

- Mobile and web apps with custom UI/UX
- AI-powered features and workflows
- Database-backed services with authentication
- API integrations and third-party connections
- Media-rich experiences with images, video, and audio

<Info>
Learn more about the types of apps you can create in [What kind of apps you can build?](/what-kind-of-apps-you-can-build)
</Info>

## Built-in capabilities

Emergent provides essential platform features out of the box:

- **[Authentication](/emergent-auth-built-in)** — User sign-up, login, and session management
- **[Database](/database-mongodb)** — MongoDB storage with automatic schema management
- **[AI integrations](/the-universal-llm-key)** — Access to LLMs, image generation, and more
- **[Media generation](/ai-media-generation-image-video-audio)** — Create images, video, and audio with AI
- **[Custom domains](/custom-domain)** — Deploy apps on your own domain
- **[Wingman assistant](/what-is-wingman)** — AI help for users inside your app

## Getting started

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Explore the workspace" icon="compass" href="/a-tour-of-the-workspace">
    Take a tour of Emergent's interface and key features
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Understand Jobs" icon="briefcase" href="/what-is-a-job">
    Learn how AI agents organize and execute work
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Browse the glossary" icon="book-open" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
    Familiarize yourself with platform terminology
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="What and How framework" icon="lightbulb" href="/what-and-how">
    Master the art of describing your vision effectively
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

<Note>
Emergent handles the complexity of modern software development—deployment pipelines, database migrations, API configuration, testing—so you can focus on creating value for your users.
</Note>
what-is-emergent.description: Emergent is an agentic vibecoding platform: you describe what you want, and AI agents build, test, and deploy it. Positioning vs traditional coding.

sendgrid.title: SendGrid
sendgrid.content: ## Overview SendGrid is a cloud-based email delivery platform that enables your Emergent app to send transactional and marketing emails reliably. Common use cases include password resets, order confirmations, notifications, and automated email campaigns. This guide shows you how to integrate SendGrid with your Emergent app using environment variables and the SendGrid API. SendGrid offers a free tier with 100 emails per day, which is sufficient for testing and small applications. Production apps typically require a paid plan. ## Prerequisites Before you begin, you'll need: - A SendGrid account ([sign up](https://signup.sendgrid.com/)) - An active Emergent project - Basic familiarity with environment variables ## Setting up SendGrid 1. Log in to your [SendGrid dashboard](https://app.sendgrid.com/) 2. Navigate to **Settings** → **API Keys** 3. Click **Create API Key** 4. Choose **Restricted Access** and enable **Mail Send** permissions (recommended for security) 5. Name your key (e.g., `emergent-production`) 6. Copy the generated API key immediately — it won't be shown again SendGrid requires you to verify the email address or domain you'll send from: 1. Go to **Settings** → **Sender Authentication** 2. For testing: verify a **Single Sender** email address 3. For production: set up **Domain Authentication** to improve deliverability Check your inbox for the verification email and follow the link. In the Emergent chat, add your SendGrid API key as an environment variable: > Add environment variable `SENDGRID_API_KEY` with value `SG.xxxxx...` Mark this variable as **secret** to prevent it from appearing in logs or client-side code. Store your verified sender email as an environment variable for easy reuse: > Add environment variable `SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL` with value `noreply@yourdomain.com` Optionally add `SENDGRID_FROM_NAME` for a friendly sender name. ## Sending emails from your app Once configured, you can send emails using the SendGrid Node.js SDK or REST API. Here's how to implement common email scenarios: ### Transactional emails ```javascript Node.js (SDK) const sgMail = require('@sendgrid/mail'); sgMail.setApiKey(process.env.SENDGRID_API_KEY); const msg = { to: 'user@example.com', from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Your order confirmation', text: 'Thank you for your order #12345', html: 'Thank you for your order #12345', }; await sgMail.send(msg); ``` ```python Python import os from sendgrid import SendGridAPIClient from sendgrid.helpers.mail import Mail message = Mail( from_email=os.environ.get('SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL'), to_emails='user@example.com', subject='Your order confirmation', html_content='Thank you for your order #12345' ) sg = SendGridAPIClient(os.environ.get('SENDGRID_API_KEY')) response = sg.send(message) ``` ### Using templates SendGrid's Dynamic Templates let you design emails visually and populate them with data: ```javascript const msg = { to: 'user@example.com', from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, templateId: 'd-abc123def456', dynamicTemplateData: { userName: 'Alice', orderNumber: '12345', orderTotal: '$99.00', }, }; await sgMail.send(msg); ``` Create templates in the SendGrid dashboard under **Email API** → **Dynamic Templates**. Copy the template ID (starts with `d-`) and pass it in your code. ## Testing email delivery ### Test mode During development, consider these strategies to avoid sending real emails: SendGrid's sandbox mode validates requests without sending actual emails: ```javascript const msg = { // ... your message mailSettings: { sandboxMode: { enable: true, }, }, }; ``` Send all development emails to a test address: ```javascript const to = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? userEmail : 'test@yourdomain.com'; ``` ### Monitoring delivery Track email activity in the SendGrid dashboard: 1. Go to **Activity** to see recent sends, bounces, and opens 2. Check **Suppressions** for bounced or unsubscribed addresses 3. Review **Statistics** for delivery rates and engagement metrics High bounce rates can damage your sender reputation. Regularly clean your email list and honor unsubscribe requests. ## Common patterns in Emergent apps ### Password reset flow ```javascript // Generate reset token const resetToken = generateSecureToken(); const resetUrl = `${process.env.APP_URL}/reset-password?token=${resetToken}`; await sgMail.send({ to: user.email, from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Password reset requested', html: `Click here to reset your password: ${resetUrl}`, }); ``` ### Scheduled notifications Use SendGrid's `sendAt` parameter to schedule emails for a future time (up to 72 hours): ```javascript const sendTime = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600; // 1 hour from now const msg = { to: 'user@example.com', from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Reminder: Your appointment is in 1 hour', text: 'See you soon!', sendAt: sendTime, }; ``` ### Batch sending Send the same email to multiple recipients efficiently: ```javascript const msg = { to: ['user1@example.com', 'user2@example.com', 'user3@example.com'], from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Team announcement', text: 'Check out our new feature!', }; ``` For large batches (1000+ recipients), consider using SendGrid's batch ID feature to cancel or pause sends if needed. ## Troubleshooting - Verify your sender identity in the SendGrid dashboard - Check the **Activity** feed for delivery status and errors - Ensure `SENDGRID_API_KEY` is set correctly and has **Mail Send** permissions - Look for emails in spam/junk folders (improve this with domain authentication) Your API key likely lacks the necessary permissions. Create a new key with **Mail Send** enabled under **Restricted Access**. Free accounts are limited to 100 emails per day. Upgrade your SendGrid plan or implement retry logic with exponential backoff for production apps. Include an unsubscribe link in marketing emails to comply with regulations: ```javascript const msg = { // ... your message trackingSettings: { subscriptionTracking: { enable: true, }, }, }; ``` SendGrid automatically adds an unsubscribe footer when enabled. ## Best practices Design emails visually in SendGrid and keep HTML out of your codebase. Templates are easier to update and A/B test. Set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records to improve deliverability and avoid the spam folder. Wrap `sgMail.send()` in try-catch blocks and log failures for investigation. Don't block user workflows on email delivery. Regularly check bounced and unsubscribed addresses. Remove them from your database to maintain a healthy sender reputation. ## Next steps - Set up [domain authentication](https://docs.sendgrid.com/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-domain-authentication) for better deliverability - Explore [Dynamic Templates](https://docs.sendgrid.com/ui/sending-email/how-to-send-an-email-with-dynamic-templates) for professional email designs - Configure [webhooks](https://docs.sendgrid.com/for-developers/tracking-events/getting-started-event-webhook) to receive delivery events in your app - Review SendGrid's [email best practices](https://sendgrid.com/blog/10-tips-to-improve-your-email-deliverability/) guide You're now ready to send reliable, professional emails from your Emergent app using SendGrid.

google-suite.title: Google Suite
google-suite.content:
## Overview

Google Suite integration allows your Emergent app to access Google services including Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Docs, Sheets, and other Workspace products. This integration uses OAuth 2.0 for secure authentication and requires configuration in the Google Cloud Console.

<Note>
Before configuring Google Suite, ensure you have a Google Cloud project and billing enabled. Some Google APIs require a verified domain for production use.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

- A Google Cloud account with a project created
- Admin access to your Emergent app
- The specific Google APIs enabled that you plan to use (Gmail API, Calendar API, Drive API, etc.)

## Setup Process

<Steps>

<Step title="Enable Google APIs">
Navigate to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com) and select your project. In the **APIs & Services** section, enable the specific Google APIs your app needs:

- **Gmail API** — for email operations
- **Google Calendar API** — for calendar access
- **Google Drive API** — for file storage and management
- **Google Docs/Sheets/Slides API** — for document operations

Click **Enable API** for each service you require.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure OAuth consent screen">
In the Google Cloud Console, go to **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**:

1. Choose **External** user type (or **Internal** if using Google Workspace)
2. Enter your app name, user support email, and developer contact
3. Add authorized domains (include your Emergent app domain)
4. Configure scopes based on the APIs you enabled
5. Add test users if your app is in testing mode

<Warning>
Apps in testing mode are limited to 100 test users. Submit for verification to remove this limit and make your integration available to all users.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Create OAuth credentials">
Navigate to **APIs & Services → Credentials** and create OAuth 2.0 credentials:

1. Click **Create Credentials → OAuth client ID**
2. Select **Web application** as the application type
3. Add authorized redirect URIs — use the callback URL provided in your Emergent integration settings
4. Save and note your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
</Step>

<Step title="Add credentials to Emergent">
In your Emergent app dashboard, navigate to **Integrations → Google Suite**:

1. Paste your Google OAuth **Client ID**
2. Paste your Google OAuth **Client Secret**
3. Select which Google services to enable
4. Save the configuration

Your app will now use these credentials to authenticate users via Google.
</Step>

<Step title="Test the integration">
Trigger the Google authentication flow in your app to verify the setup:

1. Click the sign-in or connect button in your app
2. You should be redirected to Google's consent screen
3. Grant the requested permissions
4. Verify you're redirected back to your app with access granted

Check your app logs for any authentication errors.
</Step>

</Steps>

## Service-Specific Configuration

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Gmail">
The Gmail API requires the following scopes for common operations:

- `gmail.readonly` — read-only access to messages
- `gmail.send` — send email on behalf of the user
- `gmail.modify` — read and modify (but not delete) messages
- `gmail.compose` — create and send drafts

Configure these scopes in your OAuth consent screen under **Scopes**.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Google Calendar">
For calendar integration, add these scopes:

- `calendar.readonly` — read-only calendar access
- `calendar.events` — read and write calendar events
- `calendar` — full calendar access

Calendar API supports event creation, updates, deletion, and real-time sync.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Google Drive">
Drive API scopes control file access levels:

- `drive.readonly` — read-only access to all files
- `drive.file` — access only to files created by your app
- `drive` — full Drive access
- `drive.metadata.readonly` — read file metadata only

<Tip>
Use the most restrictive scope that meets your needs. Users are more likely to grant limited permissions.
</Tip>
</Tab>

<Tab title="Docs, Sheets & Slides">
Document APIs share similar scope patterns:

- `documents.readonly` / `spreadsheets.readonly` / `presentations.readonly`
- `documents` / `spreadsheets` / `presentations` — full access
- `drive.file` — access to files created by your app

These APIs allow programmatic creation and editing of Google Workspace documents.
</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Common Issues

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Redirect URI mismatch error">
This occurs when the callback URL in your Emergent settings doesn't match the authorized redirect URIs in Google Cloud Console. Ensure the URLs match exactly, including the protocol (`https://`) and trailing slashes.

Copy the exact redirect URI from your Emergent integration settings and paste it into the Google Cloud Console authorized URIs list.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Access blocked: App not verified">
Google displays this warning for unverified apps requesting sensitive scopes. During development, click **Advanced → Go to [App Name] (unsafe)** to proceed.

For production apps, submit your OAuth consent screen for Google verification. This process can take several weeks.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Insufficient permissions / 403 errors">
Verify that:

1. The required API is enabled in Google Cloud Console
2. The necessary scopes are configured in your OAuth consent screen
3. Users have granted all requested permissions during authentication
4. Your Google Cloud project has billing enabled (required for some APIs)
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Quota exceeded errors">
Google APIs have usage quotas and rate limits. Check your quota usage in the Google Cloud Console under **APIs & Services → Dashboard**.

Request quota increases if you're hitting limits, or implement rate limiting and caching in your app.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

## Best Practices

- **Request minimal scopes** — only ask for permissions your app actively uses
- **Handle token refresh** — OAuth tokens expire; implement refresh logic
- **Store tokens securely** — never expose access tokens in client-side code
- **Respect rate limits** — implement exponential backoff for API requests
- **Use service accounts** — for server-to-server operations without user authentication
- **Monitor quota usage** — track API consumption to avoid unexpected quota exhaustion

## Related Resources

<CardGroup cols={2}>

<Card title="Google Auth" icon="key" href="/google-auth">
General Google authentication setup and troubleshooting
</Card>

<Card title="Custom Domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Configure a custom domain for OAuth callbacks
</Card>

</CardGroup>

## Further Reading

- [Google Workspace APIs Documentation](https://developers.google.com/workspace)
- [OAuth 2.0 Scopes Reference](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/scopes)
- [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com)

supabase.title: Supabase
supabase.content:
## Overview

Supabase is an open-source Firebase alternative that provides a PostgreSQL database, authentication, instant APIs, edge functions, realtime subscriptions, and storage. Emergent supports Supabase as a backend integration, allowing your AI-built applications to leverage enterprise-grade data storage and user authentication.

This guide walks you through connecting your Emergent app to Supabase and using its core features.

## What you can do with Supabase

- **PostgreSQL database**: Store structured data with the full power of a relational database
- **Built-in authentication**: Email/password, OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, etc.), magic links
- **Realtime subscriptions**: Listen to database changes and update your UI instantly
- **Row-level security**: Define fine-grained access policies directly in the database
- **Storage**: Upload and serve user files with access control
- **Edge functions**: Run server-side logic close to your users

## Prerequisites

- A Supabase account ([sign up free](https://supabase.com))
- A Supabase project with your database and auth configured
- Your Supabase project URL and anon/public API key (found in Project Settings → API)

## Connecting Supabase to your Emergent app

<Steps>
<Step title="Add Supabase credentials to your app">
In your Emergent chat, tell the AI to add Supabase as a data source. You'll need:

- **Project URL**: `https://your-project.supabase.co`
- **Anon key**: Your public API key (safe to expose in client code)

Example prompt:
```
Add Supabase integration. My project URL is https://abc123.supabase.co 
and anon key is eyJhbGc... Use it for user authentication and to store 
tasks in a 'tasks' table.
```

The AI will install the Supabase client library and configure the connection.
</Step>

<Step title="Define your database schema">
Describe your data model in chat, and the AI will either:

- Generate SQL migrations to run in the Supabase SQL Editor, or
- Use the Supabase client to create tables programmatically

<Tip>
For production apps, use Supabase's migration system in the Dashboard → Database → Migrations. This keeps your schema under version control.
</Tip>

Example:
```
Create a 'profiles' table with columns: id (uuid), email (text), 
display_name (text), created_at (timestamp). Add a foreign key 
to auth.users(id).
```
</Step>

<Step title="Set up authentication">
Tell the AI which auth methods you want (email/password, OAuth, magic links). The AI will:

- Configure the Supabase auth client
- Create sign-up, sign-in, and sign-out flows
- Handle session persistence
- Protect routes that require authentication

Example:
```
Add email/password sign-up and sign-in. Show a login form on the 
home page. After login, redirect to /dashboard.
```
</Step>

<Step title="Implement data operations">
Describe CRUD operations in natural language. The AI translates them into Supabase queries.

Example prompts:
```
When a user creates a task, insert a row in the tasks table with 
title, description, user_id, and completed=false.
```

```
On the dashboard, fetch all tasks for the current user where 
completed=false, ordered by created_at desc.
```

The AI will use `supabase.from('table').select()`, `.insert()`, `.update()`, and `.delete()` methods.
</Step>

<Step title="Add row-level security (RLS)">
For secure multi-user apps, describe access rules and the AI will generate RLS policies or guide you to add them in the Supabase Dashboard.

Example:
```
Enable RLS on the tasks table. Users can only see and edit their own tasks.
```

<Warning title="Enable RLS for sensitive data">
Without row-level security, any client with the anon key can read or modify all rows. Always enable RLS policies for tables containing user data.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Test and iterate">
Use Emergent's preview to test authentication flows and data operations. If something doesn't work, describe the issue in chat and the AI will debug and fix it.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common patterns

### Realtime subscriptions

To listen for live database changes:

```
When a new task is inserted, append it to the task list in realtime 
without refreshing the page.
```

The AI will set up a Supabase subscription using `.on('INSERT', callback)`.

### File storage

To upload and serve images or documents:

```
Add a profile picture upload. Store images in a Supabase storage bucket 
called 'avatars' and display the user's avatar in the header.
```

The AI will configure storage buckets and handle file uploads with `supabase.storage.from('bucket').upload()`.

### Server-side logic with Edge Functions

For operations that shouldn't run in the browser (webhooks, scheduled jobs, sensitive business logic):

```
Create a Supabase Edge Function that sends a daily email summary 
of completed tasks.
```

<Note>
Emergent can generate the function code, but you'll deploy it manually via the Supabase CLI or Dashboard.
</Note>

## Environment variables

The AI stores Supabase credentials as environment variables:

- `SUPABASE_URL`
- `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (for admin operations, **never expose client-side**)

These are automatically injected at runtime. You don't need to configure them manually unless deploying outside Emergent.

## Comparison with other integrations

| Feature | Supabase | [MongoDB](/database-mongodb) |
|---------|----------|------------------------------|
| Data model | Relational (SQL) | Document (NoSQL) |
| Built-in auth | ✅ Yes | ❌ No (use separate service) |
| Realtime | ✅ Native subscriptions | Requires Change Streams setup |
| File storage | ✅ Built-in | Separate GridFS or S3 |
| Best for | Structured data, user auth | Flexible schemas, rapid iteration |

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Error: Invalid API key">
Check that you're using the **anon key** (not the service role key) for client-side code. Verify the key in Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Users can see each other's data">
Enable row-level security (RLS) policies on your tables. In the Supabase Dashboard, go to Authentication → Policies and create rules like:

```sql
CREATE POLICY "Users see own tasks" ON tasks
  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Authentication redirects not working">
Make sure your Supabase project has the correct Site URL and Redirect URLs configured in Authentication → URL Configuration. For Emergent preview URLs, you may need to add wildcard patterns.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Realtime subscriptions not triggering">
Confirm that Realtime is enabled for your table in Database → Replication. Also check that RLS policies allow the user to SELECT the rows they're subscribing to.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Database (MongoDB)" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
Compare with MongoDB for document-based data models
</Card>
<Card title="Custom domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Deploy your Supabase-powered app on your own domain
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Additional resources

- [Supabase Documentation](https://supabase.com/docs)
- [Supabase Auth Helpers](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-helpers)
- [Row Level Security Guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/row-level-security)

twilio.title: Twilio
twilio.content:
## Overview

Twilio is a cloud communications platform that enables your Emergent app to send SMS messages, make voice calls, and deliver notifications. This integration is ideal for apps that need to verify users via SMS, send transactional alerts, or implement two-factor authentication.

<Note>
Twilio charges per message or call. Review [Twilio's pricing](https://www.twilio.com/pricing) before implementing SMS or voice features at scale.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Before integrating Twilio, you'll need:

- A Twilio account ([sign up here](https://www.twilio.com/try-twilio))
- A Twilio phone number (purchased from your Twilio console)
- Your Twilio Account SID and Auth Token (found in your Twilio console dashboard)

## Setting up Twilio in Emergent

<Steps>
<Step title="Obtain your Twilio credentials">
Log in to your [Twilio Console](https://console.twilio.com) and locate your **Account SID** and **Auth Token** on the dashboard. Keep these values handy — you'll need them in the next step.

If you haven't already, purchase a phone number from **Phone Numbers → Buy a Number** in the Twilio console. This number will be the sender for your SMS messages.
</Step>

<Step title="Add credentials to your Emergent app">
In your Emergent chat, tell the AI agents to add Twilio environment variables:

```
Add these environment variables:
- TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID: <your Account SID>
- TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN: <your Auth Token>
- TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER: <your purchased phone number in E.164 format>
```

The agents will securely store these in your app's environment configuration.
</Step>

<Step title="Describe your SMS or voice feature">
Tell Emergent what you want to build. For example:

- _"Add SMS verification when users sign up — send a 6-digit code to their phone number."_
- _"Send an SMS notification when an order ships, including the tracking number."_
- _"Let users opt in to receive weekly SMS reminders about their appointments."_

The AI agents will scaffold the necessary API calls using the Twilio Node.js or Python SDK (depending on your app's stack).
</Step>

<Step title="Test your integration">
Once the agents deploy your changes, test the SMS or voice functionality in your app. Check your Twilio console's **Logs → Messaging** or **Logs → Calls** to confirm messages are being sent and to debug any delivery issues.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common use cases

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Phone verification" icon="shield-check">
Send a one-time passcode via SMS during signup or login to verify a user's phone number.
</Card>

<Card title="Transactional alerts" icon="bell">
Notify users of important events—order confirmations, password resets, appointment reminders.
</Card>

<Card title="Two-factor authentication" icon="lock">
Enhance security by requiring an SMS code in addition to a password when users log in.
</Card>

<Card title="Marketing campaigns" icon="megaphone">
Send promotional messages to opted-in users. Ensure compliance with local regulations (e.g., TCPA, GDPR).
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Example implementation

Below is an example of how Emergent agents might implement an SMS verification flow using Twilio's Node.js SDK:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript Node.js
import twilio from 'twilio';

const client = twilio(
  process.env.TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID,
  process.env.TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
);

export async function sendVerificationCode(phoneNumber, code) {
  await client.messages.create({
    body: `Your verification code is: ${code}`,
    from: process.env.TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER,
    to: phoneNumber
  });
}
```

```python Python
from twilio.rest import Client
import os

client = Client(
    os.environ['TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID'],
    os.environ['TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN']
)

def send_verification_code(phone_number: str, code: str):
    client.messages.create(
        body=f'Your verification code is: {code}',
        from_=os.environ['TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER'],
        to=phone_number
    )
```
</CodeGroup>

<Info>
Phone numbers must be in E.164 format (e.g., `+14155552671`). Emergent agents typically validate and format numbers automatically when you describe your feature requirements.
</Info>

## Testing and debugging

<Accordion title="Messages aren't being delivered">
- Verify your phone number is in E.164 format with a country code (e.g., `+1` for US).
- Check Twilio's console under **Logs → Messaging** for error codes.
- Ensure your Twilio account is not in trial mode or has sufficient credit balance.
- Confirm the recipient's carrier isn't blocking messages (some carriers filter shortcodes or toll-free numbers).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Environment variables not loading">
If your app can't read `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` or other variables, ask the agents:

_"Verify my Twilio environment variables are set correctly."_

The agents will check your configuration and redeploy if needed.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Rate limiting or throttling errors">
Twilio enforces rate limits on message sending. If you're sending high volumes, consider:

- Queueing messages with a background job processor.
- Requesting a rate limit increase from Twilio support.
- Using Twilio's Messaging Services for better throughput.
</Accordion>

## Best practices

- **Validate phone numbers** before sending to avoid wasted credits on invalid destinations.
- **Respect opt-outs**: Honor unsubscribe requests immediately and maintain a suppression list.
- **Use short, clear messages**: SMS has a 160-character limit (longer messages are split and billed per segment).
- **Monitor delivery status**: Use Twilio webhooks to track delivery, failures, and user replies.
- **Secure your credentials**: Never commit `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` to version control. Emergent stores environment variables securely for you.

## Compliance and regulations

<Warning>
SMS marketing is subject to legal restrictions in many countries. In the US, you must obtain explicit consent before sending promotional messages (TCPA). In the EU, GDPR requires clear consent and easy opt-out mechanisms.

Always consult legal counsel if you're sending marketing or promotional messages.
</Warning>

## Next steps

- Explore Twilio's [Verify API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify/api) for built-in OTP workflows.
- Add WhatsApp or Facebook Messenger support via Twilio's Programmable Messaging.
- Integrate Twilio Voice to build interactive voice response (IVR) systems or place outbound calls.

<Tip>
You can extend your Twilio integration by describing additional features in chat. For example: _"Add a webhook to log SMS replies in our database"_ or _"Send an email fallback if SMS delivery fails."_
</Tip>

enterprise-plan-features.title: Enterprise plan & features
enterprise-plan-features.content:
## Overview

The **Enterprise plan** is designed for organizations that need advanced security, compliance, dedicated infrastructure, and custom commercial terms. It includes all features from lower tiers plus single sign-on, tenant isolation, audit logging, and flexible credit pooling.

Enterprise is sold as an annual contract with custom pricing. Contact your account manager or [enterprise@emergent.com](mailto:enterprise@emergent.com) to discuss your requirements.

---

## Key features

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="SAML 2.0 SSO" icon="shield-check">
    Centralized authentication via Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, or any SAML 2.0 identity provider.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Dedicated infrastructure" icon="server">
    Isolated Kubernetes clusters for your organization—no resource sharing with other tenants.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Audit logs" icon="file-search">
    12-month retention of user activity, deployments, and admin actions. Export to CSV or JSON.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Flexible credit pooling" icon="piggy-bank">
    Organization-wide cumulative credit caps and shared billing across all teams.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Single sign-on (SAML 2.0)

Enterprise workspaces can enforce SSO with any SAML 2.0–compatible identity provider. Supported IdPs include:

- **Okta**
- **Azure Active Directory** (Microsoft Entra ID)
- **Google Workspace**
- Any other SAML 2.0 provider (OneLogin, PingIdentity, etc.)

Once SSO is configured, workspace members must authenticate through your IdP to access Emergent. You can optionally disable password-based login and enforce MFA policies at the IdP level.

<Note>
SSO configuration is handled by the Emergent support team during onboarding. You will provide your SAML metadata URL or XML file, and we will supply an Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL and Entity ID.
</Note>

---

## Dedicated Kubernetes clusters

Enterprise customers receive **tenant-isolated infrastructure**:

- Your workspaces, apps, and data run on dedicated Kubernetes nodes.
- No compute or memory sharing with other Emergent customers.
- Option to deploy in a specific cloud region (subject to availability).

This isolation ensures predictable performance, compliance with data-residency requirements, and reduced risk of noisy-neighbor effects.

<Info>
Dedicated clusters are provisioned during the onboarding process. Migration of existing workspaces to dedicated infrastructure is supported—contact your account manager for a migration plan.
</Info>

---

## Audit logs

Enterprise workspaces include a **12-month audit trail** of key events:

| Event type | Examples |
|------------|----------|
| **Authentication** | User login, SSO authentication, session expiry |
| **Workspace changes** | Member added/removed, role changed, workspace settings updated |
| **App lifecycle** | App created, deployed, preview launched, deleted |
| **Credit usage** | Credit purchase, recharge, cap adjustment |
| **Admin actions** | SSO config changed, audit log exported, custom domain added |

### Exporting logs

Workspace admins can export audit logs to **CSV** or **JSON** from the **Settings → Audit** panel. Logs are retained for 12 months; older entries are automatically archived.

<Tip>
For real-time SIEM integration, contact your account manager about webhook delivery of audit events (available as a custom add-on).
</Tip>

---

## Cumulative credit caps

Standard plans require each workspace to manage credits independently. Enterprise customers can configure **organization-wide credit pooling**:

- Set a single cumulative cap across all workspaces in your organization.
- Credits are drawn from a shared pool, simplifying budgeting and procurement.
- Auto-recharge policies apply at the organization level.

This is especially useful for large teams with many workspaces—finance can manage one budget line instead of tracking per-workspace balances.

<Note>
Credit pooling is opt-in. If you prefer isolated billing per workspace, you can keep the default workspace-level caps. See [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) for details on how credits work.
</Note>

---

## Custom terms, DPA & SLA

Enterprise agreements include:

- **Custom MSA** tailored to your procurement and legal requirements.
- **Data Processing Addendum (DPA)** for GDPR, CCPA, and other privacy regulations.
- **Service Level Agreement (SLA)** with uptime commitments and support response times.

Your account manager will work with your legal and procurement teams to finalize these documents before contract signature.

<Warning>
Enterprise features (SSO, dedicated infrastructure, audit logs) are activated only after the contract is fully executed and initial payment is received.
</Warning>

---

## Getting started

<Steps>
  <Step title="Contact sales">
    Email [enterprise@emergent.com](mailto:enterprise@emergent.com) or reach out to your account manager. Share your team size, compliance needs, and any specific infrastructure requirements.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Scoping & proposal">
    We'll schedule a call to understand your use case, map out SSO and infrastructure requirements, and provide a custom proposal with pricing.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Contract & onboarding">
    Legal review, DPA and SLA negotiation, contract signature. Our onboarding team will provision your dedicated cluster and configure SSO.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Migration & go-live">
    If you have existing workspaces, we'll migrate them to the new infrastructure. You can then enforce SSO and begin using audit logs and credit pooling.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
Typical onboarding takes 2–4 weeks from contract signature to production go-live, depending on infrastructure provisioning and SSO testing.
</Info>

---

## Frequently asked questions

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Can I trial Enterprise features before signing a contract?">
    Yes—we offer a 30-day proof-of-concept with SSO and audit logging enabled on a shared cluster. Contact your account manager to request a trial.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What happens if I exceed my cumulative credit cap?">
    If auto-recharge is enabled, the system will top up your pool automatically. If auto-recharge is off, all workspaces in the organization will be paused until you add more credits.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can I use multiple SSO providers (e.g., Okta and Azure AD)?">
    A single Enterprise workspace supports one SAML provider. If you need multiple IdPs (for example, after a merger), contact us about configuring separate workspaces or a custom federation setup.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Are dedicated clusters available in all regions?">
    We currently support dedicated deployments in **US East**, **EU West**, and **Asia Pacific**. Other regions may be available on request—contact your account manager.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I enforce SSO for all workspace members?">
    After SSO is configured, navigate to **Settings → Authentication** and toggle **Enforce SSO**. This disables password login and redirects all users to your IdP.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Credit expiry & recharging" icon="credit-card" href="/credit-expiry-recharging">
    Understand how credits work, auto-recharge policies, and expiry rules.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Google Suite" icon="building" href="/google-suite">
    Team collaboration and shared workspaces (available on all plans).
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

channels-web-telegram-whatsapp-imessage-.title: Channels (Web, Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, Slack)
channels-web-telegram-whatsapp-imessage-.content:
## Overview

Wingman works seamlessly across **Web, Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, and Slack**. Each channel supports text, voice messages, and images, with per-channel message limits and connection flows. You can also accept payments directly in-channel.

All channels share the same Wingman backend—conversations sync across platforms when users link their accounts.

---

## Supported Channels

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Web" icon="globe">
    Embed Wingman as a widget or full-page chat on your site.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Telegram" icon="send">
    Deploy as a Telegram bot; supports groups and channels.
  </Card>
  <Card title="WhatsApp" icon="message-circle">
    Connect via WhatsApp Business API; 24-hour session window applies.
  </Card>
  <Card title="iMessage" icon="message-square">
    iOS-native chat; requires Apple Business Chat approval.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Slack" icon="hash">
    Add Wingman to workspaces as a bot or app.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Message and Voice Limits

Each channel enforces different size and duration caps:

| Channel    | Text message max | Voice message max | Image max |
|------------|------------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Web        | 10,000 chars     | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |
| Telegram   | 4,096 chars      | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |
| WhatsApp   | 4,096 chars      | 10 MB / 2 min     | 5 MB      |
| iMessage   | 10,000 chars     | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |
| Slack      | 4,000 chars      | 10 MB / 2 min     | 10 MB     |

<Note>
Voice messages are automatically transcribed and processed; the 10 MB / 2 min limit applies to the uploaded audio file.
</Note>

---

## Connecting a Channel

<Steps>
  <Step title="Select your channel">
    In the Wingman workspace, go to **Settings → Channels** and choose which platform to connect.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Follow the platform-specific flow">
    - **Web**: Copy the embed snippet and paste into your site's HTML.
    - **Telegram**: Create a bot via BotFather, paste the token into Emergent.
    - **WhatsApp**: Register a WhatsApp Business account, verify your number, and connect via the Meta Business Suite.
    - **iMessage**: Apply for Apple Business Chat, then link your account in Settings.
    - **Slack**: Install the Emergent app from the Slack App Directory and authorize the workspace.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Test the connection">
    Send a test message from the channel; you should see it appear in the Wingman **Inbox** within seconds.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning title="WhatsApp 24-hour window">
After a user's last message, you have **24 hours** to reply freely. Outside that window, you can only send **pre-approved message templates** (configured in Meta Business Suite). Plan proactive outreach accordingly.
</Warning>

---

## In-Channel Payments

Wingman supports checkout flows directly inside messaging apps:

- **Telegram**: Payment bots via Telegram Payments (Stripe, PayPal).
- **WhatsApp**: Send a payment link; user completes checkout in-browser.
- **Web widget**: Inline Stripe or PayPal checkout modal.
- **Slack / iMessage**: Payment links open externally.

Configure payment providers in **Settings → Payments**. See [Payment methods & regional billing](/payment-methods-regional-billing) for details.

<Tip>
Telegram and Web channels offer the smoothest in-app payment experience; WhatsApp and iMessage redirect to a browser.
</Tip>

---

## Permission Prompts

Certain Wingman actions trigger **per-channel permission prompts** the first time a user invokes them:

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Location sharing">
    Wingman may ask "Share your location?" if the skill requires geo-data. Users approve once; preference is remembered per channel.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Camera / microphone (Web only)">
    Browser-based permissions appear when Wingman requests a photo or live voice recording.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Notification preferences">
    On Telegram and Slack, users can mute/unmute Wingman's proactive messages. WhatsApp notifications follow the OS contact-notification settings.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Contact sync (optional)">
    If Wingman offers to remember contacts (e.g. "Add John to your directory"), the user confirms once.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<Info>
Emergent never stores sensitive data (like raw voice files or exact GPS) beyond the lifetime of a single request unless the user explicitly grants storage permission.
</Info>

---

## Channel-Specific Considerations

### Telegram
- Supports **groups and channels**: Wingman can respond to @mentions or all messages (configure in bot settings).
- Rich media: stickers, polls, and inline keyboards work natively.

### WhatsApp
- **24-hour session window**: after that, only template messages are allowed.
- Number verification required via Meta; approval can take 1–2 business days.

### iMessage
- Requires **Apple Business Chat** approval (stricter vetting).
- Best for customer support; less suited for high-volume broadcast.

### Slack
- Appears as a bot in channels or DMs.
- Slash commands (`/wingman help`) can trigger shortcuts.

### Web
- Fully customizable widget appearance (colors, avatar, placement).
- No platform approval needed—deploy instantly.

---

## Syncing Conversations Across Channels

When a user links their Telegram, WhatsApp, and Web accounts (via email or phone number), Wingman **unifies the conversation history**:

1. User chats on Telegram, then continues on Web.
2. Wingman recognizes the same user and retrieves context.
3. The **Inbox** shows a single threaded conversation across all channels.

<Note>
Account linking is optional but recommended for a seamless experience. Users initiate linking by verifying their contact details in any channel.
</Note>

---

## Next Steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="What is Wingman" icon="circle-help" href="/what-is-wingman">
    Learn how Wingman's AI assistant works under the hood.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Payment methods" icon="credit-card" href="/payment-methods-regional-billing">
    Configure Stripe, PayPal, and regional billing.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

giphy.title: Giphy
giphy.content:
## Overview

Giphy is a popular GIF search and sharing platform that lets you integrate animated GIFs into your applications. The Giphy integration in Emergent allows your app to search, display, and embed GIFs from Giphy's extensive library.

This guide walks you through setting up the Giphy integration for your Emergent project.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- An Emergent project (web or mobile)
- A Giphy account (free or paid)
- A Giphy API key from the [Giphy Developers Portal](https://developers.giphy.com/)

<Note>
Giphy offers a free tier with rate limits suitable for development and small-scale applications. Check the Giphy Developers Portal for current usage limits and pricing.
</Note>

## Getting your Giphy API key

<Steps>
<Step title="Create a Giphy account">
Visit [developers.giphy.com](https://developers.giphy.com/) and sign up for a free account if you don't already have one.
</Step>

<Step title="Create an app in the Giphy Dashboard">
Once logged in, navigate to the **Dashboard** and click **Create an App**. Choose the type of app you're building:

- **API** for standard integration
- **SDK** if you plan to use Giphy's native SDKs

Provide a name and description for your app.
</Step>

<Step title="Copy your API key">
After creating the app, Giphy will generate an **API Key** for you. Copy this key — you'll need it in the next section.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Adding Giphy to your Emergent project

<Steps>
<Step title="Open your project settings">
In the Emergent chat interface, tell the AI you want to add Giphy integration. For example:

```
Add Giphy integration so users can search and insert GIFs
```

The AI agents will guide you through the setup process.
</Step>

<Step title="Provide your API key">
When prompted, paste your Giphy API key. The platform will securely store it as an environment variable in your project.

<Warning>
Never commit API keys directly in your code. Emergent automatically handles secure storage of credentials.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Describe your GIF search requirements">
Tell the AI how you want to use Giphy in your app. For example:

- "Add a GIF search button in the message composer"
- "Show trending GIFs on the home page"
- "Let users search and preview GIFs before sending"

The AI will implement the appropriate UI and API calls.
</Step>

<Step title="Test the integration">
Once the AI has implemented the Giphy features, test the GIF search and display functionality in your app preview. Try searching for different terms and verify that GIFs load correctly.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common use cases

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Chat applications" icon="message-circle">
Add GIF search to message composers, allowing users to search and send animated reactions.
</Card>

<Card title="Social feeds" icon="users">
Display trending or curated GIFs in social media feeds and content discovery interfaces.
</Card>

<Card title="Marketing content" icon="megaphone">
Embed GIFs in marketing emails, landing pages, or promotional content.
</Card>

<Card title="User profiles" icon="user">
Let users select animated avatars or profile decorations from Giphy's library.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## API endpoints and features

The Giphy API provides several endpoints you can reference when describing features to the AI:

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `/search` | Search GIFs by keyword or phrase |
| `/trending` | Fetch currently trending GIFs |
| `/translate` | Convert text into a relevant GIF |
| `/random` | Get a random GIF, optionally filtered by tag |
| `/gifs` | Fetch GIF details by ID |

<Tip>
You don't need to know the API details — just describe what you want in natural language, and the AI will implement the correct endpoints.
</Tip>

## Rate limits and best practices

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="What are the rate limits?">
Giphy's free tier includes rate limits on API requests. The exact limits depend on your account type and are subject to change. Check the [Giphy Developers Portal](https://developers.giphy.com/) for current limits.

For production apps with high traffic, consider upgrading to a paid Giphy plan.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How should I handle attribution?">
Giphy's terms of service require attribution when displaying GIFs. The AI will typically include the Giphy logo or "Powered by Giphy" text automatically. Make sure this attribution remains visible in your final design.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I cache GIF results?">
Giphy's terms allow temporary caching to improve performance, but you must not store GIFs permanently or create a competing GIF library. The AI-generated code will handle caching appropriately.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What content rating should I use?">
Giphy GIFs are rated `g` (general audiences), `pg`, `pg-13`, and `r`. By default, searches exclude `r`-rated content. You can specify rating filters when describing your requirements to the AI.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="GIFs aren't loading">
- Verify your API key is correct in the project environment variables
- Check your network connection and firewall settings
- Ensure you haven't exceeded your rate limit (check the Giphy Dashboard for usage stats)
- Try a different search term — some queries may return no results
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Attribution logo is missing">
Tell the AI to add Giphy attribution:

```
Make sure the Giphy logo appears when GIFs are displayed
```

The AI will add the required attribution UI element.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Search results are inappropriate">
Specify content rating filters when describing your feature:

```
Add GIF search with G and PG ratings only, exclude mature content
```

The AI will configure the rating parameter in API calls.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next steps

Once your Giphy integration is working:

- Customize the GIF picker UI to match your app's design
- Add favorites or recent GIF functionality for returning users
- Implement GIF preview before sending in chat applications
- Explore Giphy Stickers API for static or animated sticker content

<Info>
Need help with your Giphy integration? Describe any issues or customizations you need in the Emergent chat, and the AI agents will assist you.
</Info>

understanding-models-e1-e2-e3-maxx.title: Understanding models (E1/E2/E3 & Maxx)
understanding-models-e1-e2-e3-maxx.content:
## What E1, E2, E3 are

Emergent uses a **tiered model system** to give you control over agent intelligence and credit consumption. Each tier—**E1**, **E2**, **E3**—represents a different underlying language model with distinct capabilities, speed, and cost.

- **E1** — The fastest, most efficient tier. Best for small edits, bug fixes, or when you want to iterate quickly on straightforward changes. Consumes the fewest credits.
- **E2** — A balanced middle tier. Suitable for most day-to-day building: adding features, refactoring components, implementing standard integrations. Good quality-to-cost ratio.
- **E3** — The most capable tier. Use this when you need deep reasoning, complex architectural decisions, or are working through ambiguous requirements. Consumes the most credits per job.

<Tip title="Start with E2">
For most prompts, **E2** strikes the right balance. Drop to **E1** for trivial changes; escalate to **E3** only when the agent struggles or you're tackling a genuinely hard problem.
</Tip>

### When to use which tier

| Tier | Best for | Credit impact |
|------|----------|---------------|
| **E1** | Quick fixes, typos, small CSS tweaks, simple config changes | Lowest |
| **E2** | New components, API integrations, moderate refactors | Medium |
| **E3** | Complex logic, debugging subtle issues, architectural planning | Highest |

You select the tier **before submitting your prompt** in the chat interface. The platform displays the current tier above the prompt input; click it to switch. Once a job starts, it runs on the chosen tier for its entire workflow.

<Note>
The agent's [workflow](/how-the-agent-runs-workflow-stop-reasons) (plan → code → test → review) is the same across all tiers—only the underlying model's reasoning depth changes.
</Note>

---

## Maxx mode & its credit impact

**Maxx mode** is an optional power-user setting that removes the agent's internal token budget limits, allowing it to produce **longer plans, more comprehensive code changes, and deeper test coverage** in a single job.

When Maxx is **off** (the default), the agent operates within normal context windows and stops after a reasonable number of iterations. This keeps jobs predictable and credit-efficient.

When Maxx is **on**, the agent can:
- Generate multi-file, sweeping refactors in one pass
- Write exhaustive test suites
- Tackle extremely large prompts or complex multi-step features

<Warning title="Maxx consumes significantly more credits">
A single Maxx-enabled job can use **3–10× the credits** of a normal job on the same tier, because the agent makes more LLM calls, processes larger contexts, and iterates more deeply. Use Maxx **sparingly**—only when you genuinely need the extra horsepower.
</Warning>

### When to enable Maxx

<Steps>
<Step title="Identify the need">
Ask yourself: *Is this prompt too broad or complex for a normal job?* If the agent has been stopping prematurely or you're refactoring an entire module, Maxx may help.
</Step>

<Step title="Enable before submitting">
Toggle Maxx mode in the prompt interface (next to the model tier selector). It applies only to the **next job** you start.
</Step>

<Step title="Monitor credit usage">
Check your [credit balance](/how-credits-work) after the job completes. If Maxx burned through more than expected, consider breaking future large prompts into smaller, sequential jobs.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
Maxx mode works with **any tier** (E1, E2, or E3). Combining **E3 + Maxx** gives you maximum capability but also maximum cost—reserve this for truly challenging scenarios.
</Info>

---

## Choosing the right combination

A quick decision tree:

- **Small, obvious change?** → E1, Maxx off.
- **Standard feature or integration?** → E2, Maxx off.
- **Large refactor or ambitious new subsystem?** → E2 or E3, Maxx on (but watch credits).
- **Agent keeps stopping short of a solution?** → Try the next tier up, or enable Maxx, then re-prompt.

You can always adjust mid-conversation: if a job on E2 didn't produce the depth you needed, follow up with the same prompt on E3 or with Maxx enabled. The platform retains your chat context, so the agent understands what you've already tried.

<Tip title="Iterate cheaply first">
Start with a lower tier and Maxx off. If the result isn't quite right, your follow-up prompt costs less than if you'd gone straight to E3 + Maxx and overshot.
</Tip>

mcps-connectors.title: MCPs & connectors
mcps-connectors.content:
## What is MCP?

The **Model Context Protocol** (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI agents discover and use external tools, data sources, and services. Instead of hard-coding integrations, agents speak MCP to dynamically fetch schemas, call functions, and retrieve context from any MCP-compatible server.

In Emergent, the build agent uses MCP connectors to pull real-time data (APIs, databases, file systems) and invoke external actions during code generation, testing, and deployment.

<Note>
MCP servers expose **tools** (callable functions), **resources** (readable data), and **prompts** (reusable templates). Emergent's agent discovers these capabilities automatically when you register a server.
</Note>

## Using an MCP connector

An **MCP connector** bridges Emergent's build agent to an external service. When you register a connector, the agent can:

- **Read resources** — fetch schemas, documentation, or live data (e.g., rows from a Notion database, files from Google Drive).
- **Call tools** — trigger actions like sending a Slack message, creating a Jira ticket, or querying a REST API.
- **Inject context** — use prompts defined by the server to guide code generation.

Common use cases:

| Connector type | Example | What it enables |
|----------------|---------|-----------------|
| Database | PostgreSQL MCP | Read schemas, run queries, validate migrations |
| SaaS API | Stripe MCP | Fetch product catalog, create checkout sessions |
| File system | Local filesystem MCP | Access project templates, reference documents |
| Communication | Slack MCP | Send notifications, read channel history |

<Tip>
Third-party MCP servers are often published as npm packages or Docker images. Check [modelcontextprotocol.io](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) or GitHub for community-maintained servers.
</Tip>

## Emergent as an MCP server

Emergent itself exposes an **MCP interface** on port `8013` (local) or via a public endpoint when deployed. This lets you use Emergent as a tool from other AI clients—Claude Desktop, Cursor, or custom agents.

**Available tools** (example):

- `emergent.create_app` — start a new app from a prompt.
- `emergent.deploy` — trigger deployment of a workspace.
- `emergent.get_logs` — retrieve build or runtime logs.

To connect from Claude Desktop or another MCP client, configure the server URL and any required API key in the client's MCP settings. Emergent will return its tool schemas, and the client can invoke them like any other MCP tool.

<Info>
Self-hosting users can customize the exposed tools by editing the MCP server configuration in `config/mcp.json` (see installation docs for details).
</Info>

## Registering a custom MCP server

To give the build agent access to a custom or third-party MCP server:

<Steps>
<Step title="Prepare the server endpoint">
Your MCP server must listen on a reachable address (localhost for local dev, or a public HTTPS URL for cloud). Ensure it implements the MCP specification (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, etc.).
</Step>

<Step title="Add the server to your workspace config">
In the Emergent workspace, open **Settings → Integrations → MCP Servers** and click **Add Server**. Provide:

- **Name** — a unique identifier (e.g., `my-postgres-db`).
- **Endpoint** — the base URL or `stdio` command (e.g., `http://localhost:8012` or `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`).
- **Auth** (if required) — API key, bearer token, or environment variable reference.
- **Visibility** — `private` (workspace-only) or `public` (shared across your account).
</Step>

<Step title="Save and test connection">
Click **Save**. Emergent will call the server's `initialize` method and cache the list of tools and resources. Check the **Connection Status** indicator—green means the agent can reach the server.
</Step>

<Step title="Use discovered tools in chat">
Registered tools appear in the agent's tool palette. When you describe a task that matches a tool's schema, the agent will propose calling it. You can also reference the server explicitly:

> "Use the `my-postgres-db` connector to read the users table schema and generate a GraphQL API."

</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
**Port 8012** is the default for stdio-launched MCP servers in Emergent's local environment. If your server binds to a different port, specify the full URL in the endpoint field.
</Warning>

### Public vs. private servers

- **Private** — only the current workspace can use this server. Config stored in workspace metadata.
- **Public** — any workspace in your account can discover and call the server. Config stored in your global MCP registry.

Use private for project-specific databases or credentials; use public for shared services (company Slack, internal APIs).

### Tool discovery and caching

Emergent caches tool schemas for **24 hours** after the first successful connection. If you update the server's tools (add a new function, change parameters), click **Refresh Schema** in the MCP Servers list to force a re-discovery. The agent will re-fetch the tool list and update its knowledge.

<Tip>
For rapidly evolving servers, enable **Auto-refresh on job start** in the server settings. The agent will re-discover tools at the beginning of each build job, ensuring it always sees the latest API.
</Tip>

---

**Next steps**

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Explore connectors" icon="plug" href="/integrations/connectors">
Browse pre-built connectors for popular services (databases, SaaS, cloud storage).
</Card>
<Card title="Custom agents" icon="robot" href="/custom-agents">
Learn how to extend the build agent with custom prompts and tool chains.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

database-data-on-mobile.title: Database & data on mobile
database-data-on-mobile.content:
## Shared fundamentals

Mobile apps built on Emergent use the same MongoDB backend as web apps. The database URL model, storage limits, and core behavior are identical across platforms.

For a complete explanation of how database URLs work, connection strings, storage quotas, and data persistence, see the [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) page.

Key points for mobile:

- Each Emergent app gets a dedicated MongoDB cluster with a unique connection string
- The database is hosted remotely and accessed over HTTPS — your mobile app talks to the same cloud database as the web version
- All CRUD operations, indexes, and collections work identically on iOS, Android, and web

<Note>
Mobile apps do **not** bundle a local database. All data lives in the cloud MongoDB instance provisioned for your app.
</Note>

## Republish as an update

When you modify your mobile app's backend, database schema, or business logic and want to push that change to users, you must **republish** the app to the Apple App Store and Google Play Store as a new version.

Unlike web apps (which update instantly on the next page load), mobile apps are distributed as signed binaries with fixed bundle IDs. Any change to the backend — even a database migration or API endpoint tweak — requires:

<Steps>
<Step title="Rebuild the mobile app">
Trigger a new build in Emergent. The agent will increment the version number and compile fresh iOS/Android binaries.
</Step>

<Step title="Submit to the stores">
Upload the new build to App Store Connect (iOS) and Google Play Console (Android). Both stores will review the update.
</Step>

<Step title="Users receive the update">
Once approved, existing users see an "Update available" prompt in their store app. The new version downloads and replaces the old binary.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning title="No instant rollout">
There is no "hot reload" or instant deployment for mobile. Plan for store review times (hours to days) and user adoption lag (days to weeks).
</Warning>

**Database implications:**  
The database itself does **not** redeploy. The same MongoDB cluster persists across versions. When you republish:

- Existing user data remains intact
- Schema changes (new collections, fields, indexes) take effect immediately on the backend
- Old app versions still in the wild will continue querying the *updated* database — ensure backward compatibility or force a minimum version

## Fork into a new app

Instead of updating your published app, you can **fork** it into a separate app with its own identity and database.

A fork creates:

- A new Emergent project in your workspace
- A new bundle ID / package name (e.g., `com.yourcompany.myapp-v2`)
- A new, empty MongoDB cluster (no data copied from the original)
- Independent build artifacts for iOS and Android

**When to fork:**

- You want to launch a "Pro" or region-specific variant without affecting the original
- You're testing a major refactor and need a parallel app
- You want a clean slate for data (no migration path needed)

**How to fork:**

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the app's overflow menu">
In the workspace, find the mobile app card and click the **⋮** menu.
</Step>

<Step title="Select Fork">
Choose **Fork into new app**. Emergent will clone the codebase and create a new project.
</Step>

<Step title="Change the bundle ID">
Before building, update the bundle/package ID in the app settings to avoid conflicts with the original.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info" title="Forked apps are independent">
The fork does **not** share a database, deployment pipeline, or store listing with the original. You'll submit it as a brand-new app to Apple and Google.
</Callout>

## What carries over

How your database and user data are affected depends on whether you **update** (republish) or **fork**.

| Action | Database | User data | Bundle ID | Store listing |
|--------|----------|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **Republish (update)** | Same cluster, schema changes apply | Persists; all users keep their data | Unchanged | Same app, new version number |
| **Fork** | New, empty cluster | None; starts blank | New ID required | New app submission |

**Republish:**
- Database connection string stays the same
- Existing collections and documents remain
- Schema migrations (new fields, indexes) affect all app versions immediately
- Users who haven't updated yet will query the *new* schema — plan for backward compatibility

**Fork:**
- You get a fresh MongoDB cluster with no data
- No risk of breaking the original app's data
- You must manually migrate data if you want to copy records from the original (export/import or script)

<Tip>
If you need to carry data forward into a fork, export collections from the original app's MongoDB cluster and import them into the new one. See the [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) page for connection details.
</Tip>

template-fullsatck-vs-base-python-advanc.title: Template- fullsatck vs base python (advanced)
template-fullsatck-vs-base-python-advanc.content:
## Overview

When starting a new project in Emergent, you'll choose between two starter templates: **Fullstack** and **Base Python (Advanced)**. Both are production-ready foundations, but they serve different use cases and developer workflows.

This page compares the two templates to help you pick the right starting point for your project.

<Tip title="Not sure which to choose?">
Most users building web or mobile apps should start with **Fullstack**. Choose **Base Python** if you're building a backend-only service, API, or data pipeline.
</Tip>

## Quick Comparison

| Aspect | Fullstack | Base Python (Advanced) |
|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| **Best for** | Web apps, mobile apps, full-featured products | APIs, microservices, data pipelines, custom backends |
| **Frontend** | React + Vite included, ready to render UI | None — backend only |
| **Backend** | FastAPI server pre-configured | FastAPI server pre-configured |
| **Routing** | Client-side routing (React Router) + API routes | API routes only |
| **Database** | MongoDB pre-integrated | MongoDB available (manual setup) |
| **Authentication** | Pre-built auth flows (optional) | Manual implementation required |
| **Deployment** | Single deployment (frontend + backend) | Backend service only |
| **Learning curve** | Beginner-friendly | Requires backend/Python experience |
| **Customization** | Moderate — structured for common patterns | High — minimal opinions, flexible architecture |

## When to Choose Fullstack

Choose the **Fullstack** template if you're building:

- A web application with interactive UI
- A mobile app (Emergent can convert React web apps to mobile — see [Web <-> Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical))
- A product where users log in, view dashboards, or interact with forms
- A prototype you want to demo quickly with a working interface

<Info>
The Fullstack template includes a complete React frontend. You describe your UI in chat, and agents scaffold components, pages, and routing for you.
</Info>

### What's Included

- **React 18** with Vite for fast development and hot module replacement
- **FastAPI** backend with CORS configured for local and production environments
- **MongoDB integration** — models, collections, and queries set up out of the box (see [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb))
- **Environment variable management** — `.env` files for secrets like API keys (see [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key))
- **Client-side routing** — declarative routes in React Router
- **Tailwind CSS** pre-configured for styling

## When to Choose Base Python (Advanced)

Choose the **Base Python** template if you're building:

- A REST or GraphQL API consumed by external clients
- A background worker, scheduled job, or data processing pipeline
- A microservice in a larger architecture
- A custom backend where you want full control over structure and dependencies

<Warning>
This template has no frontend. If you later need a UI, you'll need to add it manually or start a separate Fullstack project.
</Warning>

### What's Included

- **FastAPI** server with minimal boilerplate
- **Python 3.11+** runtime
- **Flexible project structure** — you define the module layout
- **MongoDB available** — you add the client and models as needed
- **No frontend dependencies** — smaller build, faster cold starts

## Making the Switch Later

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Can I add a frontend to Base Python later?">
    Yes, but it requires manual setup. You'll need to install React (or another framework), configure build tooling, and wire up routing. For most users, it's faster to start a new Fullstack project and copy over your backend code.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can I remove the frontend from Fullstack?">
    Yes. Delete the `frontend/` directory, remove frontend dependencies from your build config, and redeploy. The FastAPI backend will continue to run independently.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can I use a different frontend framework?">
    Fullstack ships with React, but you can replace it with Vue, Svelte, or any framework that compiles to static assets. You'll need to update the build step and serve the new bundle from FastAPI.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next Steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Database (MongoDB)" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
    Learn how to define models, query collections, and manage data
  </Card>
  <Card title="Custom Domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
    Point your own domain to your deployed Emergent app
  </Card>
  <Card title="Glossary" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
    Key terms and concepts in the Emergent platform
  </Card>
  <Card title="Web ↔ Mobile Conversion" icon="mobile" href="/web-mobile-conversion-canonical">
    Turn your Fullstack web app into a mobile app
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

getting-help-support-community.title: Getting help, support & community
getting-help-support-community.content:
## Where to get help

We're here to help you succeed with Emergent. Whether you have a question, need troubleshooting support, or want to connect with other builders, you have two main channels.

### Discord community

Join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/emergent) to:

- Ask questions and get quick answers from the community
- Share what you're building and get feedback
- Learn tips and workflows from experienced users
- Stay up to date with platform announcements

The Discord is the fastest way to connect with both the Emergent team and other builders.

### Support email

For issues that require account-level assistance or private discussion, email us at **support@emergent.ai**.

We typically respond within one business day. Support email is best for:

- Billing and subscription questions
- Account access issues
- Detailed bug reports
- Feature requests that include sensitive information

---

## Filing a good bug report

When something goes wrong, a detailed bug report helps us fix the issue quickly. The most important piece of information is your **Job ID**.

### Include your Job ID

Every build or operation in Emergent has a unique Job ID visible in the workspace. To find it:

<Steps>
<Step title="Locate the Job ID">
Look in the bottom-left corner of the workspace sidebar or in the job history panel. It's a string like `job_abc123xyz`.
</Step>

<Step title="Copy the full ID">
Click to copy or select and copy the entire Job ID string.
</Step>

<Step title="Include it in your report">
Paste the Job ID in your Discord message or support email. This lets us look up the exact context of your build.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
If you have multiple jobs related to the issue, include all relevant Job IDs.
</Tip>

### Add screenshots of errors

A screenshot of the error message or unexpected behavior provides critical context. Capture:

- The full error message text
- Any red error banners or console output
- The state of the workspace when the issue occurred

### Describe what you expected vs. what happened

A quick sentence or two helps us understand the gap:

> "I asked the agent to add a login page, expected it to create `/login`, but it created `/signin` instead and broke the routing."

This context, combined with your Job ID and screenshot, gives us everything we need to investigate.

---

<Info title="Learning resources">
If you're new to Emergent, check out [Your first build](/your-first-build-walkthrough) for a guided walkthrough, or visit [How apps work here](/how-apps-work-here-mental-model) to understand the platform's mental model.
</Info>
