push-notifications.title: Push notifications
push-notifications.content:
## Push notifications in Emergent

Push notifications appear in two contexts on Emergent: **system notifications** that keep you informed about your workspace, and **in-app notifications** you can enable for the mobile applications you build.

---

## Emergent platform notifications

Emergent sends push notifications to your account when important events occur:

- **Deployment complete** — your app shipped to production, with a deep link directly to the live URL.
- **Credit balance low** — reminder when your [credit balance](/credit-expiry-recharging) falls below a threshold.
- **Agent milestones** — when an AI agent finishes a complex build, encounters a blocker, or requests clarification.

<Note>
Platform push notifications arrive via the Emergent mobile app (iOS/Android) or browser notifications if you've granted permission. Deep links open the relevant workspace or chat thread.
</Note>

All platform notifications respect your account notification preferences. You can mute categories or adjust delivery hours in **Settings → Notifications**.

---

## Enabling push for apps you build

When you describe a mobile app in chat, agents can integrate push notifications using **SuprSend**, a unified notification service that handles iOS (APNs) and Android (FCM) delivery.

<Steps>

<Step title="Request push in your app specification">
In chat, describe the notification use case — for example:

> "Send a push when a new message arrives"  
> "Notify users 24 hours before their event"

The agent will scaffold SuprSend integration into your Next.js API and React Native mobile client.
</Step>

<Step title="Provide Firebase credentials (Android)">
To send Android push, the agent needs a Firebase Cloud Messaging service account:

1. Open your [Firebase Console](https://console.firebase.google.com/).
2. Select your project (or create one).
3. Navigate to **Project settings → Service accounts**.
4. Click **Generate new private key** and download the JSON file.
5. Upload `service-account.json` when the agent requests it, or paste the JSON directly into chat.

<Warning>
The service-account key grants full Firebase access. Never commit it to a public repository. Emergent encrypts uploaded credentials at rest.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Provide APNs credentials (iOS)">
For iOS push, you need an Apple Push Notification service (APNs) key:

1. Sign in to [Apple Developer](https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/authkeys/list).
2. Create a new key with the **Apple Push Notifications service (APNs)** capability enabled.
3. Download the `.p8` file (you can only download it once).
4. Note the **Key ID** and your **Team ID** (found in your Apple Developer account membership details).
5. Provide the `.p8` file, Key ID, and Team ID to the agent via chat or file upload.

<Info>
A single APNs key can serve all your apps under the same Team ID. You do not need a separate key per app.
</Info>
</Step>

<Step title="Test and deploy">
Once credentials are uploaded, the agent configures SuprSend in your backend and wires the mobile client to request push permissions on first launch.

Deploy your app normally via chat. The agent will confirm push is live and may send a test notification to verify delivery.
</Step>

</Steps>

---

## How SuprSend works in your app

Behind the scenes, Emergent agents:

- Add the **SuprSend SDK** to your Next.js API and React Native project.
- Store device tokens securely in your [MongoDB database](/database-mongodb).
- Trigger notifications via SuprSend's REST API from your backend workflows (cron jobs, webhooks, user actions).
- Handle token refresh, badge counts, and deep-link routing automatically.

You can extend notification logic by describing new triggers in chat — for example, "Send a reminder push every morning at 9 AM."

---

## Credentials security

<CardGroup cols={2}>

<Card title="Encryption at rest" icon="lock">
Firebase and APNs keys are encrypted in Emergent's secret store and never logged or exposed in build artifacts.
</Card>

<Card title="Rotation & revocation" icon="rotate-cw">
You can upload new credentials anytime by describing the change in chat. Old keys are purged immediately.
</Card>

</CardGroup>

If a credential is compromised, regenerate it in Firebase or Apple Developer and re-upload. The agent will redeploy your app with the updated key within minutes.

---

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Push works on Android but not iOS">
Verify that:

- The `.p8` key, Key ID, and Team ID match exactly.
- Your app's bundle identifier in Xcode matches the one registered in Apple Developer.
- You've tested on a physical device (push does not work in the iOS Simulator).
- The device has granted notification permissions (check Settings → Notifications).

If all credentials are correct but iOS push still fails, ask the agent to check the APNs certificate configuration.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Firebase service account upload fails">
Ensure the JSON file is valid and contains the `project_id`, `private_key`, and `client_email` fields. Re-download from Firebase Console if the file appears truncated.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Notifications deliver late or not at all">
SuprSend batches and retries deliveries, so slight delays are normal. If notifications never arrive:

- Confirm the device token was successfully registered (check your MongoDB `devices` collection).
- Verify the user granted notification permissions at the OS level.
- Check SuprSend logs via the agent — ask "Show recent push delivery logs."
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I use a different push provider?">
Yes. Describe your preferred service in chat (for example, OneSignal, Pusher Beams, or a custom APNs/FCM integration). The agent can swap providers, though SuprSend is the default because it unifies iOS and Android with minimal setup.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Deep links in notifications

Both Emergent platform notifications and your app's push messages support **deep links** — tapping a notification opens a specific screen or resource:

- **Platform notifications** deep-link into the Emergent workspace (for example, directly to a chat thread or deployment dashboard).
- **Your app's notifications** can deep-link to any screen you define. Describe the link structure in chat:

  > "When a user taps the new-message push, open the chat screen with `conversationId` pre-filled."

The agent will configure URL schemes (iOS) and intent filters (Android) automatically.

<Tip>
Deep links dramatically improve engagement. Users who tap a notification convert at 3–5× the rate of users who open the app cold.
</Tip>

---

## Related topics

<CardGroup cols={2}>

<Card title="Emergent Auth (built-in)" icon="shield-check" href="/emergent-auth-built-in">
How user authentication integrates with device-token registration for push.
</Card>

<Card title="Database (MongoDB)" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
Where device tokens and notification state are stored.
</Card>

<Card title="Custom domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Deep links work seamlessly with your custom domain once configured.
</Card>

<Card title="Credit expiry & recharging" icon="credit-card" href="/credit-expiry-recharging">
Understand when Emergent sends you low-balance push alerts.
</Card>

</CardGroup>
push-notifications.description: Push for the Emergent app itself (deploy/credit/agent alerts with deep links) and enabling push in apps you build via SuprSend (Android service-account.json, iOS .p8).

him-human-in-middle-mode.title: HIM (Human in middle) mode
him-human-in-middle-mode.content:
## What is HIM mode?

**HIM (Human in Middle) mode** is an interactive agent workflow that pauses before every code change and waits for your explicit approval. Instead of the agent autonomously writing and applying edits, it shows you the proposed diff and asks you to confirm or reject each modification.

In default mode, the agent runs autonomously—planning, coding, testing, and iterating until it reaches a natural stopping point or completes the job. HIM mode inserts a human checkpoint at every code-edit step, giving you fine-grained control over what gets written to your codebase.

## How HIM mode differs from default

<Columns cols={2}>
<Card title="Default mode" icon="zap">
Agent runs autonomously. Writes code, runs tests, iterates until the job is done or hits a stop condition. You review the final result.
</Card>

<Card title="HIM mode" icon="hand">
Agent proposes every edit as a diff and waits. You approve or reject each change before it's applied. Agent proceeds only after your input.
</Card>
</Columns>

**Key differences:**

- **Autonomy:** Default = full autonomy; HIM = step-by-step approval.
- **Speed:** Default completes jobs faster; HIM takes longer because of human review steps.
- **Control:** HIM gives you veto power over every edit; default trusts the agent to follow the plan.
- **Credit usage:** HIM can use fewer credits if you catch mistakes early, but may use more if you reject changes and the agent must re-plan.

<Note>
HIM mode does **not** pause for non-code actions like running tests, installing packages, or reading files—only when the agent wants to write or modify code.
</Note>

## When to use HIM mode

HIM mode is most useful when you need high confidence in every code change or want to teach the agent by example.

**Use HIM mode when:**

- **Editing critical or unfamiliar code** – you want to review every line before it touches production logic.
- **Working on a shared codebase** – multiple developers or tight standards mean every change needs human eyes.
- **Teaching the agent your preferences** – rejecting changes with feedback helps the agent learn your style within the session.
- **Debugging a tricky issue** – you want to steer the agent's approach step-by-step rather than letting it iterate freely.
- **Low tolerance for mistakes** – the cost of a bad edit (data loss, broken API) is high, and you'd rather catch it immediately.

**Stick with default mode when:**

- You trust the agent to handle the task end-to-end (common for new features, boilerplate, or well-scoped refactors).
- Speed matters more than micro-level control.
- You're comfortable reviewing the final diff after the job completes.

<Tip>
You can toggle HIM mode on or off mid-job. If the agent starts making unexpected changes in default mode, switch to HIM to regain control. If HIM is slowing you down, switch back to default.
</Tip>

## How to enable HIM mode

HIM mode is toggled per-job in the workspace interface.

<Steps>
<Step title="Start or resume a job">
Open the chat interface and describe your task, or continue an existing job.
</Step>

<Step title="Toggle HIM mode">
Look for the **HIM mode** toggle in the top controls of the workspace (typically near the Run/Pause button). Click it to enable.
</Step>

<Step title="Approve or reject edits">
When the agent proposes a code change, you'll see a diff preview. Click **Approve** to apply it, or **Reject** (optionally with feedback) to skip it. The agent will wait for your decision before proceeding.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
If you leave a job paused in HIM mode without responding, the agent will not proceed. Remember to approve or reject pending changes, or toggle HIM off if you want the agent to continue autonomously.
</Warning>

## Tips for effective HIM workflows

- **Give feedback when rejecting** – a short comment ("use async/await here" or "keep the original error handling") helps the agent adjust its next proposal.
- **Approve quickly for boilerplate** – if the agent is writing repetitive or low-risk code (imports, type definitions), approve in batches to stay in flow.
- **Switch modes mid-job** – start in default mode to let the agent draft a solution, then flip to HIM for final refinements.
- **Pair with Wingman** – use [Wingman](/what-is-wingman) to ask clarifying questions or request alternate approaches before approving a change.

<Info>
HIM mode works alongside all other workspace features—file explorer, terminal, database access, and test runners. Only **code edits** require approval; everything else proceeds normally.
</Info>

custom-agents.title: Custom agents
custom-agents.content:
## Agent architecture

Emergent uses a **hierarchical agent system** to break down complex application-building tasks into manageable units of work. At the top level, a **main agent** orchestrates the overall build process, while **sub-agents** handle specialized tasks like testing, deployment, or integration work.

Each agent is a language model instance equipped with:

- **Context** – the current state of your app (files, database schema, dependencies)
- **Tools** – callable functions to read/write code, run commands, query the database, deploy, etc.
- **Instructions** – system prompts that define the agent's role and constraints
- **Memory** – conversation history and state from prior turns

Agents collaborate by spawning sub-agents when a task requires focused expertise (for example, a sub-agent might handle writing unit tests while the main agent continues with feature development). This division of labor keeps each agent's context window focused and improves both speed and quality.

<Note>
Agent runs are tracked in the workspace sidebar. You can inspect logs, tool calls, and sub-agent activity in real time as your app builds.
</Note>

---

## Main agents

The **main agent** is the primary autonomous worker that interprets your chat messages and drives the build-test-deploy cycle. When you describe a feature, fix, or new app in chat, the main agent:

1. **Plans** the work by breaking your request into implementation steps
2. **Executes** those steps using its tools (editing files, running commands, querying docs)
3. **Validates** the result (spawning test sub-agents, checking build output)
4. **Reports back** in chat with a summary, diff preview, or follow-up questions

The main agent has access to the full workspace: your app's source tree, environment variables, database, and deployment config. It decides when to delegate work to sub-agents and when to proceed autonomously.

**Stop reasons** determine when a main agent pauses and returns control to you. Common stop reasons include:

- Successful completion of your request
- A question or clarification needed
- An error that requires human input (e.g., missing API key)
- Credit budget exhausted

For a detailed walk-through of the agent workflow, see [How the agent runs (workflow & stop reasons)](/how-the-agent-runs-workflow-stop-reasons).

---

## Sub-agents

**Sub-agents** are ephemeral, specialized agents spawned by the main agent to handle discrete tasks. They inherit relevant context from the main agent but operate with a narrower scope and tailored instructions.

Common sub-agent roles:

- **Test agents** – write and run unit/integration tests, validate outputs
- **Deployment agents** – handle build steps, environment provisioning, and deploy commands
- **Integration agents** – configure third-party services (Stripe, Twilio, MCP servers)
- **Refactor agents** – clean up code, apply linting, optimize performance

Sub-agents execute in parallel when possible, report results back to the main agent, and terminate once their task completes. They do not persist across turns or interact directly with you in chat.

<Tip>
Sub-agent logs appear nested under the main agent's activity in the workspace sidebar. You can expand them to see tool calls and outputs.
</Tip>

---

## Custom tools

You can extend agent capabilities by providing **custom tools**—JavaScript functions that agents can call during a run. Custom tools are useful for:

- Calling proprietary or internal APIs not covered by built-in integrations
- Performing domain-specific calculations or transformations
- Interfacing with hardware, legacy systems, or non-standard data sources

### Defining a custom tool

Custom tools are defined in a `tools/` directory in your workspace. Each tool is a TypeScript or JavaScript module that exports:

- A `name` (string) – the tool's identifier agents will invoke
- A `description` (string) – what the tool does, used by the agent to decide when to call it
- A `parameters` schema (JSON Schema object) – required/optional arguments
- An `execute` function – the implementation

**Example:** a custom tool that validates a US phone number:

```typescript
// tools/validate-phone.ts
export const name = "validate_us_phone";
export const description = "Validates a US phone number and returns formatted version";

export const parameters = {
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    phoneNumber: { type: "string", description: "Raw phone number string" }
  },
  required: ["phoneNumber"]
};

export async function execute({ phoneNumber }: { phoneNumber: string }) {
  const cleaned = phoneNumber.replace(/\D/g, "");
  if (cleaned.length !== 10) {
    return { valid: false, error: "Must be 10 digits" };
  }
  const formatted = `(${cleaned.slice(0,3)}) ${cleaned.slice(3,6)}-${cleaned.slice(6)}`;
  return { valid: true, formatted };
}
```

### Registering tools with agents

Once a tool module is present in `tools/`, it is **automatically discovered** on the next agent run. The main agent and relevant sub-agents will see the tool in their available function list and can call it as needed.

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the tool module">
Add a `.ts` or `.js` file under `tools/` exporting `name`, `description`, `parameters`, and `execute`.
</Step>

<Step title="Test locally (optional)">
Run the tool function directly in a Node script or REPL to verify it works before an agent invokes it.
</Step>

<Step title="Trigger an agent run">
Describe a task in chat that would benefit from the tool. The agent will discover and call it automatically.
</Step>

<Step title="Inspect tool calls">
Check the agent activity log to see arguments passed and results returned.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning title="Tool execution security">
Custom tools run in the same Node environment as your app's build process. Avoid executing untrusted input or performing destructive operations without validation.
</Warning>

### Tool best practices

- **Keep tools focused** – one tool per discrete operation. Agents compose multiple tool calls for complex workflows.
- **Provide clear descriptions** – agents rely on natural-language descriptions to decide when to use a tool.
- **Return structured data** – JSON objects are easier for agents to parse than free-form strings.
- **Handle errors gracefully** – return `{ error: "message" }` rather than throwing, so agents can retry or adjust strategy.

For integrating external platforms via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), see [Custom & MCP integrations](/custom-mcp-integrations).

elevenlabs.title: ElevenLabs
elevenlabs.content:
## Overview

ElevenLabs provides AI-powered text-to-speech and voice synthesis services. Integrating ElevenLabs into your Emergent project lets you generate natural-sounding speech from text, create custom voices, and build voice-enabled experiences.

This guide walks you through setting up the ElevenLabs integration so your agents can call its API directly from your application.

---

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- An active ElevenLabs account ([sign up here](https://elevenlabs.io))
- An API key from your ElevenLabs dashboard
- An Emergent project where you want to use voice synthesis

<Note>
ElevenLabs offers a free tier with limited character quota. Check your plan limits in the ElevenLabs dashboard to ensure they meet your project's needs.
</Note>

---

## Setup steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Obtain your ElevenLabs API key">

1. Log in to your [ElevenLabs account](https://elevenlabs.io)
2. Navigate to your **Profile Settings** (click your avatar in the top-right corner)
3. Select the **API Keys** tab
4. Click **Create API Key** or copy an existing key
5. Store the key securely — you'll add it to Emergent in the next step

<Warning>
Treat your API key like a password. Do not commit it to version control or share it publicly.
</Warning>

</Step>

<Step title="Add the API key to your Emergent project">

In your Emergent workspace:

1. Open the **chat** and describe your integration need:
   ```
   Add ElevenLabs integration. Store the API key as ELEVENLABS_API_KEY.
   ```
2. When prompted, paste your ElevenLabs API key
3. The agent will securely store it as an environment variable in your project

Alternatively, you can manually add the key:

1. Navigate to your project's **Settings** or environment configuration
2. Add a new environment variable:
   - **Key**: `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`
   - **Value**: your API key from ElevenLabs
3. Save the configuration

</Step>

<Step title="Describe your voice synthesis feature">

Tell the Emergent agents what you want to build. Examples:

<CodeGroup>

```text Basic text-to-speech
Add a "Speak" button next to each article.
When clicked, use ElevenLabs to convert the article text to speech and play it.
```

```text Custom voice selection
Create a voice settings page where users can choose from available ElevenLabs voices.
Store their preference and use that voice for all text-to-speech playback.
```

```text Real-time narration
When a user submits a story, generate an audio narration using ElevenLabs
and display an audio player on the story detail page.
```

</CodeGroup>

The agents will:
- Install the ElevenLabs SDK (if needed)
- Implement API calls using your stored key
- Build the UI components for playback or voice selection
- Handle error states (quota exceeded, network issues)

</Step>

<Step title="Test the integration">

Once the agents deploy your feature:

1. Navigate to the part of your app that uses ElevenLabs
2. Trigger the text-to-speech action (click a button, submit a form, etc.)
3. Verify that audio is generated and plays correctly
4. Check your ElevenLabs dashboard to confirm API usage is being tracked

<Tip>
Start with short text samples during testing to conserve your character quota.
</Tip>

If you encounter errors, describe the issue in chat:
```
The ElevenLabs audio isn't playing. I see an error: [paste error message].
```

The agents will debug and fix the integration.

</Step>

</Steps>

---

## Common use cases

<CardGroup cols={2}>

<Card title="Article narration" icon="book-open">
Generate audio versions of blog posts or articles for accessibility and multi-modal consumption.
</Card>

<Card title="Voice assistants" icon="microphone">
Build conversational interfaces that respond with natural-sounding speech.
</Card>

<Card title="Audiobook generation" icon="headphones">
Convert written content into audiobook-style narration with custom voices.
</Card>

<Card title="Notification voiceovers" icon="bell">
Add spoken alerts or announcements to your app for visually impaired users.
</Card>

</CardGroup>

---

## Configuration options

You can customize how ElevenLabs is used in your project by describing preferences to the agents:

| Option | Description | Example instruction |
|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Voice selection** | Choose from ElevenLabs' library of pre-made voices | "Use the 'Rachel' voice for all narration" |
| **Voice settings** | Adjust stability, clarity, and style parameters | "Set voice stability to 0.75 and clarity to 0.8" |
| **Model selection** | Pick a specific ElevenLabs model (multilingual, turbo, etc.) | "Use the multilingual v2 model for better accent handling" |
| **Streaming** | Enable real-time audio streaming for low-latency playback | "Stream audio as it's generated instead of waiting for the full file" |
| **Caching** | Store generated audio to reduce API calls | "Cache generated speech for 24 hours per unique text input" |

<Info>
The agents will suggest sensible defaults based on your use case. You can always refine settings by describing adjustments in chat.
</Info>

---

## Monitoring usage

ElevenLabs tracks character usage against your plan quota. To monitor:

1. Visit your [ElevenLabs dashboard](https://elevenlabs.io/app/usage)
2. Review **Character Usage** for the current billing period
3. Set up usage alerts if your plan supports them

<Warning>
If you exceed your quota, API requests will fail until you upgrade your plan or your quota resets. Build error handling into your app to gracefully inform users when synthesis is unavailable.
</Warning>

You can instruct the agents to implement quota-aware features:
```
Show a warning in the admin panel when ElevenLabs usage reaches 80% of the monthly quota.
```

---

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Audio doesn't play after generation">

**Possible causes:**
- The audio file URL is expired or inaccessible
- Browser autoplay policies are blocking playback
- CORS issues if hosting audio on a different domain

**Solutions:**
- Describe the issue in chat: "Audio generated by ElevenLabs won't play in the browser"
- Agents will add user-initiated playback controls or adjust CORS headers
- For mobile apps, ensure audio permissions are requested

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="API key authentication fails">

**Check:**
- The environment variable name is exactly `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`
- The key was copied correctly (no extra spaces)
- Your ElevenLabs account is active and the key hasn't been revoked

**Fix:**
Re-add the key by telling the agents:
```
Update the ElevenLabs API key to [paste new key]
```

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Quota exceeded errors">

**Error message:** `"quota_exceeded"` or similar in API responses.

**Immediate fix:**
- Upgrade your ElevenLabs plan, or
- Wait for your quota to reset (check your billing cycle in the ElevenLabs dashboard)

**Long-term solution:**
Ask the agents to implement caching:
```
Cache ElevenLabs audio for identical text inputs to reduce API calls.
```

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Generated voice sounds unnatural">

**Tuning options:**
- Try a different voice from the ElevenLabs library
- Adjust stability and clarity settings (lower stability = more expressive, higher = more consistent)
- Use the higher-quality model if your plan supports it

**Instruction example:**
```
Switch to the 'Josh' voice and increase stability to 0.9 for clearer speech.
```

</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Best practices

<Callout type="tip" title="Optimize for cost and performance">

- **Cache aggressively:** Store generated audio for repeated text to avoid redundant API calls
- **Truncate long inputs:** ElevenLabs charges per character; summarize or chunk very long documents
- **Use streaming:** For real-time applications, stream audio as it's generated to reduce perceived latency

</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="Enhance accessibility">

ElevenLabs integrations are powerful for making content accessible to visually impaired users and those who prefer audio. Combine with transcripts or captions for full accessibility coverage.

</Callout>

<Callout type="note" title="Respect usage limits">

If you're building a public-facing app, implement rate limiting or user quotas to prevent abuse and unexpected billing spikes.

</Callout>

---

## Next steps

Once ElevenLabs is integrated, you can:

- **Combine with other integrations:** Use [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) to pair voice synthesis with AI-generated content
- **Expand to multilingual support:** ElevenLabs supports dozens of languages — describe your localization needs in chat
- **Build custom voices:** If your plan allows, clone voices or create custom profiles for branded experiences

Describe your ideas in the Emergent chat and let the agents bring them to life.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.content:
## What's New in Emergent

This page tracks feature releases, improvements, and important changes to the Emergent platform. We ship frequently—check back often to see what's new.

<Note>
Major updates are announced in-app and via email. Breaking changes that affect existing projects are always called out clearly.
</Note>

## How to Read This Changelog

Each entry includes:

- **Date** — when the change shipped to production
- **Category** — Feature, Improvement, Fix, or Breaking Change
- **Description** — what changed and why it matters

<Callout type="warning" title="Breaking Changes">
Entries marked **Breaking Change** may require action on your part. We provide migration guidance and advance notice whenever possible.
</Callout>

## Recent Updates

### January 2025

**Feature: Web ↔ Mobile Conversion (Canonical)**  
*January 15, 2025*

You can now convert any web app to a mobile app (or vice versa) with a single chat command. Emergent preserves your data model, authentication, and business logic while adapting the UI to the target platform. Learn more in [Web ↔ Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical).

**Improvement: Custom Domain Setup**  
*January 10, 2025*

Custom domain configuration is now streamlined with automatic SSL certificate provisioning and real-time DNS validation. See the [custom domain guide](/custom-domain) for setup instructions.

**Feature: MongoDB Database Support**  
*January 8, 2025*

All new projects now include a managed MongoDB database. Access it from your app code or connect external tools using the connection string in your project settings. Read the [Database (MongoDB) documentation](/database-mongodb).

### December 2024

**Feature: The Universal LLM Key**  
*December 20, 2024*

Bring your own API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or other LLM providers. Emergent routes requests intelligently and lets you switch models mid-conversation. Details in [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key).

**Improvement: Faster Build Times**  
*December 12, 2024*

Agent build pipelines now run 40% faster on average thanks to optimized dependency resolution and parallel task execution.

**Fix: Chat History Persistence**  
*December 5, 2024*

Resolved an issue where chat history could be lost during browser refresh. All conversations now persist reliably across sessions.

## Older Releases

<Accordion title="November 2024">

**Feature: Real-Time Collaboration**  
*November 22, 2024*

Invite teammates to your project. Multiple users can now chat with agents, review code, and deploy changes simultaneously.

**Improvement: Enhanced Error Messages**  
*November 10, 2024*

Build failures and runtime errors now include actionable suggestions and links to relevant documentation.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="October 2024">

**Breaking Change: Authentication Flow Update**  
*October 28, 2024*

Migrated to a new OAuth provider. Existing sessions were preserved, but you may need to re-authenticate once. No code changes required in your projects.

**Feature: Environment Variables**  
*October 15, 2024*

Set secrets and configuration via the project settings panel. Environment variables are encrypted at rest and injected at runtime.

**Fix: Mobile Preview Rendering**  
*October 8, 2024*

Fixed rendering issues in the mobile preview pane for apps with complex CSS grid layouts.

</Accordion>

## Requesting Features

Have an idea? Share feedback directly in the app or reach out to our team. We prioritize features based on user impact and platform vision.

<Tip>
Check the [Glossary of Emergent terms](/glossary-of-emergent-terms) if you encounter unfamiliar terminology in changelog entries.
</Tip>

## Staying Informed

- **In-app notifications** — important updates appear in the platform
- **Email updates** — opt in via your account settings
- **This page** — bookmark and revisit for the full timeline

We're committed to shipping thoughtfully and keeping you informed every step of the way.

the-universal-llm-key.title: The Universal LLM Key
the-universal-llm-key.content:
## What is the Universal LLM Key?

The Universal LLM Key is a single API key that gives your projects access to multiple frontier language models—GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 2.0, and more—without requiring you to sign up for separate API accounts or manage individual keys for each provider.

Instead of juggling OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google credentials, you use your **Emergent Credits** to fund model calls through the Universal Key. The platform handles routing, authentication, and billing automatically.

<Note title="No setup to start">
Every Emergent account includes a Universal Key from day one. You can start building AI features immediately without entering payment details or creating external API accounts.
</Note>

The key works seamlessly inside your deployed apps, and on paid plans you can also use it as a **LiteLLM-compatible proxy** from your local machine or CI/CD pipelines.

---

## Universal Key vs Your Own API Key

You have two options for connecting your projects to language models:

| Aspect | Universal Key | Your Own API Key |
|--------|--------------|------------------|
| **Setup** | Ready immediately; no external accounts | Must create accounts with OpenAI, Anthropic, etc. |
| **Billing** | Charged in Emergent Credits; single invoice | Billed directly by each provider |
| **Model access** | All supported models via one key | Only models from the provider you signed up with |
| **Rate limits** | Shared platform limits (generous) | Provider's limits for your account tier |
| **Cost transparency** | Unified credit usage dashboard | Separate invoices from each provider |
| **Use outside Emergent** | Via proxy on paid plans; NAT/IP restricted | Works anywhere with no restrictions |

### When to use the Universal Key

- You're prototyping and want to try multiple models quickly
- You prefer consolidated billing and credit management
- You're building internal tools and don't want to manage external API keys
- You value simplicity over per-token cost optimization

### When to bring your own key

- You've negotiated volume discounts with a specific provider
- You need model access beyond Emergent's supported set
- You require unrestricted API access from any network location
- Your organization mandates direct contracts with AI providers

<Tip title="Switching is easy">
You can start with the Universal Key and switch to your own API keys later by updating your project's [Secrets](/secrets-env-variables). The agent will adapt automatically.
</Tip>

---

## Recharging & Credit Types

The Universal Key draws from your **Emergent Credit balance** every time your app makes a model call. When your balance runs low, you'll need to recharge to keep services running.

### How recharging works

<Steps>
<Step title="Check your balance">
View your current credit balance and usage history in **Settings → Credits**.
</Step>

<Step title="Add credits">
Purchase credits via credit card, invoice (Enterprise), or redeem a promotional code. Credits are added instantly.
</Step>

<Step title="Credits are consumed">
Each model call deducts credits based on token count and model pricing. You can see per-project breakdowns in the usage dashboard.
</Step>
</Steps>

### Credit types

Emergent offers different credit packages depending on your plan:

- **Starter credits**: Included with free and paid plans; limited monthly allocation
- **Purchased credits**: Pay-as-you-go; no expiry within the billing period
- **Promotional credits**: Time-limited (typically 30–90 days); applied first before purchased credits

For full details on credit expiry, rollover rules, and auto-recharge, see [Credit Expiry & Recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) and [How Credits Work](/how-credits-work).

<Info title="Auto-recharge available">
Paid plans can enable **auto-recharge** to prevent service interruptions. When your balance drops below a threshold (e.g., 1,000 credits), the platform automatically purchases a refill using your saved payment method.
</Info>

---

## Using the Key Outside the Platform

On **paid plans**, you can use your Universal Key as a **LiteLLM-compatible proxy endpoint** to call models from your local development environment, scripts, or CI/CD pipelines.

### Setup example

<CodeGroup>
```python Python (OpenAI SDK)
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="emg_univ_YOUR_KEY_HERE",
    base_url="https://api.emergentagi.com/v1/llm"
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

```bash cURL
curl https://api.emergentagi.com/v1/llm/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer emg_univ_YOUR_KEY_HERE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

### Network restrictions

For security, the Universal Key proxy is **IP-restricted**:

- Requests must originate from known Emergent infrastructure or your verified NAT gateway
- If you're on a dynamic IP, the platform may prompt you to verify your location the first time you call from a new network
- Enterprise plans can whitelist specific CIDR ranges for CI/CD runners

<Warning title="Free tier limitation">
The external proxy endpoint is **not available on the free tier**. Upgrade to a paid plan to use the Universal Key outside of deployed Emergent apps.
</Warning>

### Auto-recharge behavior

When you use the Universal Key externally, **auto-recharge behaves the same** as for deployed apps:

- If your balance drops below the threshold, the platform automatically purchases credits
- You'll receive an email notification after each auto-recharge
- You can disable auto-recharge in **Settings → Billing**, but external calls will fail when credits run out

---

## Regenerating the Key Breaks Live Apps

Your Universal Key is tied directly to your account and embedded in your deployed applications as a [Secret](/secrets-env-variables). If you regenerate it (for example, after a suspected leak), the old key is **immediately invalidated**.

<Callout type="error" title="Deployed apps will fail">
Any live app that references the old Universal Key will start receiving **401 Unauthorized** errors as soon as you regenerate. This includes:

- Apps making LLM calls via the Emergent SDK
- Integrations that use the key in environment variables
- External scripts or services using the old key
</Callout>

### Recovery steps

<Steps>
<Step title="Regenerate the key">
Go to **Settings → API Keys** and click **Regenerate Universal Key**. Copy the new key immediately.
</Step>

<Step title="Update Secrets">
For each affected project, open **Settings → Secrets**, find the `EMERGENT_UNIVERSAL_KEY` entry, and paste the new key.
</Step>

<Step title="Redeploy">
Trigger a redeploy (or push a new commit) so the updated Secret propagates to the live environment. The agent will handle the rest.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Test in preview first">
If your project has a preview environment, update the Secret there first and verify everything works before updating production.
</Tip>

### When to regenerate

Only regenerate your Universal Key if:

- You believe the key has been exposed publicly (e.g., committed to a public repo)
- An ex-team member had access and you need to revoke it immediately
- You're responding to a security incident

For routine key rotation, coordinate the regeneration with a maintenance window to minimize downtime.

a-tour-of-the-workspace.title: A tour of the workspace
a-tour-of-the-workspace.content:
## Overview

The Emergent workspace is divided into five main areas, each handling a distinct part of the build-test-deploy cycle. Understanding this layout will help you move quickly from idea to shipped product.

<Callout type="tip" title="New to Emergent?">
Walk through [Your first build](/your-first-build-walkthrough) to see these panels in action.
</Callout>

---

## Chat panel

The **Chat panel** is where you describe your app, request changes, and ask the agent questions. Every message you send triggers the agent to generate or modify code, install dependencies, and refresh the preview.

**Key behaviors:**

- The agent reads your entire conversation history, so you can refer back to earlier instructions.
- Attach files—screenshots, designs, CSVs, or any other asset—directly in the chat to guide the build. [Learn about file uploads](#uploading-files-and-images).
- The agent will tell you when it's working, when tests pass, and when the preview is ready.

<Note>
The chat is persistent across sessions. Close the workspace and return later; your conversation and build state are saved.
</Note>

---

## Preview panel

The **Preview panel** renders a live, interactive view of your application. Every time the agent completes a code change, the preview auto-refreshes so you can immediately see the result.

**What you can do:**

- Click through flows, fill forms, test buttons—treat it like the real app.
- Open the preview in a new browser tab for a full-screen experience.
- Use browser DevTools to inspect elements, check network requests, or debug layout issues.

<Warning>
The preview runs *in the workspace only*. It is **not** your deployed application. See [Preview vs Deployed](/preview-vs-deployed-separate) for the key differences.
</Warning>

---

## Secrets and environment variables

The **Secrets / Env area** is where you configure API keys, connection strings, and any other environment variables your app needs.

**Important distinctions:**

- Secrets stored here apply to the **preview** environment and any future deployments you create from this workspace.
- They are encrypted at rest and never exposed in the chat or logs.
- The platform injects a special [Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) automatically, so you can call OpenAI, Anthropic, and other LLM providers without adding your own keys during development.

<Tip>
Add secrets *before* asking the agent to integrate third-party services. The agent will reference them by name (e.g., `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`) when generating code.
</Tip>

Learn more in [Secrets & env variables](/secrets-env-variables).

---

## GitHub controls

The **GitHub controls** let you save your workspace code to a repository and pull updates from an existing repo.

**Core actions:**

- **Save to GitHub:** Commit the current state of your workspace to a new or existing repository. This creates a snapshot you can share, review, or roll back to.
- **Pull from GitHub:** Import code from a branch into the workspace. The agent will attempt to merge it with your current build.

<Warning>
Pulling from GitHub can overwrite local changes. Use with caution and save your work first. See [Pull from GitHub (with caution)](/pull-from-github-with-caution).
</Warning>

For step-by-step instructions, see [Save to GitHub](/save-to-github).

---

## Deploy controls

The **Deploy controls** are where you ship your application to a live, publicly accessible URL.

**Available actions:**

- **Deploy:** Create a new deployment from the current workspace state. You'll receive a unique URL that stays live until you delete it.
- **Redeploy:** Push the latest workspace changes to an *existing* deployment, preserving the same URL and deployment ID.
- **Replace:** Swap out the code of a running deployment with a different workspace or branch, keeping the same domain and environment.

<Info>
Deployments are *separate* from the preview. Each deployment gets its own secrets, database, and runtime. [Preview vs Deployed](/preview-vs-deployed-separate) explains the isolation model.
</Info>

Review your options in [Deployment types](/deployment-types) and [Deployment plan levels](/deployment-plan-levels).

---

## Uploading files and images

You can **attach files directly** in the chat panel to guide the agent's work. Common use cases include:

- **Design mockups:** Upload a screenshot or Figma export; the agent will replicate the layout and styling.
- **Data samples:** Attach a CSV or JSON file; the agent will infer the schema and build import/export flows.
- **Icons and logos:** Provide brand assets; the agent will reference them in the UI.
- **Documents:** Share a spec, API response example, or requirements doc; the agent will parse it and apply the details.

**How it works:**

1. Click the attachment icon in the chat input (or drag and drop).
2. Select one or more files (images, PDFs, spreadsheets, text).
3. Send your message; the agent processes the files alongside your instructions.

<Tip>
Combine a screenshot with a short caption like "Build a dashboard that looks like this" for fast, accurate results.
</Tip>

Files uploaded to the chat are stored temporarily for the agent's use. If your *application* needs persistent file storage (e.g., user uploads), see [File storage (Emergent Object Store)](/file-storage-emergent-object-store).

---

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Your first build" icon="rocket" href="/your-first-build-walkthrough">
    Walk through a complete build from chat to deployment.
  </Card>
  <Card title="The chat-to-deployment flow" icon="diagram-project" href="/the-chat-to-deployment-flow">
    Understand the end-to-end lifecycle of an Emergent app.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Secrets & env variables" icon="key" href="/secrets-env-variables">
    Configure API keys and environment-specific settings.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Deployment types" icon="server" href="/deployment-types">
    Choose the right deployment strategy for your app.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

pre-deploy-pre-publish-health-check.title: Pre-deploy / pre-publish health check
pre-deploy-pre-publish-health-check.content:
## Before you deploy

Every deploy (web or mobile) is a published snapshot of your app. Taking a few minutes to verify readiness before you ship will save hours of firefighting later.

<Note title="Preview ≠ production">
The [preview environment](/preview-vs-deployed-separate) runs your latest code in development mode. Deployment creates a separate, optimized production build — so always test the *deployed* version after your first publish.
</Note>

---

## Preview and test thoroughly

Before you hit deploy, exercise your app as a real user would.

<Steps>

<Step title="Test all core features">
Walk through your primary user flows end-to-end: sign-up, login, main actions, checkout, etc. Confirm buttons trigger the right actions, forms validate correctly, and data saves as expected.
</Step>

<Step title="Check responsiveness">
Resize your browser (or use dev tools device emulation) to confirm layouts adapt cleanly from mobile to tablet to desktop. Text should remain readable, buttons tappable, and images properly scaled.
</Step>

<Step title="Test interactivity and state">
Open dropdowns, modals, tabs, and drawers. Verify animations play smoothly, loading spinners appear during async work, and error messages show when they should.
</Step>

<Step title="On-device testing for mobile apps">
If you are deploying a mobile app, install the preview build on a real device (iOS or Android) via TestFlight or an APK. Touch targets, scrolling behavior, keyboard handling, and camera/gallery permissions all behave differently on real hardware.
</Step>

</Steps>

<Tip>
Ask a colleague or friend to try the preview — fresh eyes catch usability issues you've become blind to.
</Tip>

---

## Pre-deploy readiness checklist

Before you publish to production, confirm each item below.

### Technical readiness

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Environment variables and secrets">
Ensure production API keys, database credentials, and third-party service tokens are set in your deployment environment (not hardcoded). The [Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) is included by default; add any additional keys your app requires.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Database migrations and seed data">
If your app uses [MongoDB](/database-mongodb) or another data store, confirm schema changes are applied and any required seed data (categories, initial settings, etc.) is present in production.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Authentication flows">
Test sign-up, login, logout, and password reset with real email addresses. Verify email delivery (check spam folders), session persistence, and protected route behavior.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Third-party integrations">
Confirm payment gateways, email services, analytics, and any external APIs are configured with production credentials and return expected responses.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Error handling">
Deliberately trigger error states (invalid form input, network failures, missing resources) and confirm your app shows helpful messages rather than crashing or hanging.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

### Content and polish

| Item | What to check |
|------|---------------|
| **Copy and spelling** | Scan visible text for typos, placeholder "lorem ipsum," and broken grammar. |
| **Images and assets** | Verify all images load, logos are high-resolution, and icons are consistent. |
| **Branding** | Confirm app name, favicon, and splash screen reflect your final brand. |
| **Legal pages** | Include privacy policy, terms of service, and any required disclaimers. |

### Performance and SEO (web)

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Page load speed">
Open your preview in an incognito window and watch the initial render. If it feels sluggish, investigate large images, heavy third-party scripts, or unoptimized bundles.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Meta tags and Open Graph">
Confirm page titles, descriptions, and social share images (`og:image`, `twitter:card`) are set so links preview well when shared.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Mobile viewport meta tag">
Verify `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` is present so mobile browsers render at the correct scale.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

### Mobile-specific (iOS and Android)

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="App store metadata">
Prepare your app name, description, screenshots, category, and keywords. Have your icon ready in all required sizes (iOS needs 1024×1024, Android needs adaptive icon layers).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Permissions and capabilities">
Ensure your app requests only the permissions it actually uses (camera, location, notifications, etc.) and include usage descriptions that explain *why* each permission is needed.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Platform-specific testing">
Test on both iOS and Android devices if you are building cross-platform. Pay attention to status bar styling, safe area insets, back-button behavior, and keyboard dismissal.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Deployment confidence checklist

Right before you click "Deploy," confirm:

- [ ] **You have tested in preview** and fixed any obvious bugs.
- [ ] **Environment variables are set** for production.
- [ ] **Database and backend services are live** and accessible.
- [ ] **Core user flows work end-to-end** (sign-up, main feature, checkout, etc.).
- [ ] **Branding, copy, and legal pages** are final and proofread.
- [ ] **(Web)** Meta tags, favicon, and custom domain (if using) are configured. See [custom domain](/custom-domain).
- [ ] **(Mobile)** App store assets and permissions are ready.

<Success>
When you can check every box above, you are ready to ship. Deploy with confidence — and remember you can always push updates if you discover something after launch.
</Success>

---

## After you deploy

Once your app is live, verify the deployed build behaves identically to preview. The [preview and deployed environments](/preview-vs-deployed-separate) are separate, so it is normal to see a production URL (web) or a new build number (mobile).

Monitor user feedback, error logs, and analytics for the first few hours. Early adopters will often surface edge cases you missed in testing.

<Tip title="Keep iterating">
Every deploy is a snapshot — not a finish line. Use real-world usage to guide your next round of improvements.
</Tip>

design-inconsistencies.title: Design inconsistencies
design-inconsistencies.content:
## Overview

Design inconsistencies—misaligned elements, inconsistent spacing, broken layouts on different screen sizes—are common when building visually complex apps. Emergent's agents can fix these issues when you describe what's wrong or share a screenshot.

The agent has full access to your app's design system, components, and styling. Treating it as a collaborative designer usually resolves issues faster than trying to edit code manually.

## Common design issues

### Layout breaks on mobile or desktop

If your app looks correct on one screen size but broken on another, describe the problem in chat:

- "The sidebar overlaps content on mobile"
- "Cards stack vertically on desktop—they should be in a grid"
- "Navigation menu doesn't collapse on small screens"

The agent will adjust responsive breakpoints, Flexbox/Grid rules, or component variants.

<Tip>
Attach a screenshot showing the broken layout. Visual context helps the agent diagnose faster.
</Tip>

### Inconsistent spacing or alignment

Spacing drift happens when components use hard-coded margins instead of design tokens. Tell the agent:

- "Button spacing is uneven across pages"
- "Card padding looks different in the dashboard vs. settings"
- "Headings don't align with the left edge of content"

The agent will normalize spacing using your design system's tokens (`spacing-4`, `gap-md`, etc.) or create them if missing.

### Colors or fonts don't match the design

If brand colors, typography, or button styles vary:

- "Primary button color is inconsistent—some are blue, some teal"
- "Headings use different fonts on different pages"
- "This section should use the brand green, not gray"

The agent will update components to reference theme variables and ensure consistency.

<Note>
If you haven't defined a design system yet, ask the agent to create one: "Set up a design system with our brand colors and typography."
</Note>

### Elements overlap or have incorrect z-index

Overlapping modals, dropdowns hidden behind other elements, or fixed headers covering content are z-index issues. Describe what you see:

- "The dropdown menu appears behind the modal backdrop"
- "Fixed header covers the top of the page content"
- "Tooltip is cut off by the card container"

The agent will adjust stacking contexts and `z-index` values.

### Images or icons are missing, broken, or incorrectly sized

If assets don't display properly:

- "Profile images are stretched/squashed"
- "Icons are too large in the navigation"
- "Hero image doesn't load"

The agent can fix aspect ratios, apply `object-fit`, update icon sizing, or swap placeholder URLs for working assets.

## How to report design issues

<Steps>
<Step title="Describe the issue clearly">
Use plain language: "The login form is off-center on desktop" or "Button text is cut off on mobile."
</Step>

<Step title="Share a screenshot or screen recording">
Attach an image showing the problem. Highlight the affected area if helpful. The agent's vision capability processes screenshots directly.
</Step>

<Step title="Specify the page or component">
If the issue is localized: "This happens on the `/dashboard` page" or "Only in the `UserCard` component."
</Step>

<Step title="Mention the device/viewport if relevant">
"This only happens on mobile" or "Broken in Safari, fine in Chrome."
</Step>
</Steps>

The agent will propose a fix, update the code, and deploy. You'll see changes in the live preview immediately.

<Tip title="Use comparisons">
"Make the spacing match the homepage" or "This card should look like the one in the sidebar" helps the agent match existing patterns.
</Tip>

## Preventing design drift

### Request a design system early

Ask the agent to scaffold a design system with reusable tokens for colors, typography, spacing, and shadows:

```
"Create a design system with our brand colors (primary: #3B82F6, secondary: #10B981) and consistent spacing."
```

The agent will generate theme files and apply them across components.

### Use design system tokens consistently

When requesting new features, reference the design system:

- "Use `primary-600` for the button background"
- "Apply `spacing-lg` between sections"

This keeps styling predictable.

### Review on multiple viewports

Emergent's preview updates in real time. Test your app at different screen sizes (resize the preview pane or open the live URL on your phone). Report layout issues as you spot them.

<Info>
The workspace preview pane supports responsive resizing. Drag the edge to simulate mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports.
</Info>

### Consolidate one-off styles

If you notice repeated custom styles ("This heading is bold and 24px in three places"), ask the agent to extract a reusable component or style:

```
"Create a `SectionHeading` component for these repeated bold 24px headings."
```

## When to escalate

Most design issues resolve with a chat message and optional screenshot. If the agent's fix doesn't work after 2–3 attempts:

- Describe what changed and what's still broken
- Share before/after screenshots
- Ask the agent to explain its approach: "Why is this element still misaligned?"

The agent can reason through CSS specificity conflicts, framework quirks, or inherited styles.

<Warning>
Avoid editing generated CSS or component files directly in the code editor unless you're experienced with the framework. Manual edits can conflict with the agent's changes and create merge issues.
</Warning>

## Related resources

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Workspace tour" icon="compass" href="/a-tour-of-the-workspace">
Learn how to use the preview pane and inspect design changes
</Card>
<Card title="Web ↔ Mobile conversion" icon="mobile" href="/web-mobile-conversion-canonical">
Adapt designs for different platforms
</Card>
<Card title="Glossary" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
Understand design system, tokens, and other Emergent terms
</Card>
</CardGroup>

shopify.title: Shopify
shopify.content:
## Overview

Emergent's Shopify integration lets your app connect to Shopify stores, retrieve product catalogs, manage orders, and synchronize inventory—all through a simple API connection. This guide walks you through setting up the integration so your app can interact with Shopify data.

<Note>
Before you begin, you'll need a Shopify store (or Partner account with a development store) and admin access to install apps and generate API credentials.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

- A Shopify store or development store
- Admin permissions to install apps and manage API credentials
- An active Emergent project where you want to add Shopify functionality

## Setup process

<Steps>

<Step title="Create a Shopify app">

Log in to your Shopify Partner Dashboard (or your store's admin) and create a new app:

1. Navigate to **Apps** in your Shopify admin
2. Click **Develop apps** (or **App and sales channel settings** → **Develop apps**)
3. Click **Create an app**
4. Enter an app name (e.g., "My Emergent Integration")
5. Click **Create app**

</Step>

<Step title="Configure API scopes">

Your app needs permission to access store data. In the app settings:

1. Click **Configure Admin API scopes**
2. Select the scopes your integration requires (common ones include `read_products`, `write_products`, `read_orders`, `write_orders`, `read_inventory`, `write_inventory`)
3. Click **Save**

<Tip>
Start with read-only scopes during development; you can add write permissions later when you're ready to modify store data.
</Tip>

</Step>

<Step title="Install the app on your store">

After configuring scopes:

1. Click **Install app** in the app overview
2. Review the permissions and click **Install**
3. Shopify will generate an **Admin API access token**—copy this token immediately (you won't be able to see it again)

</Step>

<Step title="Add credentials to Emergent">

In your Emergent workspace:

1. Open the **Settings** panel
2. Navigate to **Integrations** → **Shopify**
3. Paste your **Store URL** (e.g., `mystore.myshopify.com`)
4. Paste the **Admin API access token** you copied earlier
5. Click **Save**

Your app can now call Shopify APIs using these credentials.

</Step>

<Step title="Test the connection">

Verify the integration by describing a simple query to Emergent:

```
"Fetch the first 10 products from my Shopify store and display their titles and prices."
```

Emergent will generate code that uses the Shopify API to retrieve products. If the connection is successful, you'll see product data in your app.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Common use cases

<CardGroup cols={2}>

<Card title="Product catalog sync" icon="box">
Display your Shopify inventory in a custom storefront or mobile app
</Card>

<Card title="Order management" icon="receipt">
Create, update, and track orders programmatically
</Card>

<Card title="Inventory monitoring" icon="warehouse">
Real-time stock level checks and low-inventory alerts
</Card>

<Card title="Customer data" icon="users">
Retrieve customer profiles, order histories, and preferences
</Card>

</CardGroup>

## API rate limits

Shopify enforces rate limits on API calls to protect store performance. The standard REST Admin API allows:

- **2 requests per second** for most endpoints
- **4 requests per second** for GraphQL (with cost-based throttling)

<Warning>
If your app exceeds rate limits, Shopify will return `429 Too Many Requests` errors. Build in exponential backoff and respect the `Retry-After` header in responses.
</Warning>

## Webhooks for real-time updates

Instead of polling Shopify for changes, register webhooks to receive instant notifications when products, orders, or inventory change:

1. In your Shopify app settings, go to **Webhooks**
2. Click **Create webhook**
3. Select the event (e.g., `products/update`, `orders/create`)
4. Enter your Emergent app's webhook endpoint URL
5. Click **Save**

Emergent can generate webhook handlers that parse and store incoming Shopify events.

<Info>
Describe your webhook requirements in chat—Emergent will scaffold the endpoint, parse the payload, and help you store or act on the data.
</Info>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="API credentials not working">
- Verify the access token was copied correctly (no extra spaces)
- Confirm the app is installed on the correct store
- Check that required API scopes are enabled in the app configuration
- Regenerate the token if you suspect it was compromised
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Missing product data">
- Ensure `read_products` scope is granted
- Verify products are published to the sales channel your app is accessing
- Check that you're querying the correct store (if you have multiple)
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Rate limit errors">
- Implement exponential backoff in your request logic
- Cache frequently accessed data to reduce API calls
- Consider switching to GraphQL for more efficient bulk queries
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

## Additional resources

- [Shopify Admin API documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin)
- [Shopify GraphQL reference](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql)
- [Webhook event reference](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-rest/latest/resources/webhook)

<Tip>
Once your Shopify integration is live, you can expand it by asking Emergent to "add a product search feature" or "create a dashboard showing today's orders"—the AI will build on your existing Shopify connection.
</Tip>

key-integrations-catalogue.title: Key integrations catalogue
key-integrations-catalogue.content:
## Overview

Emergent supports a curated set of integrations that let your app connect to third-party APIs, databases, and services without leaving the platform. Each integration is configured through environment variables in your [workspace settings](/a-tour-of-the-workspace), and the platform securely injects credentials at runtime.

<Info>
All API keys and secrets are encrypted at rest and never exposed in logs or client-side code.
</Info>

---

## AI & Language Models

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Universal LLM Key" icon="brain" href="/the-universal-llm-key">
    Access OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other LLM providers through a single unified key managed by Emergent.
  </Card>
  <Card title="OpenAI" icon="message-square">
    Direct integration for GPT models, embeddings, and assistants. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` in your environment.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Anthropic" icon="cpu">
    Claude models for chat and function calling. Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Google AI" icon="sparkles">
    Gemini models and PaLM API. Configure `GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY`.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Databases & Storage

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="MongoDB" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
    Managed NoSQL database provisioned automatically for every workspace.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Supabase" icon="box">
    Postgres database, authentication, and storage. Set `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Firebase" icon="flame">
    Realtime database, Firestore, and authentication. Provide `FIREBASE_CONFIG` JSON.
  </Card>
  <Card title="AWS S3" icon="folder">
    Object storage for files and media. Requires `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `AWS_S3_BUCKET`.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Payment & Commerce

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Stripe" icon="credit-card">
    Accept payments, manage subscriptions, and handle billing. Set `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="PayPal" icon="wallet">
    Alternative payment gateway. Configure `PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID` and `PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Shopify" icon="shopping-bag">
    E-commerce store integration. Requires `SHOPIFY_STORE_URL` and `SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Communication & Messaging

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="SendGrid" icon="mail">
    Transactional email delivery. Set `SENDGRID_API_KEY`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Twilio" icon="phone">
    SMS, voice, and WhatsApp messaging. Requires `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` and `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Slack" icon="message-circle">
    Post messages and interact with Slack workspaces. Configure `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Discord" icon="hash">
    Bot integration for Discord servers. Set `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Analytics & Monitoring

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Google Analytics" icon="bar-chart">
    Track page views and events. Provide `GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Mixpanel" icon="trending-up">
    Product analytics and funnel tracking. Set `MIXPANEL_TOKEN`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Sentry" icon="alert-circle">
    Error tracking and performance monitoring. Requires `SENTRY_DSN`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="PostHog" icon="activity">
    Open-source product analytics. Configure `POSTHOG_API_KEY` and `POSTHOG_HOST`.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Authentication & Identity

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Auth0" icon="lock">
    Managed authentication with social logins. Set `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, and `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Clerk" icon="shield">
    User management and authentication components. Requires `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="OAuth Providers" icon="users">
    Direct OAuth integration with Google, GitHub, Facebook, and more. Configure provider-specific keys.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Utilities & Automation

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Zapier" icon="zap">
    Connect to thousands of apps via webhooks. No API key required — configure webhook URLs.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Airtable" icon="table">
    Spreadsheet-database hybrid. Set `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` and `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Google Sheets" icon="sheet">
    Read and write spreadsheet data. Requires Google OAuth or service account credentials.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Scheduled Tasks" icon="clock" href="/integrations-scheduled-tasks">
    Run cron jobs and recurring workflows natively in Emergent.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Maps & Location

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Google Maps" icon="map">
    Geocoding, places, and directions. Set `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Mapbox" icon="map-pin">
    Custom map styles and geospatial APIs. Requires `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## How to add an integration

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open workspace settings">
    Click the gear icon in the left sidebar or navigate to **Settings** in your workspace.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Add environment variables">
    Under **Environment Variables**, click **Add Variable** and enter the key name and secret value for your integration.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Reference in your code">
    Access the variable with `process.env.VARIABLE_NAME` (Node.js) or your framework's environment API.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Redeploy">
    Environment changes take effect on the next build. Emergent will prompt you to redeploy if necessary.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
Never commit API keys to your repository or share them in chat. Always use environment variables.
</Warning>

---

## Request a new integration

If you need an integration not listed here, describe it in chat and the AI agents will attempt to configure it using standard REST APIs or SDKs. For official platform support, contact the Emergent team or submit a feature request.

<Tip>
Most modern APIs work out-of-the-box by setting the appropriate environment variables and installing the vendor's SDK through chat (e.g., "install the Notion SDK and connect to my workspace").
</Tip>

---

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Integrations & scheduled tasks" icon="plug" href="/integrations-scheduled-tasks">
    Learn how integrations work and how to set up recurring jobs.
  </Card>
  <Card title="A tour of the workspace" icon="compass" href="/a-tour-of-the-workspace">
    Overview of the workspace UI and where to manage environment variables.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>
