gemini.title: Gemini
gemini.content:
## Overview

Google Gemini is a family of multimodal AI models that can be integrated into your Emergent applications for chat, content generation, vision tasks, and more. Emergent provides built-in support for Gemini models through the Universal LLM Key system, making it simple to add Google's latest AI capabilities to your app.

This guide walks you through setting up Gemini in your Emergent project and making your first API call.

---

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- An active Emergent project
- A Google Cloud account with access to the Gemini API
- A Gemini API key from [Google AI Studio](https://makersuite.google.com/app/apikey) or Google Cloud Console

<Note>
Gemini API keys are free to generate, though usage may be subject to Google's rate limits and pricing based on your tier and model selection.
</Note>

---

## Getting Your Gemini API Key

<Steps>
<Step title="Navigate to Google AI Studio">
Visit [Google AI Studio](https://makersuite.google.com/app/apikey) and sign in with your Google account.
</Step>

<Step title="Create an API key">
Click **Get API key** or **Create API key**, then select an existing Google Cloud project or create a new one. Copy the generated key immediately—you won't be able to view it again.
</Step>

<Step title="Store the key securely">
Keep your API key in a secure location. You'll add it to Emergent in the next section.
</Step>
</Steps>

---

## Adding Gemini to Your Emergent Project

Emergent uses the [Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) system to manage AI provider credentials securely. You can add your Gemini key either through the dashboard or by setting an environment variable.

### Option 1: Via the Emergent Dashboard

<Steps>
<Step title="Open your project settings">
Navigate to your project in the Emergent dashboard and open the **Settings** or **Integrations** tab.
</Step>

<Step title="Add the Gemini key">
Locate the **AI Providers** section, select **Google Gemini**, and paste your API key into the designated field.
</Step>

<Step title="Save your changes">
Click **Save** to securely store your key. Emergent encrypts all API keys at rest.
</Step>
</Steps>

### Option 2: Via Environment Variable

You can also provide your Gemini key as an environment variable in your project:

```bash
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key_here
```

<Tip>
Environment variables take precedence over dashboard settings, making them ideal for local development or CI/CD pipelines.
</Tip>

---

## Using Gemini in Your Code

Once configured, you can call Gemini models using standard AI SDK patterns or direct HTTP requests. Emergent automatically routes your requests through the Universal LLM Key system.

### Example: Chat Completion

<CodeGroup>
```javascript
// Using Vercel AI SDK
import { generateText } from 'ai';
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';

const result = await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-1.5-flash'),
  prompt: 'Explain how photosynthesis works in simple terms.',
});

console.log(result.text);
```

```python
# Using Google's Python SDK
import google.generativeai as genai

genai.configure(api_key=process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY)
model = genai.GenerativeModel('gemini-1.5-flash')

response = model.generate_content(
    'Explain how photosynthesis works in simple terms.'
)
print(response.text)
```

```typescript
// Using fetch directly
const response = await fetch(
  'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-1.5-flash:generateContent',
  {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'x-goog-api-key': process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      contents: [{
        parts: [{ text: 'Explain how photosynthesis works in simple terms.' }]
      }]
    })
  }
);

const data = await response.json();
console.log(data.candidates[0].content.parts[0].text);
```
</CodeGroup>

---

## Available Gemini Models

Google offers several Gemini model variants optimized for different use cases:

| Model | Best For | Context Window |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| `gemini-1.5-pro` | Complex reasoning, long-form content, multimodal tasks | Up to 2M tokens |
| `gemini-1.5-flash` | Fast, efficient responses for most use cases | Up to 1M tokens |
| `gemini-1.0-pro` | Stable production workloads, text-only tasks | 32K tokens |

<Info>
Model availability and capabilities may change. Check [Google's documentation](https://ai.google.dev/models/gemini) for the latest model options and specifications.
</Info>

---

## Multimodal Capabilities

Gemini models support text, image, audio, and video inputs, making them ideal for applications that need to process multiple content types.

### Example: Vision Task

```javascript
import { generateText } from 'ai';
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';

const result = await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-1.5-flash'),
  messages: [
    {
      role: 'user',
      content: [
        { type: 'text', text: 'What is in this image?' },
        { type: 'image', image: 'https://example.com/photo.jpg' }
      ]
    }
  ]
});

console.log(result.text);
```

---

## Best Practices

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="How do I choose between Gemini models?">
Use `gemini-1.5-flash` for most applications—it's fast and cost-effective. Switch to `gemini-1.5-pro` when you need maximum reasoning depth, very long context windows, or complex multimodal tasks. Use `gemini-1.0-pro` only if you need a stable, text-only model for production workloads.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How are API keys secured in Emergent?">
All API keys entered through the dashboard are encrypted at rest and never exposed in client-side code. Emergent's backend handles authentication transparently, so your keys remain secure even in public repositories.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I use different Gemini models in the same project?">
Yes. You can specify the model name in each API call, allowing you to mix `gemini-1.5-flash` for simple queries and `gemini-1.5-pro` for complex tasks within the same application.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What if I hit rate limits?">
Google enforces rate limits based on your API tier. If you encounter `429` errors, implement exponential backoff in your retry logic or upgrade your Google Cloud quota. Emergent does not impose additional rate limits on Gemini calls.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Troubleshooting

<Warning>
If you see authentication errors, verify that your `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is correctly set and that the key has not been revoked or restricted in the Google Cloud Console.
</Warning>

Common issues and solutions:

- **"API key not valid"** — Double-check that you copied the full key without extra spaces. Regenerate the key in Google AI Studio if needed.
- **"Model not found"** — Ensure you're using a valid model identifier (e.g., `gemini-1.5-flash`). Some models may require allowlist access.
- **Slow responses** — Gemini Pro models may take longer for complex requests. Consider using Flash models for latency-sensitive applications.
- **CORS errors** — Gemini API calls should be made server-side. If calling from the browser, proxy requests through your Emergent backend.

---

## Related Resources

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="The Universal LLM Key" icon="key" href="/the-universal-llm-key">
Learn how Emergent manages AI provider credentials securely
</Card>

<Card title="Glossary" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
Understand key terms used throughout the platform
</Card>
</CardGroup>

streaks-rewards.title: Streaks & rewards
streaks-rewards.content:
## What is a streak?

A **streak** counts consecutive days on which you submit at least one job to Emergent. Every midnight UTC, the platform checks whether you ran a job during the previous 24 hours; if so, your streak increments by one day.

Streaks are available only to paid subscribers (Starter, Developer, or Team plans). Free users do not accrue streak counts or earn streak rewards.

<Note title="What counts as a job?">
Any workspace operation that consumes credits—such as generating a component, running a build, or creating media—extends your streak. Simply opening the workspace does not count.
</Note>

---

## Streak rewards

Maintaining a streak unlocks bonus credits and special items:

| Milestone       | Reward                                                                 |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Day 7           | **500 bonus credits** deposited into your workspace balance            |
| Day 14          | Mystery box (small) containing credits or a repair token               |
| Day 30          | Mystery box (large) containing a higher-value credit bundle            |
| Every 7 days thereafter | Rotating rewards cycle through credit bundles and mystery boxes |

Rewards are credited automatically at the start of the day (00:01 UTC) following the milestone. Check your workspace **Activity** panel or billing page to see the deposit.

<Tip>
Day-7 bonuses stack if you maintain multiple streaks across different billing periods—keep coding daily to maximize your free credits.
</Tip>

---

## Mystery boxes

Mystery boxes are virtual loot drops that open automatically when awarded. Contents include:

- **Credit bundles** ranging from 200 to 2,000 credits  
- **Repair tokens** (one per box) that let you restore a broken streak once  

The exact contents are randomised but weighted toward higher values at longer milestones (day 30+ boxes contain larger bundles on average).

---

## Repair tokens

A **repair token** forgives one missed day and keeps your streak alive. Tokens are:

- **Single-use**—once consumed, the token disappears  
- **Applied automatically** the first time you would otherwise lose a streak  
- **Earned** through mystery boxes or occasional promotional events  

When you miss a day, the platform checks your token inventory; if you hold at least one token, it deducts the token and preserves your current streak count. You'll see a notification confirming the repair.

<Warning>
Tokens do **not** stack the forgiveness window—missing two consecutive days will consume one token on the first miss, then break the streak on the second.
</Warning>

---

## Eligibility and rules

<Steps>

<Step title="Active paid subscription required">
Your plan (Starter, Developer, or Team) must be current. If your subscription lapses, the streak pauses but does **not** reset; reactivating the plan resumes counting from the paused total.
</Step>

<Step title="One job per calendar day (UTC)">
The platform measures days in UTC. A job submitted at 23:59 UTC counts for that day; the next job must land before 23:59 UTC the following day.
</Step>

<Step title="Grace period for timezone edge cases">
A 2-hour grace window (00:00–02:00 UTC) extends the previous day's eligibility if you submit a job during that window **and** your account timezone is set to a zone west of UTC. This prevents penalising users near the international date line.
</Step>

<Step title="Plan downgrades or cancellations">
Downgrading to Free freezes your streak immediately; upgrading back to a paid tier resumes it. Cancelling outright resets the streak to zero after the billing period ends.
</Step>

</Steps>

---

## Viewing your current streak

Open the **Billing** page from the workspace sidebar. The streak counter appears near the top, showing:

- Current consecutive days  
- Next milestone and reward  
- Repair tokens in inventory  

A calendar widget highlights the days you've submitted jobs in the current month.

---

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Do collaborative jobs count toward my streak?">
Yes. Any job you initiate or approve in a shared workspace counts, regardless of which team member triggered it.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens if I change plans mid-streak?">
Upgrading (Free → Starter, Starter → Developer) preserves your streak. Downgrading to Free pauses it; reactivating a paid plan resumes from the paused count.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I buy repair tokens directly?">
Not yet. Tokens are currently earned only through mystery boxes and special promotions. We may add a token shop in future releases.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Do bonus credits from streaks expire?">
Yes. Streak-reward credits follow the same [expiry policy](/credit-expiry-recharging) as purchased credits—they remain valid for the duration of your active subscription and expire when the plan lapses.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Tips for maintaining a long streak

- **Set a daily reminder** at a consistent time (morning or evening) to run a quick job—even a small UI tweak or test build counts.  
- **Batch exploratory work** into your streak window rather than clustering it all on weekends.  
- **Monitor your token inventory** so you know whether you have forgiveness cushion for travel or busy days.  
- **Check the Activity feed** each day to confirm the job registered before midnight UTC.

Streaks reward consistent engagement and help offset credit costs for regular builders. Keep the momentum going and watch the bonuses accumulate.
streaks-rewards.description: Paid-user daily-streak system counting days with a job submission; credit rewards (day-7 bonus, mystery boxes), repair tokens, and eligibility rules.

razorpay.title: Razorpay
razorpay.content:
## Overview

Razorpay is a payment gateway that enables businesses in India and Southeast Asia to accept, process, and disburse payments online. This guide walks you through integrating Razorpay into your Emergent application to accept payments from customers.

<Note>
Razorpay is primarily designed for businesses operating in India. Ensure your business is eligible and complies with Razorpay's registration requirements before integrating.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- A Razorpay account ([sign up here](https://razorpay.com))
- Your Razorpay **API Key** and **API Secret** from the Razorpay Dashboard
- Basic understanding of payment flows (checkout, webhooks, order verification)

## Getting Your Razorpay Credentials

<Steps>
  <Step title="Log into the Razorpay Dashboard">
    Navigate to [dashboard.razorpay.com](https://dashboard.razorpay.com) and sign in with your credentials.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Access API Keys">
    In the left sidebar, go to **Settings** → **API Keys**.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Generate keys">
    If you haven't already, click **Generate Key** to create a new key pair. You'll see both a `key_id` (public) and a `key_secret` (private).
    
    <Warning>
    The **Key Secret** is shown only once. Store it securely — you'll need it for server-side operations.
    </Warning>
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Copy your credentials">
    Note down:
    - **Key ID** (starts with `rzp_test_` for test mode or `rzp_live_` for production)
    - **Key Secret**
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Storing Credentials in Emergent

To keep your Razorpay credentials secure, store them as environment variables rather than hardcoding them in your app.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open your project settings">
    In the Emergent editor, navigate to your project's **Settings** or **Environment Variables** panel.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Add Razorpay variables">
    Create the following environment variables:
    
    - `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` — your public key (e.g., `rzp_test_ABC123`)
    - `RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET` — your private key secret
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Reference them in code">
    In your server-side logic, reference these as `process.env.RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` and `process.env.RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET`.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Implementing Razorpay Checkout

Razorpay provides a hosted checkout interface that simplifies payment collection. Below is a typical integration pattern.

### Creating an Order (Server-Side)

Before displaying the checkout, create an order on your backend using the Razorpay API.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript Node.js (Express)
import Razorpay from 'razorpay';

const razorpay = new Razorpay({
  key_id: process.env.RAZORPAY_KEY_ID,
  key_secret: process.env.RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET,
});

app.post('/api/create-order', async (req, res) => {
  const { amount, currency = 'INR' } = req.body;

  const options = {
    amount: amount * 100, // amount in smallest currency unit (paise)
    currency,
    receipt: `receipt_${Date.now()}`,
  };

  try {
    const order = await razorpay.orders.create(options);
    res.json({ orderId: order.id, amount: order.amount });
  } catch (error) {
    res.status(500).json({ error: error.message });
  }
});
```

```python Python (Flask)
from razorpay import Client
import os

razorpay_client = Client(auth=(
    os.getenv('RAZORPAY_KEY_ID'),
    os.getenv('RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET')
))

@app.route('/api/create-order', methods=['POST'])
def create_order():
    data = request.json
    amount = data.get('amount')
    currency = data.get('currency', 'INR')

    order = razorpay_client.order.create({
        'amount': amount * 100,  # paise
        'currency': currency,
        'receipt': f'receipt_{int(time.time())}'
    })

    return jsonify({
        'orderId': order['id'],
        'amount': order['amount']
    })
```
</CodeGroup>

### Displaying the Checkout (Client-Side)

Use the Razorpay Checkout.js library to present the payment modal to users.

```html
<script src="https://checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js"></script>

<button id="pay-button">Pay Now</button>

<script>
  document.getElementById('pay-button').onclick = async () => {
    // Fetch order from your backend
    const response = await fetch('/api/create-order', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 500, currency: 'INR' }) // ₹500
    });
    const { orderId, amount } = await response.json();

    // Initialize Razorpay Checkout
    const options = {
      key: 'YOUR_RAZORPAY_KEY_ID', // replace or load from config
      amount,
      currency: 'INR',
      order_id: orderId,
      name: 'Your App Name',
      description: 'Payment for XYZ',
      handler: function (response) {
        // Payment successful
        console.log('Payment ID:', response.razorpay_payment_id);
        console.log('Order ID:', response.razorpay_order_id);
        console.log('Signature:', response.razorpay_signature);
        
        // Verify payment on your server
        verifyPayment(response);
      },
      prefill: {
        name: 'Customer Name',
        email: 'customer@example.com',
      },
      theme: {
        color: '#3399cc'
      }
    };

    const rzp = new Razorpay(options);
    rzp.open();
  };
</script>
```

<Tip>
When working in Emergent, describe the checkout flow to the AI agents in chat (e.g., "Add a Razorpay checkout button that creates an order for ₹500"). The agents will scaffold the frontend and backend code for you.
</Tip>

## Verifying Payment Signatures

Always verify payment signatures server-side to prevent tampering.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Receive payment response">
    After a successful payment, Razorpay returns `razorpay_payment_id`, `razorpay_order_id`, and `razorpay_signature` to your `handler` callback.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Send to your server">
    POST these values to a server endpoint for verification.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Verify the signature">
    Use the following logic to confirm authenticity:
    
    <CodeGroup>
    ```javascript Node.js
    const crypto = require('crypto');

    app.post('/api/verify-payment', (req, res) => {
      const { razorpay_order_id, razorpay_payment_id, razorpay_signature } = req.body;

      const body = razorpay_order_id + '|' + razorpay_payment_id;
      const expectedSignature = crypto
        .createHmac('sha256', process.env.RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET)
        .update(body)
        .digest('hex');

      if (expectedSignature === razorpay_signature) {
        // Payment is legitimate
        res.json({ status: 'success' });
      } else {
        res.status(400).json({ status: 'verification_failed' });
      }
    });
    ```

    ```python Python
    import hmac
    import hashlib

    @app.route('/api/verify-payment', methods=['POST'])
    def verify_payment():
        data = request.json
        order_id = data['razorpay_order_id']
        payment_id = data['razorpay_payment_id']
        signature = data['razorpay_signature']

        body = f"{order_id}|{payment_id}"
        expected_signature = hmac.new(
            os.getenv('RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET').encode(),
            body.encode(),
            hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest()

        if expected_signature == signature:
            return jsonify({'status': 'success'})
        else:
            return jsonify({'status': 'verification_failed'}), 400
    ```
    </CodeGroup>
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning title="Always Verify Server-Side">
Client-side validation alone is insufficient. An attacker can manipulate browser requests. Signature verification on your backend is the only reliable proof of a legitimate payment.
</Warning>

## Handling Webhooks

Razorpay sends webhook events (e.g., `payment.captured`, `payment.failed`) to notify you of payment status changes asynchronously.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Configure webhook URL">
    In the Razorpay Dashboard, go to **Settings** → **Webhooks** and add your endpoint URL (e.g., `https://yourdomain.com/api/razorpay-webhook`).
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Set a webhook secret">
    Razorpay lets you define a secret for webhook signature verification. Note this down.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Implement the webhook handler">
    <CodeGroup>
    ```javascript Node.js
    app.post('/api/razorpay-webhook', (req, res) => {
      const webhookSignature = req.headers['x-razorpay-signature'];
      const webhookSecret = process.env.RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET;

      const expectedSignature = crypto
        .createHmac('sha256', webhookSecret)
        .update(JSON.stringify(req.body))
        .digest('hex');

      if (expectedSignature === webhookSignature) {
        const event = req.body.event; // e.g., 'payment.captured'
        const payload = req.body.payload.payment.entity;

        // Handle event (update database, send confirmation email, etc.)
        console.log('Webhook event:', event, payload);

        res.status(200).send('OK');
      } else {
        res.status(400).send('Invalid signature');
      }
    });
    ```
    </CodeGroup>
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Testing in Development

Razorpay provides test mode credentials (keys starting with `rzp_test_`) and test card numbers for safe experimentation.

<Callout type="info" title="Test Card Numbers">
- **Success:** `4111 1111 1111 1111` (any future expiry, any CVV)
- **Failure:** Use `4111 1111 1111 1234` to simulate a failed payment

No real money is charged in test mode.
</Callout>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Use test credentials">
    Set `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` and `RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET` to your test-mode keys.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Initiate a checkout">
    Trigger a payment in your app and use a test card number.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Verify in Dashboard">
    Check the **Transactions** tab in the Razorpay Dashboard to see test payments.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Going Live

<Steps>
  <Step title="Complete KYC and activation">
    Razorpay requires business verification before you can accept live payments. Submit required documents in the Dashboard under **Account & Settings** → **Account Activation**.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Switch to live keys">
    Once approved, generate **live mode** keys (`rzp_live_...`) and update your environment variables in Emergent.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Test end-to-end">
    Perform a small real transaction to confirm everything works.
  </Step>
  
  <Step title="Monitor transactions">
    Use the Razorpay Dashboard to track payments, refunds, and settlements.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning title="Store Live Keys Securely">
Never commit live API secrets to version control. Use Emergent's environment variables or a secrets manager.
</Warning>

## Common Use Cases

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Subscriptions" icon="repeat">
    Use Razorpay's Subscriptions API to bill customers on a recurring basis (monthly, annually, etc.).
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Payment Links" icon="link">
    Generate shareable payment links for quick invoicing without building a checkout UI.
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Refunds" icon="rotate-ccw">
    Issue full or partial refunds programmatically via the Razorpay API.
  </Card>
  
  <Card title="Smart Collect" icon="download">
    Accept payments via UPI, bank transfer, or virtual accounts for B2B scenarios.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Payment succeeds but webhook isn't received">
    - Confirm your webhook URL is publicly accessible (not `localhost` in production).
    - Check the **Webhooks** logs in the Razorpay Dashboard for delivery failures.
    - Verify the endpoint responds with a `200 OK` status.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Signature verification fails">
    - Ensure you're using the correct `key_secret` (test vs. live).
    - Check that the concatenation order matches: `order_id|payment_id`.
    - Confirm no extra whitespace or encoding issues in the signature string.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Checkout modal doesn't open">
    - Verify the Razorpay Checkout.js script is loaded (`https://checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js`).
    - Check browser console for JavaScript errors.
    - Ensure `key`, `amount`, and `order_id` are all correctly populated.
  </Accordion>
  
  <Accordion title="Amount mismatch errors">
    Razorpay amounts are in the smallest currency unit (paise for INR). For ₹100, send `10000` (100 × 100). Double-check your multiplication in both order creation and checkout.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Additional Resources

- [Razorpay API Documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/)
- [Checkout.js Integration Guide](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-gateway/web-integration/)
- [Webhooks Reference](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/)
- [Razorpay Dashboard](https://dashboard.razorpay.com)

---

Need help integrating Razorpay? Describe your payment flow in the Emergent chat, and the AI agents will generate the necessary backend routes, frontend UI, and webhook handlers for you.

starting-the-process.title: Starting the process
starting-the-process.content:
## What can be built?

Emergent's mobile build system supports three types of mobile applications:

- **Native Android apps** — compiled APKs that install on Android devices and publish to Google Play Console.
- **Native iOS apps** — compiled IPA files that install on iPhones and publish to the App Store.
- **Progressive Web Apps (PWAs)** — installable web apps that run in a browser but feel native, with offline support and home-screen shortcuts.

<Note title="Platform support note">
Apple Watch and iPad apps can be coded (Swift/SwiftUI) within Emergent but cannot yet be published to the App Store through the platform. Support for these platforms is coming soon.
</Note>

All mobile apps are built using **React Native** and the **Expo framework**, which share a single codebase for both iOS and Android.

---

## Requirements

Before you start building, make sure you have:

<Steps>
<Step title="An Emergent account">
Sign up or log in at [emergent.build](https://emergent.build). You'll use the **Mobile Agent** from within your workspace.
</Step>

<Step title="The Expo Go app (for testing)">
Download **Expo Go** on your phone—it's free on both the App Store (iOS) and Google Play (Android). You'll use it to scan a QR code and preview your app live without publishing.
</Step>

<Step title="Developer accounts (for publishing)">
To ship to production, you need:

- **Apple Developer Program** account ($99/year) for iOS.
- **Google Play Console** account (one-time $25 fee) for Android.

<Warning>
Apple account approval takes **24–48 hours**. Create your account early in the process to avoid delays when you're ready to publish.
</Warning>
</Step>
</Steps>

For more on the publishing step, see [Publishing to the stores](/publishing-to-the-stores).

---

## What is Expo?

**Expo** is the open-source framework and toolchain that powers every mobile app you build in Emergent. It sits on top of React Native and provides:

- A managed build service (no Xcode or Android Studio required on your machine).
- Over-the-air updates—push fixes without resubmitting to the stores.
- A comprehensive library of native modules (camera, location, notifications, etc.).

**Expo Go** is a free companion app for iOS and Android. During development, you scan a QR code from the Emergent workspace and your app runs **live on your device**—no need to compile an APK, no App Store submission, no waiting. Code changes appear instantly.

<Tip>
Think of Expo Go as a live sandbox: it's perfect for prototyping, iteration, and demos. When you're ready to ship, Emergent builds a standalone binary you submit to the stores.
</Tip>

---

## Development workflow

Building a mobile app in Emergent follows a tight feedback loop between you and the Mobile Agent:

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the Mobile Agent and describe your app">
Navigate to the **Build › Mobile Apps** section of your workspace. Start a new conversation with the Mobile Agent and describe what you want to build—features, screens, data, design preferences, integrations.
</Step>

<Step title="Answer clarifying questions">
The agent will ask follow-up questions about authentication, navigation style, API endpoints, branding, and any ambiguities in your request. Answer these in the chat to refine the spec.
</Step>

<Step title="Preview live on your phone via Expo Go">
Once the agent generates the app, it displays a **QR code** in the workspace. Open Expo Go on your phone, tap **Scan QR code**, and point your camera at the screen. Your app launches immediately.

<Info>
Both your computer and phone must be on the same Wi-Fi network for the preview to work. If you see a connection error, check your network or use the tunnel option (available in advanced settings).
</Info>
</Step>

<Step title="Iterate and debug with the agent">
Test the app on your device. If something is broken or missing, describe the issue in the chat. The agent will update the code, and the preview reloads automatically. Repeat until you're satisfied.
</Step>

<Step title="Move to publishing when ready">
When the app is stable and feature-complete, proceed to [Publishing to the stores](/publishing-to-the-stores) to create production builds and submit them to Google Play and the App Store.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Converting an existing web app?">
If you've already built a web app in Emergent and want a mobile version, see [Web ↔ Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical) for guidance on adapting layouts, navigation, and state.
</Tip>

For a step-by-step walkthrough of your first build, see [Your first build (walkthrough)](/your-first-build-walkthrough). For an overview of how Emergent turns chat into deployed apps, read [The chat-to-deployment flow](/the-chat-to-deployment-flow).

claude.title: Claude
claude.content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of large language models known for extended context windows, strong reasoning capabilities, and careful instruction-following. Emergent natively supports Claude models through the **Universal LLM Key**, allowing you to use Claude for code generation, chat interactions, and other AI-powered features throughout the platform.

<Note>
Claude models are available on all Emergent plans. Your usage is metered through your Universal LLM Key balance.
</Note>

## Supported Models

Emergent currently supports the following Claude model families:

| Model | Context Window | Best For |
|-------|----------------|----------|
| Claude 3.5 Sonnet | 200K tokens | Code generation, complex reasoning, detailed documentation |
| Claude 3 Opus | 200K tokens | Highest-quality outputs, nuanced understanding |
| Claude 3 Sonnet | 200K tokens | Balanced performance and speed |
| Claude 3 Haiku | 200K tokens | Fast responses, simple tasks |

Model availability and naming may be updated as Anthropic releases new versions. Emergent automatically maps to the latest stable releases.

## Setting Up Claude

<Steps>
<Step title="Ensure you have LLM credits">
Claude models consume credits from your Universal LLM Key balance. Check your current balance in **Settings → Billing** or by clicking your profile icon.

If you need to add credits, see [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) for top-up instructions.
</Step>

<Step title="Select Claude in the model picker">
When starting a new conversation or editing an existing agent's configuration, open the **model picker** dropdown. Claude models appear under the "Anthropic" provider section.

Choose the model that best fits your use case—`Claude 3.5 Sonnet` is recommended for most code generation tasks.
</Step>

<Step title="Start building">
Describe your app, feature, or question as you normally would. Emergent's agents will use Claude to interpret your request, generate code, write tests, and deploy your application.
</Step>
</Steps>

## When to Use Claude

Claude excels in scenarios requiring:

- **Long-context understanding** — Claude can process large codebases, extensive documentation, or multi-file diffs in a single prompt.
- **Nuanced instruction-following** — Complex requirements with many constraints are handled reliably.
- **Safety-conscious outputs** — Claude is designed to refuse unsafe or problematic requests, reducing the risk of generating vulnerable code.

<Tip>
If you're working on a project with detailed domain logic or intricate state management, Claude 3.5 Sonnet often produces cleaner, more maintainable code than smaller or faster models.
</Tip>

## Switching Between Models Mid-Conversation

You can change models at any point during a conversation:

1. Click the **model badge** in the conversation header.
2. Select a different Claude variant (or switch to another provider entirely).
3. Continue chatting—subsequent messages will use the newly selected model.

Previous messages remain unchanged; only new responses reflect the updated model choice.

## Cost and Rate Limits

- **Pricing** is based on tokens consumed (input + output). Emergent's Universal LLM Key pricing includes a small markup over Anthropic's API rates to cover infrastructure and aggregation.
- **Rate limits** are managed automatically. If you hit a temporary quota, Emergent will queue your request and retry, or you can manually retry after a brief wait.

Check your **Usage Dashboard** under Settings to monitor token consumption by model and conversation.

<Warning>
Claude models with extended context windows can consume credits quickly when processing very large inputs. Review your prompt size if costs are higher than expected.
</Warning>

## Context Window Best Practices

Claude's 200K-token context is powerful, but here's how to make the most of it:

- **Include full file contents** when asking for refactors or debugging—Claude can handle the entire codebase context.
- **Provide examples** of desired output formats; Claude learns patterns from in-context demonstrations.
- **Avoid repetition** if possible; Claude retains conversation history well, so you don't need to re-explain setup in every message.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Claude responses are slower than expected">
Larger models (Opus, Sonnet) prioritize quality over speed. If you need faster iteration, try **Claude 3 Haiku** for simpler tasks, then switch back to Sonnet for final polish.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Model returns 'overloaded' errors">
Anthropic's API occasionally experiences high demand. Emergent will automatically retry. You can also manually retry the message or switch to another model temporarily.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Unexpected refusals or overly cautious responses">
Claude is trained to decline potentially unsafe requests. If you believe a refusal is incorrect, rephrase your prompt to clarify intent, or try a different model for comparison.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Related Resources

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="The Universal LLM Key" icon="key" href="/the-universal-llm-key">
Manage credits, view usage, and top up your balance
</Card>
<Card title="Glossary" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
Learn platform-specific terms like agents, conversations, and deployments
</Card>
</CardGroup>

ai-media-generation-image-video-audio.title: AI media generation (image/video/audio)
ai-media-generation-image-video-audio.content:
## Overview

Emergent lets you generate images, video and audio directly from your workspace using state-of-the-art AI models. Each media type consumes credits at different rates depending on model size, quality settings and output duration.

All media generation happens through [the Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key), which routes requests to the appropriate provider and automatically tracks usage against your workspace credit balance.

---

## Supported models and credit multipliers

The table below shows the available models and their credit cost per generation. Credit multipliers are applied **in addition to** the base credit cost for each API call.

| Model | Provider | Output type | Credit multiplier | Typical use |
|-------|----------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|
| **Imagen 4** | Google | Image | 2× | High-quality, photorealistic images with accurate text rendering |
| **GPT Image 1** | OpenAI | Image | 1.5× | General-purpose image generation, illustrations and concept art |
| **Sora 2** | OpenAI | Video | 10× | Text-to-video and image-to-video, cinematic quality up to 20 seconds |
| **Veo-3** | Google | Video | 8× | High-fidelity video from text prompts, natural motion and lighting |
| **ElevenLabs** | ElevenLabs | Audio (voice) | 3× | Natural voice synthesis, multilingual support and voice cloning |
| **Suno** | Suno | Audio (music) | 4× | Music generation from text descriptions, multiple styles and genres |

<Note title="Credit balance">
Check your current credit balance and recharge options on the [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) page.
</Note>

---

## How to generate media

<Steps>

<Step title="Describe your intent in chat">
Ask the AI agent to generate an image, video or audio clip. Be specific about style, mood, duration and any other constraints.

Example prompts:
- "Generate a hero image for the landing page showing a futuristic cityscape at sunset"
- "Create a 10-second video intro with our logo animating in"
- "Generate a calm voiceover for the tutorial narration in a British accent"
</Step>

<Step title="Agent selects the model">
The agent automatically picks the most suitable model based on your request. If you want a specific provider, mention it explicitly (e.g. "use Imagen for this" or "generate with Sora").
</Step>

<Step title="Media is generated and inserted">
The agent generates the asset, uploads it to your workspace storage and inserts a reference in your codebase or [database](/database-mongodb). You'll see a preview in the chat and a credit deduction in your usage log.
</Step>

</Steps>

<Tip>
For long or high-quality video, generation can take several minutes. The agent will keep you updated on progress.
</Tip>

---

## Image generation

### Imagen 4 vs GPT Image 1

- **Imagen 4** excels at photorealism, accurate text rendering in images and complex scenes with multiple objects.
- **GPT Image 1** is more cost-effective for illustrations, concept art and stylized visuals.

Both models support aspect ratio control and style prompts. The agent infers the best choice unless you specify a preference.

### Common workflows

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Hero images" icon="image">
    Generate large, high-resolution visuals for landing pages and marketing materials.
  </Card>
  <Card title="UI placeholders" icon="palette">
    Create consistent placeholder graphics for design mockups and prototypes.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Product renders" icon="cube">
    Produce photorealistic product shots from text descriptions.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Icon sets" icon="shapes">
    Generate cohesive icon families in a specific style.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---

## Video generation

### Sora 2 vs Veo-3

- **Sora 2** (OpenAI) produces cinematic, story-driven sequences with strong character consistency and smooth motion. It supports both text-to-video and image-to-video workflows.
- **Veo-3** (Google) offers high-fidelity output with realistic lighting and natural camera movement. It's particularly strong for product demos and architectural walkthroughs.

Both models can generate up to 20 seconds per clip. For longer sequences, the agent stitches multiple clips or edits them programmatically.

<Warning title="Video generation is credit-intensive">
A single 10-second video at standard quality can consume 10× the credits of a typical LLM call. Review the cost estimate before confirming generation.
</Warning>

### Supported input formats

- **Text prompt** — describe the scene, action and style.
- **Starting image** — provide a still frame and describe the motion.
- **Style reference** — link to an existing video or describe a visual style (e.g. "documentary feel" or "anime aesthetic").

---

## Audio generation

### ElevenLabs (voice synthesis)

ElevenLabs converts text to natural-sounding speech in dozens of languages. You can choose from a library of pre-built voices or clone a custom voice by uploading sample audio.

**Use cases:**
- Tutorial narration and onboarding flows.
- Dynamic in-app announcements or alerts.
- Voiceovers for video content.

For detailed configuration (voice selection, pitch, speed), see the [ElevenLabs](/elevenlabs) integration page.

### Suno (music generation)

Suno generates original music from text descriptions. Specify genre, mood, instrumentation and duration (up to 4 minutes per clip).

**Use cases:**
- Background music for video content.
- Custom app soundtracks and loading screens.
- Placeholder audio for prototypes.

<Info>
Generated music is royalty-free for use within your Emergent projects. For commercial redistribution outside the platform, review Suno's licensing terms.
</Info>

---

## Best practices

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Write detailed prompts">
The more specific your description, the better the output. Include style, lighting, camera angle, mood and any objects or text that must appear. For video, describe the start and end states explicitly.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Iterate in chat">
If the first result isn't quite right, ask the agent to refine it ("make the lighting warmer," "add a logo in the top-right corner"). Each refinement is a new generation and consumes additional credits.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Reuse assets across pages">
Once generated, media files are stored in your workspace. Reference them in multiple places (pages, emails, database records) without regenerating.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Monitor credit usage">
Check the credit log regularly if you're generating large volumes of media. Video and music generation can consume credits quickly, especially at high quality settings.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Integration with the workspace

All generated media is automatically:
- Uploaded to your workspace storage.
- Optimized for web delivery (images are converted to WebP, videos to H.264/VP9).
- Accessible via a permanent URL that works in both development and production.

If you deploy to a [custom domain](/custom-domain), media URLs are rewritten to serve from your domain's asset CDN.

For programmatic access (e.g. storing media URLs in your [MongoDB database](/database-mongodb)), the agent provides the public URL after generation.

---

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="The Universal LLM Key" icon="key" href="/the-universal-llm-key">
    How Emergent routes API calls and tracks usage
  </Card>
  <Card title="Credit expiry & recharging" icon="coins" href="/credit-expiry-recharging">
    Manage your credit balance and auto-recharge settings
  </Card>
  <Card title="ElevenLabs integration" icon="microphone" href="/elevenlabs">
    Deep-dive on voice synthesis and cloning
  </Card>
  <Card title="Glossary" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
    Definitions of workspace, agent, credit and other key terms
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

save-to-github.title: Save to GitHub
save-to-github.content:
## Overview

Emergent lets you push your project's code directly to a GitHub repository from the workspace. This is useful for version control, collaboration, or integrating the generated application into an existing CI/CD pipeline.

<Warning>
**Never commit secrets or credentials**  
Before pushing to GitHub, ensure `.env` files, API keys, and other sensitive data are stored only in Emergent's [secrets manager](/secrets-env-variables). Credentials committed to a public or shared repository can be compromised and exploited.
</Warning>

---

## Prerequisites

Before you can push code to GitHub, make sure you have:

- A GitHub account and a repository (new or existing) where you want to push the code
- Authorized Emergent to access your GitHub account (you'll be prompted during the push flow if not already connected)
- Reviewed your project files to confirm no sensitive data is included in the codebase

---

## Push to GitHub

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the workspace">
Navigate to your project workspace in Emergent. For an overview of the workspace layout, see [A tour of the workspace](/a-tour-of-the-workspace).
</Step>

<Step title="Initiate the push">
Click the **Push to GitHub** button or select **GitHub** from the integrations menu. Emergent will prompt you to authorize the GitHub integration if you haven't already.
</Step>

<Step title="Select repository and branch">
Choose an existing repository or create a new one. Specify the target branch—typically `main` or a feature branch. If the branch does not exist, Emergent will create it for you.
</Step>

<Step title="Review files to be committed">
Emergent displays a list of changed or new files. Review this list carefully to ensure no `.env`, `.env.local`, or other secret files are included. If secrets are present, remove them and store them in the [secrets manager](/secrets-env-variables) instead.
</Step>

<Step title="Commit and push">
Provide a commit message describing the changes, then click **Push**. Emergent commits the code to the specified branch and pushes it to your GitHub repository.
</Step>
</Steps>

---

## What Gets Pushed

Emergent pushes the **full application source code**, including:

- Frontend files (HTML, React/Vue components, styles)
- Backend routes, controllers, and middleware
- Configuration files (`package.json`, framework config, etc.)
- Build and deployment scripts

**Not included** by default:

- `.env` and local environment files (these remain in the secrets manager)
- `node_modules` or vendor dependencies (listed in `.gitignore`)
- Temporary build artifacts

<Tip>
Always check the commit preview before pushing. If you see files that should not be versioned, add them to `.gitignore` or remove them from the workspace before pushing.
</Tip>

---

## Subsequent Pushes

After your initial push, you can continue to push updates as your project evolves:

1. Make changes in the Emergent workspace via chat or direct edits
2. Click **Push to GitHub** again
3. Select the same repository and branch (or a new branch for a feature)
4. Review the diff, add a commit message, and push

Each push creates a new commit in your GitHub repository, preserving the full history of your project.

---

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Emergent says I need to authorize GitHub">
Click the authorization link in the push dialog to connect your GitHub account. You'll be redirected to GitHub to grant Emergent access, then returned to the workspace to complete the push.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="I don't see my repository in the list">
Ensure the repository exists in your GitHub account and that Emergent has permission to access it. If you recently created the repo, refresh the repository list in the push dialog.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Push failed with a 'conflict' error">
Someone else may have pushed changes to the branch. Pull the latest changes in your local environment, resolve any conflicts, then push again from Emergent—or create a new feature branch for your changes.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="I accidentally pushed a secret—what now?">
**Immediately** revoke the exposed credential (API key, token, etc.) and replace it with a new one stored in Emergent's [secrets manager](/secrets-env-variables). Then remove the secret from your repository's commit history using `git filter-branch` or the BFG Repo-Cleaner, and force-push the cleaned history. Consider any data or services accessed by that credential as potentially compromised.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Next Steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Secrets & Env Variables" icon="lock" href="/secrets-env-variables">
Learn how to manage API keys and sensitive configuration securely
</Card>
<Card title="Custom Domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Deploy your app on a custom domain after pushing to GitHub
</Card>
</CardGroup>

debugging-testing-with-the-agent.title: Debugging & testing with the agent
debugging-testing-with-the-agent.content:
## Overview

When your app doesn't behave as expected, Emergent's agent can diagnose and fix issues directly in the chat. This guide shows you how to surface errors, provide context, and use the platform's built-in testing tools to ship a polished app.

<Note>
The agent works best when given complete error messages and clear reproduction steps. The more detail you provide, the faster it can iterate toward a fix.
</Note>

## Debugging with the agent

<Steps>
<Step title="Paste the full error message">
When your app throws an error, copy the **entire error text** from the console, logs, or error modal—including stack traces, file paths, and line numbers. Paste it directly into the chat with a short prompt:

```
please solve this error

[full error text here]
```

The agent will parse the stack trace, identify the failing component or API call, and propose a fix.

<Tip>
If the error occurs in the browser console, right-click the message and select "Copy" to capture the full output, including stack frames.
</Tip>
</Step>

<Step title="Upload a screenshot for UI bugs">
Visual issues—misaligned components, missing styles, incorrect colors—are often faster to diagnose from a screenshot. Upload an image (drag-and-drop or click the attachment icon) and add a brief description:

```
This modal is cut off on mobile (screenshot attached). The submit button is hidden below the fold.
```

The agent will inspect the component's layout constraints and suggest CSS or flex adjustments.
</Step>

<Step title="Provide context for stubborn bugs">
If a bug is intermittent or hard to reproduce, describe the conditions:

- **When** does it happen? (e.g., "only after logging in," "on the second page load")
- **Where** does it occur? (specific page, route, or user flow)
- **What** user action triggers it? (button click, form submission, navigation)

Example:

```
The "Add to Cart" button doesn't respond when I click it after navigating from the product list. It works fine if I reload the product detail page directly.
```

This helps the agent narrow down state-management issues, routing bugs, or missing event handlers.
</Step>

<Step title="Read automated test results">
After each build, the platform runs a suite of automated tests covering routes, API endpoints, and key user flows. Test results appear in the chat as a summary card. If tests fail, the agent will:

1. Show which test failed and why
2. Automatically attempt a fix
3. Re-run the tests to confirm the issue is resolved

You can also request specific tests:

```
test the checkout flow end-to-end
```

<Info>
Automated tests catch regressions early—especially useful when you're iterating quickly on features. Review the test output to understand what the agent validated.
</Info>
</Step>

<Step title="Request internal test builds for mobile apps">
Before publishing to the App Store or Play Store, generate an **internal test build** to validate the experience on real devices. In the chat, ask:

```
create an iOS test build
```

or

```
create an Android test build
```

The agent will produce a signed build (TestFlight for iOS, internal track for Android) and provide installation instructions. Share the build link with testers to gather feedback before your public launch.

<Tip>
Internal builds let you test on actual hardware, verify push notifications, and confirm in-app purchases—scenarios that are difficult to simulate in the workspace preview.
</Tip>

See [Publishing to the stores](/publishing-to-the-stores) for details on moving from test builds to production releases.
</Step>
</Steps>

## When to escalate

Most bugs can be resolved in chat with clear error messages and context. If an issue persists after several iterations:

- Check the [App slow, crashing or cold-starting](/app-slow-crashing-or-cold-starting) troubleshooting guide for performance-related problems
- Verify that third-party API keys and environment variables are correctly configured (see [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) for examples)
- Review the [Glossary of Emergent terms](/glossary-of-emergent-terms) to ensure you're using platform concepts correctly

<Warning>
If your app handles sensitive data, review [Your data & ownership](/your-data-ownership) to understand how logs and error traces are stored during debugging sessions.
</Warning>

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="The chat-to-deployment flow" icon="messages" href="/the-chat-to-deployment-flow">
Understand how the agent moves from your prompt to a live build
</Card>
<Card title="A tour of the workspace" icon="browser" href="/a-tour-of-the-workspace">
Explore the preview, logs, and file browser for deeper debugging
</Card>
</CardGroup>

cancellation-refunds.title: Cancellation & refunds
cancellation-refunds.content:
## Cancelling your subscription

You can cancel your Emergent subscription at any time through the web app, mobile app, or directly in the Stripe customer portal.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Cancel via web or mobile app">
    Navigate to **Settings** → **Billing** and select **Cancel subscription**. You'll be asked to confirm; once confirmed, your subscription moves to a cancelled state at the end of the current billing period.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Cancel via Stripe">
    If you subscribed through Stripe Checkout, you can also manage your subscription in the [Stripe customer portal](/stripe). Click **Manage billing** in Settings → Billing to open the portal, then choose **Cancel subscription**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
Cancellations take effect at the end of your current billing cycle. You retain full access and any remaining subscription credits until that date.
</Note>

## What happens to your credits

When you cancel, the treatment of your credits depends on how you acquired them:

| Credit type | What happens on cancellation |
|-------------|------------------------------|
| **Subscription credits** (monthly allowance) | Remain usable until the end of the current billing period, then expire. Any unused balance is forfeited. |
| **Top-up credits** (one-time purchases) | Persist indefinitely. You can continue using them on the Free plan after your subscription ends. See [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) for details. |

<Tip>
If you have unused top-up credits, consider downgrading to the Free plan instead of cancelling outright. You'll keep access to your apps and can spend those credits over time.
</Tip>

## What happens to your apps

All apps you've built remain **fully accessible and deployed** after cancellation. You can:

- View, test and share live URLs
- Export code or download assets
- Re-run builds using top-up credits (if you have any) or by resubscribing

<Warning title="New builds require credits">
Once subscription credits expire, you'll need top-up credits or an active plan to create new apps or request changes to existing ones. Read-only access is always free.
</Warning>

## Refund eligibility

Emergent offers **prorated refunds on subscription credits only**, subject to the conditions below.

### Subscription credits (prorated)

If you cancel within the first 7 days of a new billing cycle and have used fewer than 10% of that cycle's credit allowance, you're eligible for a prorated refund of the unused portion.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Request a refund">
    Email [support@emergent.build](mailto:support@emergent.build) with your account email and billing date. Include a brief reason (optional but helpful).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review & approval">
    The support team verifies usage and eligibility, typically within 1–2 business days.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Refund issued">
    Approved refunds are processed to your original payment method within 5–10 business days.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Top-up credits (non-refundable)

One-time credit top-ups are **final and non-refundable** once purchased. Because top-up credits never expire and can be used at any time, they are treated as a stored balance rather than a subscription service.

<Info>
Top-up credits remain in your account even if you downgrade or cancel. You can always return and spend them later.
</Info>

## Disputes and chargebacks

If you file a chargeback or payment dispute with your bank or card issuer **before contacting support**, your account will be automatically suspended to prevent fraud. To resolve:

1. **Contact support first** at [support@emergent.build](mailto:support@emergent.build). Most billing issues can be resolved quickly.
2. If a chargeback has already been filed, email us immediately with details. We'll work with you and the payment processor to close the dispute and restore access.

<Danger title="Chargeback consequences">
Accounts with unresolved chargebacks may be permanently closed and banned from future use of the platform.
</Danger>

## Retention offers

If you're cancelling due to cost, usage limits, or a missing feature, **let us know**. We occasionally offer:

- **Discounted plans** for students, educators, or non-profits
- **Extended trials** if you're evaluating the platform for a larger project
- **Custom credit packages** for teams with specific usage patterns

Reach out to [support@emergent.build](mailto:support@emergent.build) before cancelling. We'll do our best to find a solution that works for you.

---

For more on how credits are allocated and consumed, see [How credits work](/how-credits-work). For billing management and invoices, see [Stripe](/stripe).

emergent-auth-built-in.title: Emergent Auth (built-in)
emergent-auth-built-in.content:
## What is Emergent Auth?

Emergent Auth is the platform's built-in authentication and user-management system. Every app created on Emergent automatically includes authentication capabilities—no third-party service or complex configuration required.

When you describe user sign-up, login, or access control in your chat prompt, the AI agents wire up Emergent Auth behind the scenes. User credentials, sessions, and profile data are stored securely within your app's environment.

<Note>
Emergent Auth is included at no additional cost. You don't need API keys, OAuth apps, or separate billing for auth providers.
</Note>

## How it works

Emergent Auth provides:

- **Email/password authentication** — users sign up and log in with an email and password.
- **Session management** — sessions are maintained server-side; tokens are stored in secure HTTP-only cookies.
- **Password reset flows** — automated email-based password recovery (outbound email is handled by the platform).
- **User profiles** — a `User` collection is created in your app's database, storing email, hashed password, and any custom fields you define.

The underlying user data lives in your app's [MongoDB database](/database-mongodb), so you can query and extend it just like any other collection.

## Typical usage in prompts

You interact with authentication by describing what you want in natural language. For example:

- *"Users should be able to sign up with email and password, then log in to see their dashboard."*
- *"Add a login page. Only logged-in users can create posts."*
- *"Let users reset their password if they forget it."*

The agents will generate login and sign-up UI, wire up backend endpoints, enforce route protection, and handle sessions—all using Emergent Auth.

## Route protection and access control

Once authentication is enabled, you can specify which pages or API endpoints require a logged-in user:

- *"Make the `/admin` page require login."*
- *"Only the post author can edit or delete their own post."*

The platform enforces these rules at the routing layer. Unauthenticated users are redirected to the login page; unauthorized actions return an error.

<Tip>
You can also define role-based access by adding a `role` field to the `User` collection (e.g., `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`) and instructing the agents to check it.
</Tip>

## Session and token storage

Sessions are stateful and backed by a session store tied to your app's database. Authentication tokens are:

- Stored in **HTTP-only cookies** (not accessible to client JavaScript, reducing XSS risk).
- **Signed and encrypted** by the platform runtime.
- Valid for a configurable duration (default is typically 7–30 days; the agents set a sensible default or you can request a specific expiry).

<Info>
Emergent Auth does **not** use JWTs in client-side `localStorage`. All session state lives server-side for enhanced security.
</Info>

## User data and the User collection

When you enable authentication, a `User` collection is created in your app's MongoDB database. At minimum, each document includes:

- `email` (string, unique)
- `password` (hashed with bcrypt or Argon2)
- `createdAt` and `updatedAt` timestamps

You can extend the schema with additional fields:

- *"Add a `displayName` field to the User model."*
- *"Store user profile picture URLs in the User collection."*

Because `User` is a standard MongoDB collection, you can query it, index it, and relate it to other collections (e.g., linking `Post.author` to `User._id`).

## Password reset and email

Password-reset flows are handled automatically when you request them:

1. User clicks "Forgot password?" and enters their email.
2. The platform sends a time-limited reset link to that email.
3. User clicks the link, sets a new password, and is redirected to login.

Outbound emails are delivered via the platform's internal mail service—no SendGrid or Postmark integration required (though you can customize the "from" address and branding by describing it in chat).

<Warning>
Ensure your app has a valid custom domain configured if you want password-reset emails to link back to `yourdomain.com` rather than the default Emergent subdomain. See [Custom domain](/custom-domain) for setup.
</Warning>

## OAuth and social login (future)

Currently, Emergent Auth supports email/password authentication. Social login providers (Google, GitHub, etc.) are on the roadmap. If you need OAuth today, you can ask the agents to integrate a third-party service like Auth0 or Clerk, though that will require API keys and separate billing.

## Security best practices

Emergent Auth follows industry-standard security practices out of the box:

- Passwords are **never stored in plaintext**; they are hashed using bcrypt or Argon2.
- Sessions use **secure, HTTP-only cookies** with `SameSite` and `Secure` flags in production.
- Rate limiting is applied to login and sign-up endpoints to mitigate brute-force attacks.
- HTTPS is enforced for all production apps.

<Tip>
If your app handles sensitive data (health, finance, etc.), describe additional requirements in your prompt—e.g., *"Require two-factor authentication"* or *"Log all login attempts."* The agents will implement these features.
</Tip>

## Switching to a third-party auth provider

If you later decide to migrate to an external provider (e.g., Clerk, Supabase Auth, Auth0), you can instruct the agents to refactor your app:

- *"Replace Emergent Auth with Clerk for authentication."*

The agents will update routes, remove the built-in session logic, and integrate the new provider's SDK. User data migration may require additional steps depending on the provider.

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Database (MongoDB)" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
    Learn how user data is stored and queried in your app's MongoDB instance.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Custom domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
    Configure a custom domain so password-reset emails link to your branded URL.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

referrals-partners-program.title: Referrals & Partners program
referrals-partners-program.content:
## Overview

Emergent rewards you for bringing new users to the platform and offers partnership opportunities for content creators and communities. Three programs are available depending on your plan and audience size:

- **Referral program** — earn credits when friends sign up and become paid users
- **Partners program** — earn 20% recurring cash commissions on subscriptions
- **Secret Perks** — exclusive Pro-only benefits and early access

<Note title="Paid users only">
All referral and partner benefits require an active paid Emergent plan (Indie, Startup or Pro). Free-tier users cannot earn referral credits or partner commissions.
</Note>

---

## Referral program

Share your unique referral link with friends and colleagues. When a referee signs up, verifies their email and upgrades to any paid plan, you both receive credits.

### How it works

<Steps>
<Step title="Find your referral link">
Navigate to **Settings → Referrals** in the Emergent workspace. Copy your unique link.
</Step>

<Step title="Share your link">
Send the link to friends, post it in your community or share on social media.
</Step>

<Step title="Earn credits when they upgrade">
When a referee signs up via your link and purchases a paid plan, you receive **50 credits** and they receive **5 bonus credits**.
</Step>
</Steps>

### Eligibility & limits

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Referrer** | Must have an active paid plan (Indie, Startup or Pro) |
| **Referee** | Must be a new user who has not previously held a paid plan |
| **Credit award** | 50 credits to referrer, 5 credits to referee |
| **Monthly cap** | Referral credits are capped per billing period (cap varies by plan tier) |
| **Expiry** | Referral credits follow the same expiry rules as plan credits — see [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) |

<Warning title="Fraudulent referrals">
Self-referrals, duplicate accounts and coordinated sign-ups to farm credits violate the terms of service and will result in account suspension and forfeiture of all referral credits.
</Warning>

Referral credits appear in your workspace balance within minutes of the referee's first paid subscription charge.

---

## Partners program

The **Partners program** is designed for content creators, educators, community leaders and agencies who can drive meaningful adoption of Emergent. Partners earn **20% recurring cash commissions** (paid via Wise) on every subscription referred.

### Who should apply

- YouTube creators, bloggers or podcasters covering AI, no-code or SaaS development
- Course instructors teaching app building or prompt engineering
- Communities, Slack/Discord groups or forums with engaged developer audiences
- Agencies and consultancies recommending Emergent to clients

### Benefits

| Benefit | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **20% recurring commission** | Earn 20% of every subscription payment (monthly or annual) for as long as the user remains a paid customer |
| **Cash payouts via Wise** | Commissions are paid in USD, EUR, GBP or other currencies supported by Wise |
| **Custom tracking links** | Unique partner links and dashboard to monitor sign-ups, conversions and earnings |
| **Marketing assets** | Access to logos, screenshots, demo videos and co-marketing support |
| **Priority support** | Dedicated partner success contact for technical questions and joint campaigns |

### How to apply

<Steps>
<Step title="Upgrade to a paid plan">
You must hold an active Indie, Startup or Pro subscription to qualify.
</Step>

<Step title="Submit your application">
Email [partners@emergent.ai](mailto:partners@emergent.ai) with:
- Your name and Emergent account email
- Links to your audience platform (YouTube channel, blog, community, etc.)
- Monthly reach or audience size estimate
- A brief pitch: how you plan to promote Emergent
</Step>

<Step title="Review and onboarding">
The Emergent team reviews applications within 3–5 business days. Approved partners receive a welcome email with tracking links, payment setup instructions and marketing assets.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Info title="Approval criteria">
The Partners program is selective. Emergent prioritizes applicants with engaged, relevant audiences and a genuine alignment with the platform's mission. Approval is not guaranteed.
</Info>

---

## Secret Perks (Pro plan only)

**Secret Perks** is an exclusive benefit tier for Pro subscribers, offering early access to experimental features, priority bug fixes and surprise bonuses.

### What's included

- **Early access** to beta features before they reach Indie and Startup users
- **Priority support** tickets (responses within 4 hours during business hours)
- **Sneak peeks** of upcoming AI models, deployment targets and integrations
- **Occasional credit bonuses** during promotional periods or product milestones
- **Input on roadmap** via quarterly Pro-user surveys and feedback sessions

<Tip title="Perks evolve over time">
Secret Perks change periodically as new features ship and priorities shift. Pro users receive email updates whenever new perks are added.
</Tip>

Secret Perks are automatic for all Pro subscribers — no application or separate opt-in required.

---

## Frequently asked questions

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Can I use referral credits and partner commissions together?">
Yes. Referral credits apply to friends and colleagues you introduce casually; partner commissions apply to users acquired through your marketing efforts. The programs can run in parallel as long as you meet the eligibility requirements for each.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Do referral credits stack with plan credits?">
Referral credits are added to your workspace balance and consumed alongside plan credits. They follow the same expiry and recharge rules — see [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) for details.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens to my partner commissions if I downgrade or cancel?">
Partner commissions already earned remain payable. However, you cannot generate new referrals or receive new commissions unless you reactivate a paid plan.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Are there geographic restrictions?">
Referral credits are available worldwide. Partner cash payouts require a supported Wise account — most countries are eligible, but sanctions and banking regulations may restrict availability in certain regions.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I become a partner if I only have a small audience?">
Partner applications are evaluated on quality and relevance, not size alone. A highly engaged niche community or a well-written blog may be approved even with modest reach. Focus your application on how you plan to deliver value to your audience.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Getting started

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Referrals dashboard" icon="link" href="/settings/referrals">
Copy your referral link and track sign-ups in real time
</Card>

<Card title="Apply for Partners" icon="handshake" href="mailto:partners@emergent.ai">
Submit your application to join the Partners program
</Card>

<Card title="Plans & pricing" icon="credit-card" href="/plans">
Review plan tiers and upgrade to unlock referral and partner benefits
</Card>

<Card title="Credit expiry rules" icon="clock" href="/credit-expiry-recharging">
Understand how referral credits expire and recharge
</Card>
</CardGroup>
