paddle.title: Paddle
paddle.content:
## Overview

Paddle is a merchant of record payment platform that handles subscription billing, sales tax compliance, and global payments infrastructure. Integrating Paddle with your Emergent app enables you to accept payments, manage subscriptions, and handle customer billing without building your own payment infrastructure.

This guide walks you through connecting Paddle to your Emergent application using environment variables and the Paddle SDK.

<Note>
Paddle acts as the merchant of record, meaning they handle all payment processing, tax calculation, and compliance requirements on your behalf.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- A Paddle account (sign up at [paddle.com](https://paddle.com))
- Access to your Paddle dashboard
- Your Paddle API credentials (Vendor ID and API Key)
- An Emergent app where you want to accept payments

## Getting Your Paddle Credentials

<Steps>
<Step title="Log in to your Paddle dashboard">
Navigate to [vendors.paddle.com](https://vendors.paddle.com) and sign in to your account.
</Step>

<Step title="Locate your Vendor ID">
Your Vendor ID is displayed in the top-right corner of the dashboard. It's a numeric identifier unique to your account.
</Step>

<Step title="Generate an API Key">
Go to **Developer Tools → Authentication** in the sidebar, then click **Generate Key**. Store this key securely — it won't be shown again.

<Warning>
Treat your API Key like a password. Never commit it to version control or expose it in client-side code.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Configure webhook secrets (optional)">
If you plan to receive webhook events from Paddle (for subscription updates, payment confirmations, etc.), generate a webhook secret under **Developer Tools → Notifications**. Save this for later configuration.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Adding Paddle to Your Emergent App

<Steps>
<Step title="Set environment variables">
In your Emergent app's chat interface, tell the AI to add the following environment variables:

```
PADDLE_VENDOR_ID=your_vendor_id
PADDLE_API_KEY=your_api_key
PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=your_webhook_secret
```

Replace the placeholder values with your actual Paddle credentials. The AI will securely store these in your app's environment.
</Step>

<Step title="Install the Paddle SDK">
Ask the AI to install the appropriate Paddle SDK for your app's stack:

<CodeGroup>
```bash Node.js
npm install @paddle/paddle-node-sdk
```

```bash Python
pip install paddle-billing
```

```bash PHP
composer require paddle/paddle-php-sdk
```
</CodeGroup>
</Step>

<Step title="Initialize the Paddle client">
Describe to the AI how you want to use Paddle. For example:

> "Create a Paddle client using the environment variables. I want to be able to create checkout sessions and handle webhook events for subscription updates."

The AI will generate the necessary initialization code and integration logic.
</Step>

<Step title="Test the integration">
Ask the AI to create a test checkout flow. Paddle provides a sandbox environment for testing without processing real payments. Tell the AI:

> "Create a test payment page that uses Paddle's sandbox mode. Add a button to initiate a checkout for a $10 monthly subscription."
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common Use Cases

<Tabs>
<Tab title="One-time Payments">
For single purchases, create a checkout session with a one-time product:

- Define your product in the Paddle dashboard
- Create a checkout link or overlay using the Product ID
- Handle the `payment.succeeded` webhook to fulfill the order
</Tab>

<Tab title="Subscriptions">
For recurring billing:

- Set up a subscription plan in Paddle with your desired billing interval
- Create checkout sessions that reference the plan
- Listen for `subscription.created`, `subscription.updated`, and `subscription.canceled` webhooks
- Update user access based on subscription status
</Tab>

<Tab title="Usage-based Billing">
For metered usage:

- Create a usage-based pricing plan in Paddle
- Report usage events via the API as customers consume resources
- Paddle automatically calculates charges based on reported usage
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Handling Webhooks

Paddle sends webhook events to notify your app of payment and subscription changes. Configure a webhook endpoint in your app to receive these events.

<Steps>
<Step title="Create a webhook route">
Ask the AI to create an endpoint that receives POST requests from Paddle:

> "Create a `/webhooks/paddle` endpoint that verifies the webhook signature using `PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and processes incoming events."
</Step>

<Step title="Add the webhook URL in Paddle">
In your Paddle dashboard, go to **Developer Tools → Notifications** and add your webhook URL:

```
https://your-app.emergent.build/webhooks/paddle
```

<Info>
If you're using a [custom domain](/custom-domain), use that domain in your webhook URL instead.
</Info>
</Step>

<Step title="Handle key events">
Tell the AI which events matter for your business logic. Common events include:

- `payment.succeeded` — Payment completed successfully
- `subscription.created` — New subscription started
- `subscription.updated` — Subscription changed (plan upgrade/downgrade)
- `subscription.canceled` — Subscription ended
- `transaction.completed` — Transaction finalized
</Step>
</Steps>

## Testing Your Integration

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="How do I test without real payments?">
Paddle provides a sandbox environment for testing. In your Paddle dashboard, toggle to **Sandbox** mode in the top navigation. Use sandbox credentials in your `PADDLE_VENDOR_ID` and `PADDLE_API_KEY` environment variables during development.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I simulate different payment scenarios?">
In sandbox mode, Paddle provides test card numbers that simulate various outcomes (successful payments, declined cards, 3D Secure challenges, etc.). Check Paddle's documentation for the full list of test credentials.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I verify webhooks are working?">
Use the **Event Log** in your Paddle dashboard to see all webhook deliveries. You can also manually resend events to test your endpoint's handling logic.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Going Live

When you're ready to accept real payments:

<Steps>
<Step title="Complete Paddle's verification process">
Submit your business details and complete any required verification steps in the Paddle dashboard.
</Step>

<Step title="Switch to production credentials">
Update your environment variables with your production Vendor ID and API Key (not the sandbox credentials).
</Step>

<Step title="Update webhook URLs">
Ensure your webhook endpoint is configured with your production domain and is publicly accessible.
</Step>

<Step title="Test a real transaction">
Process a small test payment using a real card to confirm everything works end-to-end.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Troubleshooting

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Checkout not loading" icon="circle-exclamation">
Verify your `PADDLE_VENDOR_ID` is correct and matches the environment (sandbox vs. production) you're using.
</Card>

<Card title="Webhooks not received" icon="webhook">
Check that your webhook URL is publicly accessible and that the signature verification is using the correct `PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
</Card>

<Card title="API authentication errors" icon="key">
Confirm your `PADDLE_API_KEY` is valid and hasn't been regenerated. API keys are environment-specific (sandbox keys don't work in production).
</Card>

<Card title="Tax calculation issues" icon="receipt">
Ensure customer location data is being passed correctly to Paddle. Paddle requires accurate location info for sales tax compliance.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Next Steps

- Explore Paddle's customer portal for self-service subscription management
- Set up email receipts and invoices in your Paddle dashboard
- Implement plan upgrades and downgrades
- Add promo codes and discounts for marketing campaigns

<Tip>
You can describe any payment flow to the Emergent AI in plain English, and it will generate the necessary Paddle integration code. For example: "Add a pricing page with three subscription tiers and handle upgrades between them."
</Tip>

account-security-login.title: Account security & login
account-security-login.content:
## Sign-in methods

Emergent supports five authentication methods to fit your workflow:

- **Email + password** – traditional username/password sign-in.
- **Google OAuth** – fast login with your Google account (see [Google auth](/google-auth) for configuration).
- **Apple OAuth** – secure sign-in with Apple ID.
- **Phone OTP** – SMS one-time passcode authentication (carrier rates apply).
- **SSO** – SAML or OpenID Connect for enterprise teams (Pro/Enterprise plans).

You can link multiple providers to the same Emergent account by signing in with each method while already authenticated. Once linked, any method grants access to your workspace.

<Tip title="Switching providers">
If you signed up with email but want to use Google going forward, sign in with your email, then visit **Settings → Account → Connected accounts** and authorize Google. Both methods will then unlock the same workspace.
</Tip>

## Resetting your password

<Steps>
<Step title="Navigate to the sign-in screen">
Click **Sign In** from the Emergent homepage.
</Step>

<Step title="Request a reset link">
Select **Forgot password?** below the email field. Enter your email address and submit.
</Step>

<Step title="Check your inbox">
You'll receive a password-reset email within a few minutes (check spam if it doesn't arrive). The link expires after **24 hours**.
</Step>

<Step title="Set a new password">
Click the link, enter a new password (minimum 8 characters), and confirm. You'll be signed in automatically.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
Password reset is only available for accounts that signed up with **email + password**. OAuth accounts (Google, Apple) inherit security from the identity provider and do not have Emergent passwords.
</Note>

## Changing your email address

**Email addresses cannot be changed once an account is created.** This immutability ensures audit integrity, billing consistency, and prevents accidental email collisions in team workspaces.

### Workaround: GitHub migration

If you must switch to a new email:

1. Export any critical projects or data you want to preserve.
2. Create a new Emergent account with the desired email address.
3. Transfer projects manually by cloning repositories or re-importing app definitions.

<Warning title="Team seats and billing">
Deleting your old account and re-joining a team will consume a new seat. Contact [support@emergent.dev](mailto:support@emergent.dev) if you need help coordinating a migration with minimal disruption.
</Warning>

## Deleting your account

Account deletion is irreversible but includes a **45-day grace period** during which your account is soft-deleted and can be restored.

<Steps>
<Step title="Navigate to account settings">
Click your avatar → **Settings → Account**.
</Step>

<Step title="Request deletion">
Scroll to **Danger zone** and select **Delete account**. Confirm your password (or re-authenticate via OAuth).
</Step>

<Step title="Grace period begins">
Your account is immediately deactivated. All apps, projects, and data are hidden but retained for **45 days**.
</Step>

<Step title="Restore or purge">
During the grace period you can sign in to restore your account with one click. After 45 days all data is permanently purged and cannot be recovered.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Danger title="Permanent data loss">
After the 45-day grace period, deletion is final. Export any critical projects, code, or databases **before** initiating deletion. See [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) for export instructions.
</Danger>

### What happens to team workspaces?

- If you are the **sole owner**, the workspace is also soft-deleted. Transfer ownership to another member before deletion to preserve team resources.
- If you are a **member**, you are simply removed. The workspace and its apps remain unaffected.

## Session and token security

Emergent uses industry-standard session management to protect your account:

| Feature | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **Session duration** | 30 days of inactivity before auto-logout |
| **Token storage** | Secure HTTP-only cookies; tokens are never exposed to client JavaScript |
| **Token rotation** | Refresh tokens rotate on every use; stolen tokens expire within minutes |
| **Device tracking** | Active sessions are listed in **Settings → Security** with IP, browser, and last-seen timestamp |
| **Remote logout** | Revoke any session remotely (useful if you left a device signed in) |

<Info>
Emergent does **not** store plaintext passwords. All credentials are hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12) and OAuth providers never share passwords with our platform.
</Info>

### Revoking sessions

<Steps>
<Step title="Open security settings">
Click your avatar → **Settings → Security → Active sessions**.
</Step>

<Step title="Review devices">
Each row shows a device fingerprint, browser, IP address, and last activity timestamp.
</Step>

<Step title="Revoke unwanted sessions">
Click **Revoke** next to any session you don't recognize or no longer use. That device will be logged out immediately.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Sign out everywhere">
If you suspect unauthorized access, use **Sign out all other sessions** at the top of the list to invalidate every session except your current one. Change your password immediately afterward.
</Tip>

## Best practices

- **Enable two-factor authentication** (2FA) if your OAuth provider supports it (Google, Apple both do). Emergent inherits 2FA from the identity provider.
- **Review active sessions monthly**, especially if you use shared or public computers.
- **Use a password manager** for strong, unique passwords on email-based accounts.
- **Link multiple sign-in methods** so you have a backup if one provider is unavailable.

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Can I require 2FA for my entire team workspace?">
Yes, on **Enterprise plans**. Contact [sales@emergent.dev](mailto:sales@emergent.dev) to enable organization-wide 2FA enforcement. Members without 2FA will be prompted to configure it on their next sign-in.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens if I lose access to my OAuth provider?">
If you've linked multiple sign-in methods, use an alternate provider. If OAuth is your only method and you lose access, contact [support@emergent.dev](mailto:support@emergent.dev) with proof of ownership (billing receipts, project metadata) to regain access.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Are API tokens covered by the same security policies?">
Yes. Personal access tokens (PATs) for the Emergent API follow the same rotation and expiry rules. Review and rotate tokens in **Settings → Developer → API tokens**. Tokens are scoped to specific permissions and can be revoked individually. See [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) for more on API security.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
account-security-login.description: Sign-in methods (email/Google/Apple/phone-OTP/SSO), password reset, why email can't be changed (+ GitHub workaround), account deletion with 45-day grace, and session/token security

payment-methods-regional-billing.title: Payment methods & regional billing
payment-methods-regional-billing.content:
## Overview

Emergent routes your credit purchase through the payment processor best suited to your country and currency. We support **Stripe**, **Razorpay**, **PagBrasil**, **Paddle**, and **RevenueCat** depending on where you are and how you pay.

Credit prices vary by currency to reflect local purchasing power and payment-processing costs. We do **not** store card details on our servers—all tokenization and secure storage happens at the processor.

---

## Supported payment processors

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Stripe" icon="credit-card" href="/stripe">
    Global coverage, cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, bank transfers in 40+ countries.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Razorpay" icon="building-columns" href="/razorpay">
    India-specific: UPI, Netbanking, cards, wallets. INR-optimized.
  </Card>
  <Card title="PagBrasil" icon="landmark">
    Brazil: Pix, boleto, local cards. BRL transactions.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Paddle" icon="globe">
    Merchant-of-record model; handles VAT/sales tax automatically.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

When you click **Buy Credits**, Emergent chooses the processor based on:

- **Your IP geolocation** and browser locale.
- **Your selected currency** (USD, INR, BRL, KRW, EUR, GBP).
- **Regulatory fit**—some processors are better licensed for certain regions.

<Note>
You cannot manually pick a processor. The platform selects the optimal route to minimize fees and maximize payment-method availability.
</Note>

---

## Currency-specific credit rates

Credit prices differ by currency. The table below shows the **indicative rate** for **1,000 credits**; actual bundles may offer volume discounts.

| Currency | ~1,000 credits | Notes |
|----------|----------------|-------|
| **USD** | ~$10 | Default global rate |
| **INR** | ~₹750 | Razorpay, lower per-credit cost |
| **BRL** | ~R$50 | PagBrasil, accounts for Pix fees |
| **KRW** | ~₩12,000 | Stripe Korea, card/bank transfer |
| **EUR** | ~€9 | Stripe/Paddle, VAT added at checkout |
| **GBP** | ~£8 | Stripe UK, VAT included |

<Warning>
Rates are illustrative. The workspace **Buy Credits** page shows the live, region-locked price including any taxes or payment-gateway surcharges.
</Warning>

See [How credits work](/how-credits-work) and [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) for usage mechanics.

---

## How payment routing works

<Steps>
  <Step title="You click Buy Credits">
    The platform reads your IP, browser `Accept-Language`, and any previously used currency preference.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Currency & processor are selected">
    Emergent picks the processor with the lowest combined fee + best local method support for your region.
  </Step>
  <Step title="You complete payment">
    You are redirected to the processor's hosted checkout (Stripe, Razorpay, etc.). Card details never touch our servers.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Credits land in your workspace">
    On successful webhook confirmation, credits appear within seconds. If the webhook is delayed, credits may take up to 5 minutes.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
If you travel or use a VPN, the platform may offer a different processor/currency. You can manually switch currency in the checkout selector if multiple options are available.
</Tip>

---

## Legal entity names on your statement

Depending on the processor, your bank or credit-card statement will show one of these:

| Processor | Statement descriptor |
|-----------|----------------------|
| **Stripe** | `EMERGENT AI` or `EMERGENT.AI` |
| **Razorpay** | `EMERGENT INDIA` or `RAZORPAY*EMERGENT` |
| **PagBrasil** | `PAGBRASIL*EMERGENT` |
| **Paddle** | `PADDLE.NET*EMERGENT` |
| **RevenueCat** | `REVENUECAT*EMERGENT` (mobile IAP receipts) |

<Note>
Paddle acts as **merchant of record**, so the legal invoice entity is Paddle.com Market Ltd. (UK) or Paddle.com Inc. (US). VAT/sales tax is calculated and remitted by Paddle.
</Note>

---

## No stored cards

Emergent **does not store** your card number, CVV, or full PAN. When you pay:

1. The processor (Stripe, Razorpay, etc.) tokenizes your card and returns a non-sensitive token.
2. We store only the token, last four digits, brand (Visa/Mastercard), and expiry—for display purposes.
3. Subsequent purchases use the same token; you can delete saved methods in **Settings → Billing**.

<Info>
If you delete a saved payment method, you will be prompted to re-enter card details on your next purchase. No billing happens without your explicit "Buy" click.
</Info>

---

## Cryptocurrency & stablecoins

We accept **USDC** (on Ethereum, Polygon, and Solana) and **USDT** (Ethereum, Tron) through a **Coinbase Commerce** integration. When you select crypto:

- You are given a time-limited wallet address and exact amount.
- Credits are added **after 1 on-chain confirmation** (typically < 5 min for Polygon/Solana, ~15 min for Ethereum).
- The exchange rate is locked for **15 minutes**; if you send after expiry, contact support for manual reconciliation.

<Warning title="Testnet tokens are not accepted">
Only send mainnet stablecoins. Sending test USDC or tokens on the wrong chain will result in **permanent loss**—we cannot recover cross-chain sends.
</Warning>

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Why does the crypto price differ from card price?">
    Crypto checkout includes a **~2% processor fee** and a **volatility buffer** for stablecoin de-pegging risk. The final credit count is guaranteed once you send.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can I pay in Bitcoin or Ethereum?">
    Not currently. We accept only **USDC** and **USDT** to avoid slippage and ensure instant fiat conversion.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Do I get an invoice for crypto payments?">
    Yes. An invoice PDF is emailed within 24 hours. For tax purposes, the invoice shows the USD-equivalent value at the time of payment.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Refunds & chargebacks

Emergent credits are **non-refundable** once delivered, except:

- **Duplicate charge** due to a processor error.
- **Unauthorized transaction** (you must file a support ticket within 48 hours).
- **Service outage** preventing credit usage for > 72 hours (pro-rata credit restoration).

<Danger title="Chargebacks freeze your workspace">
Initiating a chargeback before contacting support will **immediately suspend** your workspace and all running apps until the dispute is resolved. Chargeback fees may be passed through.
</Danger>

If you believe you were overcharged, email **billing@emergent.ai** with your transaction ID before disputing with your bank.

---

## VAT, GST & sales tax

- **India (GST)**: 18% GST is added at checkout for Razorpay transactions if you do not provide a valid GSTIN.
- **EU (VAT)**: Stripe and Paddle add VAT (15–27%) based on your IP; business customers can reverse-charge by entering a valid VAT ID.
- **US sales tax**: Applied in states where Emergent has nexus (currently CA, NY, TX, WA). Paddle handles remittance.
- **Brazil (ISS/PIS/COFINS)**: Included in the BRL rate; no separate line item.

<Info>
If you need a VAT invoice with your company details, add your VAT ID in **Settings → Billing → Tax Information** before purchase. Invoices are regenerated automatically.
</Info>

---

## Changing your default currency

1. Go to **Settings → Billing → Payment Methods**.
2. Click **Change Currency**.
3. Select your preferred currency from the dropdown.
4. The next credit purchase will use that currency and route to the corresponding processor.

<Note>
Changing currency does **not** convert existing credit balances. Credits purchased in INR remain denominated in INR; future purchases in USD will appear as a separate balance.
</Note>

---

## Multi-currency credit balances

If you purchase credits in **multiple currencies** (e.g., USD and INR), your workspace will show separate balances:

- **1,250 credits (USD)** – used first for new app runs.
- **800 credits (INR)** – used after USD balance is exhausted.

The platform **spends the oldest credits first** (FIFO) to minimize expiry waste. See [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) for expiry rules.

---

## Common issues

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Payment succeeded but credits didn't arrive">
    Webhook delays can take up to 5 minutes. Check **Settings → Billing → Transaction History**. If the status is "Pending," wait. If "Failed," contact support with the transaction ID.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Card declined — what should I do?">
    Common causes: insufficient funds, 3DS challenge not completed, card not enabled for international transactions, or anti-fraud block. Try a different card or payment method (UPI, bank transfer).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can I use a prepaid or virtual card?">
    Yes, as long as the card supports recurring merchant authorizations. Some VCCs block tokenization—test with a small purchase first.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="My company requires purchase orders (PO). Can I pay by invoice?">
    Yes, for **annual Enterprise plans** (minimum $10,000/year). Email **sales@emergent.ai** with your PO, and we will issue a NET-30 invoice. Pay-as-you-go credit purchases do not support invoicing.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="How credits work" icon="coins" href="/how-credits-work">
    Understand credit consumption, metering, and rate limits.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Credit expiry & recharging" icon="clock" href="/credit-expiry-recharging">
    Expiry rules, auto-recharge, and low-balance alerts.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

pre-publish-health-check.title: Pre-publish health check
pre-publish-health-check.content:
## Why run a pre-publish health check?

Before you commit to a production build or submit your mobile app to the App Store or Google Play, it's critical to verify that the app behaves as expected on real devices. A pre-publish health check catches UI glitches, navigation issues, API errors, and performance problems **before** they reach your users—saving you time, EAS build credits, and embarrassment.

Emergent generates a live preview URL for every mobile app. Use it to test thoroughly before you trigger a production build or start the [publishing to the stores](/publishing-to-the-stores) process.

---

## Preview & test the mobile app first

<Info title="Test early, test often">
Your workspace provides an instant preview of the mobile app. Open it on your phone to check layout, navigation, and features—all without burning a build credit or waiting for a compile.
</Info>

Every time the AI agents rebuild your mobile app, Emergent updates the preview. You can:

- Open the preview URL in your browser (desktop or mobile) to see a web-based simulation.
- Scan the QR code with your phone to launch the live app in Expo Go (see below).
- Navigate through every screen, tap buttons, fill forms, and verify API calls.

**What to check:**

- UI renders correctly on both iOS and Android (test on at least one device from each platform if possible).
- Navigation flows work end-to-end (tab bars, drawer menus, deep links).
- Forms validate input and display error messages.
- Images, fonts, and icons load.
- API calls succeed (check network panel or logs if something breaks).
- Push notifications, authentication flows, or third-party SDKs behave as expected.

If you spot a bug, describe it in chat—Emergent's agents will fix the code and regenerate the preview. Repeat until the app is solid.

---

## Local testing & testing on your phone with Expo Go

The fastest way to test your mobile app on a real device is with **Expo Go**, a free companion app that runs Expo projects instantly—no Xcode, no Android Studio, no builds.

<Steps>
<Step title="Install Expo Go on your phone">
Download **Expo Go** from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/expo-go/id982107779) (iOS) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=host.exp.exponent) (Android). It's free and maintained by Expo.
</Step>

<Step title="Open the preview in your workspace">
In the Emergent workspace, locate the mobile app preview panel. You'll see a QR code and a preview URL. See [a tour of the workspace](/a-tour-of-the-workspace) if you need help finding it.
</Step>

<Step title="Scan the QR code">
- **iOS**: Open the Camera app and point it at the QR code. Tap the notification banner that appears.
- **Android**: Open Expo Go and tap **Scan QR Code**, then point your camera at the code.

The app will load and run directly on your device, connected to Emergent's live preview server.
</Step>

<Step title="Iterate and re-test">
Make changes in chat, wait for the agents to rebuild, and the app in Expo Go will **hot-reload automatically**—usually within seconds. You can iterate quickly without leaving your phone.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Use Expo Go for all pre-publish testing">
Expo Go gives you a production-like experience on real hardware. Test gestures, animations, keyboard behavior, and camera/location permissions. Only move to a full EAS build once the app is stable.
</Tip>

<Warning title="Expo Go limitations">
Expo Go cannot run apps with custom native code (e.g., certain third-party SDKs or native modules outside the Expo SDK). If your app uses such features, you'll need a development build or a production build via EAS. Most Emergent apps work fine in Expo Go.
</Warning>

---

## EAS price & plan comparison

When you're ready to generate a production build—either for local testing, TestFlight/internal testing, or store submission—you'll use **Expo Application Services (EAS Build)**. EAS is Expo's cloud build infrastructure; Emergent integrates with it to compile your app in the background.

<Note title="Separate from Emergent plans">
EAS pricing is set by Expo, not Emergent. You'll need an Expo account and an EAS subscription (or free tier credits) to trigger builds. See [plans & the free tier](/plans-the-free-tier) for how Emergent's own pricing works.
</Note>

### EAS Build pricing tiers (as of 2024)

The table below compares Expo's EAS Build plans. Visit [expo.dev/pricing](https://expo.dev/pricing) for the latest official pricing.

| Feature | **Free** | **Production** | **Enterprise** |
|---------|----------|----------------|----------------|
| **Price** | $0/month | ~$99/month (per-seat or team pricing) | Custom |
| **Builds per month** | Limited credits (~15–30 depending on platform) | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Concurrency** | 1 build at a time | Higher (2–4+ concurrent) | Custom |
| **Build timeout** | Standard | Extended | Custom |
| **Priority queue** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Support** | Community | Email/chat | Dedicated |
| **Best for** | Prototyping, personal projects, early testing | Production apps, frequent releases | Large teams, compliance, SLA requirements |

**Notes:**

- The **Free** tier gives you enough credits to test the build process and generate a few production APKs/IPAs. Perfect for validating your app before committing to a paid plan.
- **Production** tier is billed per seat or team; check Expo's pricing page for exact numbers (prices vary by region and team size).
- **Enterprise** includes on-premise build workers, audit logs, SSO, and custom SLAs—contact Expo's sales team.

<Tip title="Start with the free tier">
If you're pre-publishing for the first time, use EAS Free to generate a test build. Once you're confident the app is ready and you need frequent builds (e.g., for beta testing or App Store submission), upgrade to Production.
</Tip>

### How builds are triggered in Emergent

When you ask Emergent to "build the mobile app for iOS" or "create an Android APK," the platform:

1. Commits the latest code to your project repository.
2. Runs `eas build` via the EAS CLI, authenticated with your Expo account.
3. Queues the build on Expo's servers (subject to your EAS plan's concurrency and priority).
4. Returns the build URL and artifact (APK or IPA) once complete.

You'll be prompted to connect your Expo account the first time you request a build. See [your first build (walkthrough)](/your-first-build-walkthrough) for step-by-step instructions.

---

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Publishing to the stores" icon="store" href="/publishing-to-the-stores">
Once your app passes the health check, learn how to submit it to the App Store and Google Play.
</Card>

<Card title="App slow, crashing or cold-starting" icon="gauge" href="/app-slow-crashing-or-cold-starting">
Troubleshoot performance issues before you publish.
</Card>

<Card title="Build generation for a pre-existing Play Store app" icon="android" href="/build-generation-for-a-pre-existing-play-store-app">
Updating an existing listing? This guide covers keystore signing and version management.
</Card>

<Card title="Your first build (walkthrough)" icon="hammer" href="/your-first-build-walkthrough">
New to EAS builds? Start here for a complete walkthrough.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

custom-domain.title: Custom domain
custom-domain.content:
## Overview

Every web app deployed on Emergent receives a free subdomain at `yourappname.emergent.build`. To present your app under your own brand, add a custom domain through the **Deployments** panel. Custom domains require you to configure DNS records with your domain registrar (e.g., Cloudflare, Namecheap, GoDaddy) and point them to Emergent's infrastructure.

This page walks you through DNS setup, troubleshooting, and common questions about the default subdomain.

<Note>
Custom domains are available for **web apps only**. Mobile apps use their own distribution channels (App Store, Play Store) and do not rely on DNS.
</Note>

---

## DNS: A record + Emergent IP

To serve your app at your root domain (e.g., `example.com`), add an **A record** that points to the IP address shown in the custom domain configuration flow.

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the custom domain panel">
In the Emergent workspace, navigate to **Deployments** → **Custom Domain** (web apps only). Click **Add Custom Domain**.
</Step>

<Step title="Copy the Emergent IP address">
The panel displays a dedicated IP address for your app. Copy this IP — you will use it in the next step.
</Step>

<Step title="Create an A record at your DNS provider">
Log in to your domain registrar or DNS host (Cloudflare, Namecheap, etc.). Add a new **A record**:

- **Host / Name**: `@` (or leave blank, depending on your provider)
- **Type**: `A`
- **Value / Points to**: the IP address from step 2
- **TTL**: `Auto` or `3600` (1 hour)

Save the record.
</Step>

<Step title="Confirm the domain in Emergent">
Return to the custom domain panel, enter your domain (e.g., `example.com`), and click **Verify**. Emergent will check for the A record and provision an SSL certificate once the record is detected.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info" title="SSL provisioning">
SSL certificates are issued automatically via Let's Encrypt after DNS verification. This usually takes a few minutes but can take up to 24 hours if DNS propagation is slow.
</Callout>

---

## CNAME (`www`) entry

Most users expect both `example.com` and `www.example.com` to work. Add a **CNAME record** to route `www` traffic to your root domain.

<Steps>
<Step title="Add the CNAME record">
In your DNS provider's dashboard, create a new **CNAME** record:

- **Host / Name**: `www`
- **Type**: `CNAME`
- **Value / Points to**: `example.com` (your root domain, no `http://`)
- **TTL**: `Auto` or `3600`

Save the record.
</Step>

<Step title="Test both URLs">
After DNS propagates, visit both `https://example.com` and `https://www.example.com`. Both should load your app. Emergent automatically redirects `www` to the root domain (or vice versa, depending on your configuration).
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
Some DNS providers (like Cloudflare) also support **CNAME flattening** or **ALIAS records** at the root. If you prefer to use a CNAME instead of an A record, consult your provider's documentation.
</Tip>

---

## Troubleshooting a stuck domain

If your custom domain does not load after adding DNS records, follow these checks:

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Verify DNS records are correct">
Use a DNS lookup tool (e.g., [dnschecker.org](https://dnschecker.org) or `dig example.com` in your terminal) to confirm:

- The **A record** for `@` (root) points to the Emergent IP.
- The **CNAME** for `www` points to your root domain.

If the records are missing or incorrect, update them at your DNS provider and allow a few minutes for propagation.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Wait for DNS propagation">
DNS changes can take anywhere from a few minutes to 48 hours to propagate globally, depending on your provider and the previous TTL. If you recently added or changed records, wait 1–2 hours and check again.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Check SSL certificate status">
In the Emergent **Deployments** panel, the custom domain row shows a status badge (e.g., **Pending**, **Active**, **Error**). If it says **Pending**, SSL provisioning is in progress. If it says **Error**, click **Details** to see the specific issue (often a DNS mismatch or CAA record blocking Let's Encrypt).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Clear your browser cache">
Browsers and operating systems cache DNS lookups. Try visiting your domain in an **incognito/private window** or run `ipconfig /flushdns` (Windows) / `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache` (macOS) to clear local caches.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<Warning>
If your domain registrar uses **proxy/CDN mode** (e.g., Cloudflare's orange cloud), ensure the A record is set to **DNS only** (gray cloud) during initial SSL provisioning. You can re-enable proxying after the certificate is issued.
</Warning>

---

## What the Emergent subdomain is

Every web app on Emergent is assigned a default URL in the format:

```
https://yourappname.emergent.build
```

This subdomain:

- Is **always available**, even if you add a custom domain.
- Receives the same deployments and updates as your custom domain.
- Uses a **wildcard SSL certificate** managed by Emergent (always HTTPS).
- Reflects the **app name** you chose during creation.

<Callout type="info" title="Will the subdomain work as-is?">
Yes. You can share the `yourappname.emergent.build` URL immediately — no DNS setup required. It is a fully functional production URL. Custom domains are optional and purely for branding.
</Callout>

If you are prototyping or running an internal tool, the Emergent subdomain is often sufficient. For customer-facing apps, a custom domain (e.g., `app.yourcompany.com`) is recommended.

---

## Changing the app name & Google auth label

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Can I rename my app (and subdomain)?">
Yes. In the workspace **Settings** → **App Name**, you can rename your app. The Emergent subdomain will update to `newappname.emergent.build`. Existing links using the old subdomain will break, so update any bookmarks or shared URLs.

<Warning>
Renaming the app does **not** automatically update OAuth redirect URIs in third-party providers (Google, GitHub, etc.). If you use [Google auth](/google-auth) or [Emergent Auth](/emergent-auth-built-in), you must also update the authorized redirect URI in the Google Cloud Console or GitHub OAuth app settings to match the new subdomain.
</Warning>
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Why does Google auth show 'Sign in to [old app name]'?">
Google's OAuth consent screen displays the **OAuth application name** configured in the Google Cloud Console, not the Emergent app name. To change the label users see:

1. Go to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com).
2. Select your project → **APIs & Services** → **OAuth consent screen**.
3. Update the **Application name** field.
4. Save changes.

The new name will appear on the Google sign-in prompt within a few minutes. For more details, see the [Google auth](/google-auth) page.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Google auth" icon="key" href="/google-auth">
Configure OAuth providers and update redirect URIs.
</Card>
<Card title="Emergent Auth (built-in)" icon="shield-check" href="/emergent-auth-built-in">
Use the platform's built-in auth system without third-party setup.
</Card>
<Card title="The chat-to-deployment flow" icon="rocket" href="/the-chat-to-deployment-flow">
Understand how code changes are built, tested and deployed.
</Card>
<Card title="A tour of the workspace" icon="compass" href="/a-tour-of-the-workspace">
Explore the Deployments panel and other workspace features.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

running-low-out-of-credits.title: Running low / out of credits
running-low-out-of-credits.content:
## What happens when credits run low

Emergent monitors your credit balance in real time as AI agents work on your app. **If your balance reaches zero mid-build**, the platform will pause all active generation tasks immediately. You'll see a notification in the workspace, and the build will stop wherever it left off—code already written remains saved, but the agents won't continue until you top up.

<Info title="No partial-charge surprises">
You are only charged for the work that completes. If a build stops halfway due to insufficient credits, you pay only for the tokens consumed up to that point.
</Info>

Once you **add more credits** (via the billing page or automatic renewal), you can resume the build by sending a new prompt or clicking "Continue" if the workspace offers that option. The agents will pick up context from where they stopped.

If you're uncertain how many credits remain, check the **credit balance indicator** in the top navigation bar or visit your account settings.

---

## Renewal & negative balance

Emergent supports **automatic monthly credit renewal** if you've enabled it in your billing settings. Under normal circumstances, your balance is topped up at the start of each billing cycle.

<Warning title="Negative balance and app takedown risk">
If your account has **fewer than 50 credits** at renewal time, the platform may allow your balance to go **negative** in order to complete an in-flight build. This grace period is temporary.

When Emergent's next billing check runs (typically within 24–48 hours), accounts with a negative balance will be flagged. **If the balance remains negative, your deployed app may be taken down** until you recharge and bring the account back into positive territory.
</Warning>

**To avoid this scenario:**

- Monitor your credit usage closely if you're near the end of a billing cycle.
- Set up **low-balance email alerts** (if available in your plan) so you're notified before hitting zero.
- Manually top up credits before starting a large build if your remaining balance is tight.

For more detail on how credits expire and how to recharge, see [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging).

---

## Estimating cost before building

**Large or complex builds** can consume hundreds or even thousands of credits, depending on the scope of your prompts, the number of files generated, and the iterations required. Before diving in, it helps to **budget for the work ahead**.

### Quick estimation tips

- **Start small**: Build a minimal version of one feature first, note the credit cost, then extrapolate for additional features.
- **Review past builds**: Check your billing history or workspace logs to see how many credits similar prompts consumed.
- **Ask in smaller chunks**: Breaking a big request into multiple focused prompts often gives you better control and visibility into incremental costs.

<Tip title="Test with a prototype">
If you're unsure how expensive a new idea will be, scaffold a simple proof-of-concept in a separate app. Once you've validated the cost and feasibility, you can commit to the full build with confidence.
</Tip>

### When to top up in advance

If you're planning a **major refactor**, **adding a complex backend integration**, or **converting between web and mobile** (see [Web ↔ Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical)), consider topping up your account beforehand. Running out mid-build can disrupt agent context and require you to re-explain requirements.

For ongoing projects, many users find that **enabling auto-renewal** and setting a comfortable monthly credit allowance provides the smoothest experience—no interruptions, and you stay in flow.

stripe.title: Stripe
stripe.content:
## Overview

Stripe is a payment processing platform that enables your Emergent app to accept payments, manage subscriptions, and handle complex billing scenarios. This guide walks you through integrating Stripe into your project using Emergent's natural language interface.

<Note>
Stripe integration requires a Stripe account. You can create one at [stripe.com](https://stripe.com) and use test mode during development at no cost.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Before integrating Stripe, ensure you have:

- A Stripe account (test mode credentials work for development)
- Your Stripe **Publishable Key** (starts with `pk_`)
- Your Stripe **Secret Key** (starts with `sk_`)
- A clear understanding of what payment flows your app needs (one-time payments, subscriptions, etc.)

## Integration Steps

<Steps>
<Step title="Tell Emergent about your payment needs">
Describe your payment requirements in natural language. Be specific about what you want to accomplish:

**Example prompts:**
- "Add Stripe payment processing. Users should be able to purchase credits for $10, $25, or $50."
- "Integrate Stripe subscriptions with three tiers: Basic ($9/month), Pro ($29/month), and Enterprise ($99/month)."
- "Add a checkout flow where users can buy individual products from a catalog."

Emergent's agents will generate the appropriate Stripe integration code, including client-side checkout components and server-side payment endpoints.
</Step>

<Step title="Provide your Stripe API keys">
Once the integration code is generated, you'll need to add your Stripe credentials as environment variables.

In your Emergent project, tell the agent:

```
Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to sk_test_xxxxx
Set STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to pk_test_xxxxx
```

<Warning>
Never commit secret keys to your codebase. Use Emergent's environment variable system to keep credentials secure. In production, replace test keys (`sk_test_`, `pk_test_`) with live keys (`sk_live_`, `pk_live_`).
</Warning>

The agent will configure these as secure environment variables accessible to your backend code.
</Step>

<Step title="Test the payment flow">
Ask Emergent to test the integration:

```
Test the Stripe checkout flow
```

The agents will verify that:
- Checkout sessions are created correctly
- Payment confirmation webhooks are received
- Success and cancellation redirects work as expected

Use [Stripe's test card numbers](https://stripe.com/docs/testing) to simulate successful and failed payments during testing.
</Step>

<Step title="Handle webhooks">
For production-grade integrations, configure webhook handling. Tell Emergent:

```
Set up Stripe webhooks to handle payment confirmation and subscription events
```

The agent will:
- Create webhook endpoints in your backend
- Parse and verify Stripe webhook signatures
- Update your database based on payment events

You'll receive a webhook URL to add in your Stripe Dashboard under **Developers → Webhooks**.
</Step>

<Step title="Deploy to production">
When you're ready to go live:

1. Replace test API keys with live keys in your environment variables
2. Update webhook endpoints in your Stripe Dashboard to point to your production domain
3. Ensure your [custom domain](/custom-domain) is configured if using one

Ask Emergent: `Deploy the app with production Stripe keys`
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common Payment Patterns

<Tabs>
<Tab title="One-time payments">
For simple product purchases or one-off charges:

```
Add a "Buy Now" button that charges $49.99 for premium access
```

Emergent will create a Stripe Checkout session that handles the entire payment flow, including success/cancel redirects.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Subscriptions">
For recurring billing:

```
Create a subscription system with monthly and annual billing options
```

The agents will set up Stripe subscription products, handle plan changes, and manage billing cycles.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Usage-based billing">
For metered or consumption-based pricing:

```
Set up usage-based billing where users are charged $0.10 per API call
```

This creates a metered billing system that reports usage to Stripe and bills accordingly.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Payment links">
For simple no-code payment collection:

```
Generate a Stripe payment link for a $199 consulting package
```

Returns a shareable URL that you can use in emails, marketing pages, or chat messages.
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Refining Your Integration

After the initial setup, you can refine the integration with natural language:

- "Add a customer portal where users can manage their subscription and update payment methods"
- "Show a payment history page with all past invoices"
- "Add a discount code field to the checkout"
- "Send a confirmation email after successful payment"
- "Store customer payment info for future purchases"

## Security Best Practices

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Use webhooks" icon="webhook">
Don't rely solely on client-side success callbacks. Webhooks provide authoritative, server-verified payment confirmation.
</Card>

<Card title="Validate amounts server-side" icon="shield-check">
Never trust payment amounts from the client. Always define prices and calculations in backend code.
</Card>

<Card title="Test failure scenarios" icon="alert-triangle">
Use Stripe's test cards to simulate declined payments, insufficient funds, and fraud scenarios.
</Card>

<Card title="Handle idempotency" icon="repeat">
Stripe operations should be idempotent to prevent duplicate charges if requests are retried.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Payments succeed but webhooks aren't received">
Verify your webhook URL is publicly accessible and correctly configured in the Stripe Dashboard. During local development, use Stripe CLI to forward webhooks to localhost, or ask Emergent: `Set up local webhook testing for Stripe`
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Invalid API key errors">
Double-check that you're using the correct key type (publishable keys for frontend, secret keys for backend) and that they match your Stripe account mode (test vs. live).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Checkout session expires too quickly">
Stripe Checkout sessions expire after 24 hours by default. If users abandon checkout frequently, consider storing session state and allowing them to resume, or create a new session on return.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Currency or region issues">
Stripe supports 135+ currencies but availability varies by country. Tell Emergent which currencies and regions you need to support: `Configure Stripe to accept EUR and GBP in addition to USD`
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next Steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Database Integration" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
Store payment records and subscription status in your MongoDB database
</Card>

<Card title="Custom Domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Configure a custom domain for professional payment page branding
</Card>
</CardGroup>

<Info>
Stripe's pricing is pay-as-you-go with no monthly fees. You're charged a percentage of each successful transaction. Check [Stripe's pricing page](https://stripe.com/pricing) for current rates in your region.
</Info>

openai.title: OpenAI
openai.content:
## Overview

OpenAI provides industry-leading language models including GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, and GPT-3.5 Turbo. Emergent supports OpenAI models out of the box, allowing you to build applications powered by these models through simple chat interactions.

You can use OpenAI models in two ways:
- **Automatically** via [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) — Emergent provides access without requiring your own API key
- **With your own API key** — Connect your OpenAI account for direct billing and usage tracking

## Using OpenAI with the Universal LLM Key

The simplest way to get started is using Emergent's Universal LLM Key, which provides immediate access to OpenAI models without any configuration.

<Note>
The Universal LLM Key is included with your Emergent account and supports multiple AI providers including OpenAI. Your usage is metered as part of your Emergent subscription.
</Note>

When you describe your app in chat, Emergent agents automatically use OpenAI models (or other supported providers) through the Universal LLM Key. No additional setup is required — just start building.

## Connecting Your Own OpenAI API Key

For direct control over billing, higher rate limits, or access to organization-specific models, you can connect your own OpenAI API key.

<Steps>
<Step title="Obtain your OpenAI API key">
Visit [platform.openai.com/api-keys](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) and sign in to your OpenAI account. Click **Create new secret key**, give it a descriptive name, and copy the key immediately (it won't be shown again).

<Warning>
Never commit your API key to version control or share it publicly. Treat it like a password.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Add the key to your Emergent project">
In your Emergent project settings, navigate to **Integrations** → **AI Providers**. Select **OpenAI** from the list and paste your API key into the provided field.

Alternatively, you can set the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable in your project's environment settings.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure model preferences (optional)">
Once connected, you can specify which OpenAI model your application should use. Common options include:

- `gpt-4-turbo` — Latest GPT-4 Turbo with improved performance and lower cost
- `gpt-4` — Standard GPT-4 for maximum capability
- `gpt-3.5-turbo` — Fast, cost-effective model for simpler tasks

Set your preferred model in your application's AI configuration or specify it when describing features in chat.
</Step>

<Step title="Verify the connection">
Test your connection by asking Emergent to build a feature that uses AI. The agents will now route requests through your OpenAI account. You can monitor usage and costs in your OpenAI dashboard.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Available OpenAI Models

Emergent supports the full range of OpenAI's text generation models:

| Model | Best For | Context Window |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| GPT-4 Turbo | Complex reasoning, long contexts | 128K tokens |
| GPT-4 | High-quality reasoning and creativity | 8K tokens |
| GPT-3.5 Turbo | Fast responses, cost efficiency | 16K tokens |

<Info>
Model availability and specifications may change. Check OpenAI's documentation for the latest information on model capabilities and pricing.
</Info>

## Building AI Features with OpenAI

When describing your app in chat, you can reference OpenAI capabilities directly:

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Natural language requests">
Simply describe what you want in natural language:

*"Add a chatbot that uses GPT-4 to answer customer questions about our products"*

*"Create a content summarizer using GPT-3.5 Turbo"*

*"Build an AI writing assistant with GPT-4 Turbo for generating blog posts"*
</Tab>

<Tab title="Code integration">
Emergent agents will generate the appropriate code to integrate OpenAI models. Your application will include properly structured API calls with error handling, streaming support, and token management.

The generated code handles:
- Authentication and API key management
- Request formatting and model parameters
- Response parsing and streaming
- Rate limiting and error recovery
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Best Practices

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Choose the right model" icon="brain">
Use GPT-4 for complex reasoning and creativity. Use GPT-3.5 Turbo for speed and cost efficiency on simpler tasks.
</Card>

<Card title="Monitor usage" icon="chart-line">
Track your OpenAI API usage in the OpenAI dashboard to manage costs. Set usage limits if needed.
</Card>

<Card title="Implement caching" icon="database">
For repeated queries, describe caching requirements to Emergent agents to reduce API calls and costs.
</Card>

<Card title="Handle rate limits" icon="gauge">
Describe retry logic and graceful degradation when explaining features that make frequent API calls.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Cost Optimization

When building AI-powered features, consider these strategies to optimize OpenAI costs:

- **Use appropriate models** — Don't use GPT-4 when GPT-3.5 Turbo is sufficient
- **Implement prompt caching** — Cache responses for identical or similar queries
- **Limit context length** — Only include necessary context in prompts
- **Use streaming** — Stream responses for better user experience without extra cost
- **Set max tokens** — Configure maximum response lengths to prevent runaway costs

<Tip>
When describing AI features to Emergent, mention cost optimization requirements explicitly: *"Build this feature to minimize token usage"* or *"Use GPT-3.5 Turbo for cost efficiency"*.
</Tip>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="API key not working or showing authentication errors">
Verify that:
- Your API key was copied correctly without extra spaces
- Your OpenAI account has billing enabled and sufficient credits
- The API key has not been revoked in your OpenAI dashboard
- You've saved the configuration in Emergent after pasting the key
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Rate limit errors">
OpenAI enforces rate limits based on your account tier. If you encounter rate limit errors:
- Implement exponential backoff and retry logic (describe this to Emergent agents)
- Upgrade your OpenAI account tier for higher limits
- Reduce request frequency in your application logic
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="High costs or unexpected billing">
Review your OpenAI usage dashboard to identify expensive operations:
- Check if prompts are longer than necessary
- Verify you're using the intended model (GPT-4 costs more than GPT-3.5)
- Look for API calls in loops or high-frequency events
- Set up usage alerts in your OpenAI account
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Model not available or deprecated warnings">
OpenAI occasionally deprecates older models. If you see deprecation warnings:
- Update your model configuration to use current model versions
- Describe the required change to Emergent agents: *"Update to use gpt-4-turbo instead of gpt-4-0314"*
- Test thoroughly after model changes as behavior may differ slightly
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Related Resources

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="The Universal LLM Key" icon="key" href="/the-universal-llm-key">
Learn about Emergent's built-in AI access across multiple providers
</Card>

<Card title="Glossary of Emergent Terms" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
Understand key concepts and terminology used in Emergent
</Card>
</CardGroup>

how-credits-work.title: How credits work
how-credits-work.content:
## What credits are

Credits are Emergent's usage currency. Every action the platform takes on your behalf—generating code, running tests, deploying to the cloud, calling external APIs—consumes a small number of credits from your account balance. This metered approach keeps costs predictable and aligns what you pay with what you actually use.

You'll see your current balance in the top-right corner of the workspace. When credits run low, you can top up or upgrade your plan at any time.

---

## What consumes credits

Credits are deducted whenever the platform performs work:

- **Code generation**  
  Each time you send a prompt and Emergent's agents write, refactor or extend your app's code, credits are consumed. The amount scales with the scope of the change and the complexity of the files touched.

- **Testing & validation**  
  Automated tests—unit tests, integration checks, visual regression scans—all consume credits. The more comprehensive the test suite, the higher the cost per run.

- **Cloud deploys**  
  Building, bundling and pushing your app to production infrastructure (including CDN invalidation and serverless edge deployment) uses credits proportional to build time and artifact size.

- **Integrations & scheduled tasks**  
  Calling third-party APIs, scheduling cron jobs and running background workers through [Integrations & scheduled tasks](/integrations-scheduled-tasks) each deduct credits based on execution duration and frequency.

- **Database operations**  
  Heavy read/write workloads against the [MongoDB database](/database-mongodb), particularly complex aggregations or large bulk inserts, incur incremental charges.

- **LLM calls via the Universal Key**  
  If you use [the Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) to let your *app* call language models at runtime, those API calls are billed through your Emergent credit balance (not your personal OpenAI or Anthropic account).

<Info title="Maxx mode uses more credits">
When you enable **Maxx mode** (the toggle in the prompt bar), Emergent agents plan more thoroughly, explore alternative implementations and run deeper validation passes. This produces higher-quality results but consumes 2–4× the credits of a standard prompt.
</Info>

---

## Credits per prompt & setting a limit

The cost of a single prompt varies widely—from a handful of credits for a small UI tweak to hundreds for a full feature with tests and deployment. The platform shows an **estimated cost** before committing large changes, so you're never surprised.

<Tip title="Cap your spending with a per-prompt limit">
In **Settings → Billing**, you can set a **maximum credits per prompt**. If an agent's plan would exceed that ceiling, Emergent will ask you to approve the overage or break the task into smaller steps. This guardrail prevents runaway costs on complex requests.
</Tip>

If you regularly work on large, multi-file features, consider raising your limit or switching to a higher-tier plan with a more generous monthly credit allowance and lower per-credit rate.

---

## Monitoring usage

The workspace sidebar displays a real-time **credit meter** showing your current balance and this month's consumption trend. Click it to open a detailed breakdown by category (generation, testing, deploy, integrations) and see which prompts or deploys were the costliest.

You'll also receive an email alert when your balance drops below 20 % of your plan's monthly allowance, giving you time to top up before hitting zero.

<Warning title="Paused projects when balance reaches zero">
If your credit balance hits zero mid-operation, in-progress builds and deploys will pause. You can resume immediately by adding credits—no work is lost, but your app won't go live until the deploy completes.
</Warning>

---

## Topping up & rollover

- **One-time top-ups** never expire; unused credits roll over indefinitely.  
- **Monthly plan credits** roll over for up to three billing cycles, then expire.  
- You can mix plan credits and top-up credits; the platform always spends expiring credits first to maximize your value.

For high-volume teams, contact support to discuss annual prepaid bundles with volume discounts.

what-is-a-job.title: What is a Job?
what-is-a-job.content:
## What is a Job?

In Emergent, a **job** is a single application or project. Every time you describe a new app and start building, you create a job. The term "job" appears throughout the platform — in your workspace, the sidebar, notifications, and billing — and always refers to one discrete build.

A job encompasses everything related to that app: the chat history where you described it, the generated code, test runs, deployments, and all iterations as you refine the product.

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Does one job = one app?">
    Yes. Each job corresponds to exactly one application. If you want to build a weather dashboard and a recipe tracker, those are two separate jobs.
    
    Everything tied to a single app — code, dependencies, deployment config, chat context — lives within that job's workspace.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I manage multiple jobs?">
    Your workspace lists all your jobs in the sidebar. Click any job name to switch to it and load its chat, code, and deployment history.
    
    You can rename, archive, or delete jobs from the job settings menu (accessed via the three-dot icon next to the job name). Archiving a job removes it from the active list but preserves all its data.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can I work on multiple jobs at the same time?">
    The workspace UI focuses on one job at a time, but you can open multiple browser tabs or windows — each pointing to a different job — and work in parallel.
    
    Builds, tests, and deployments run independently per job, so starting a build in one job does not block another.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What happens when I fork a job?">
    Forking creates a new job that starts with a copy of the current job's code and state. This is useful when you want to explore a different direction or experiment without affecting the original.
    
    The forked job is fully independent: changes in one do not affect the other. For more detail, see [Forking](/forking).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Do jobs cost credits individually?">
    Yes. Each job consumes credits based on its own build, test, and deployment activity. Building and iterating on multiple jobs in parallel will use credits from your account balance accordingly.
    
    For pricing details, see [How credits work](/how-credits-work).
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Projects

<Info>
**Projects** let you group related jobs together for easier organisation. A project is simply a folder that contains multiple jobs — think of it as a way to keep all the apps for a client, a product suite, or a learning experiment in one place.
</Info>

To create a project, use the "New Project" option in the workspace sidebar. You can then move existing jobs into it or create new jobs directly inside the project.

Switching between projects updates the sidebar to show only the jobs within that project. You can always return to the "All Jobs" view to see everything across all projects.

Projects are purely organisational — they do not share code, dependencies, or configuration between jobs. Each job inside a project remains independent.
what-is-a-job.description: 1. What a Job is: a single build/app/project in Emergent - the term you'll see across the platform.

custom-mcp-integrations.title: Custom & MCP integrations
custom-mcp-integrations.content:
## Overview

Wingman can be extended with both **first-party** and **custom third-party** Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, giving your agents access to external tools, data sources, and APIs. You configure servers by adding an endpoint and a JSON configuration block; Wingman handles authentication and credential injection at runtime.

<Note>
MCP integrations are managed per workspace. Each server you add becomes available to all agents in that workspace.
</Note>

---

## Supported server types

Emergent currently supports MCP servers that expose:

- **Tools** — callable functions that agents can invoke during conversations (e.g., database queries, file operations, API calls).
- **Resources** — read-only data sources that agents can reference (e.g., documentation, schemas, knowledge bases).

<Warning title="Unsupported: Prompts">
MCP *prompt* primitives are **not yet supported**. Servers that rely exclusively on prompts will not function correctly.
</Warning>

---

## Adding an MCP server

<Steps>

<Step title="Navigate to Wingman settings">
Open the **Wingman** tab in your workspace sidebar, then click the **gear icon** (⚙️) in the top-right corner to open Wingman settings.
</Step>

<Step title="Locate the MCP Servers section">
Scroll to the **Custom & MCP integrations** section. You'll see a list of configured servers (if any) and an **Add Server** button.
</Step>

<Step title="Click Add Server">
Click **Add Server**. A modal will appear prompting you for two fields:

- **Endpoint** — the URL or command that starts the MCP server (see [Endpoint formats](#endpoint-formats) below).
- **Configuration JSON** — a JSON object defining environment variables, arguments, and other server-specific settings.
</Step>

<Step title="Enter the endpoint">
Paste the server's endpoint. Common formats:

- `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`
- `uvx mcp-server-git`
- `docker run --rm -i your-org/mcp-server:latest`
- `https://your-api.com/mcp` (for HTTP-based servers)

See [Endpoint formats](#endpoint-formats) for details.
</Step>

<Step title="Provide the configuration JSON">
Enter a JSON object with any required environment variables, command-line arguments, or runtime settings. For example:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db",
    "API_KEY": "sk-..."
  },
  "args": ["--verbose"]
}
```

Credentials are stored securely and injected at runtime—they are **never logged or exposed** to the agent's conversation history.
</Step>

<Step title="Save and test">
Click **Save**. Wingman will attempt to initialize the server. If successful, you'll see a green checkmark and the server's tools/resources will appear in the Wingman interface. If initialization fails, review the error message and check your endpoint and configuration.
</Step>

</Steps>

---

## Endpoint formats

MCP servers can be invoked in several ways:

| Format | Example | When to use |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| **npx** | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres` | Official or npm-published MCP servers |
| **uvx** | `uvx mcp-server-git` | Python-based MCP servers using uv |
| **Docker** | `docker run --rm -i your-org/mcp-server:latest` | Containerized servers requiring isolation |
| **HTTP** | `https://your-api.com/mcp` | Remote MCP servers accessible over HTTPS |
| **Local binary** | `/path/to/my-mcp-server` | Custom-built executables |

<Info>
For `npx` and `uvx`, the `-y` flag (or equivalent) auto-accepts prompts. For Docker, `--rm -i` ensures the container is cleaned up and accepts stdin.
</Info>

---

## Configuration JSON schema

The configuration object supports the following keys:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "KEY": "value"
  },
  "args": ["--flag", "value"],
  "timeout": 30000
}
```

- **`env`** *(object, optional)* — Environment variables passed to the server process. Use this for API keys, database URLs, and other secrets.
- **`args`** *(array, optional)* — Command-line arguments appended to the endpoint invocation.
- **`timeout`** *(integer, optional)* — Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for server initialization (default: `30000`).

<Warning title="Credential security">
Secrets in the `env` object are encrypted at rest and injected only when the server is spawned. **Never commit credentials to version control.**
</Warning>

---

## Credential handling

Emergent stores MCP server credentials separately from your workspace code:

1. **Encryption at rest** — all `env` values are encrypted in the database.
2. **Runtime injection** — credentials are decrypted and passed to the server process only when needed.
3. **No agent exposure** — agents can *invoke* tools but cannot read or log credential values.

<Tip>
For shared workspaces, use [environment variables](/the-universal-llm-key#environment-variables) or a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, Vault) and reference them in the configuration JSON via placeholder syntax (if your server supports it).
</Tip>

---

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Server fails to initialize">
**Check**:
- The endpoint is correct and the binary/package is installed.
- Environment variables are spelled correctly and values are valid.
- The server supports MCP version 1.0 or later.
- Firewall/network rules allow outbound connections (for HTTP endpoints).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Tools appear but agents can't invoke them">
**Possible causes**:
- The server requires credentials that weren't provided in `env`.
- The tool definition is malformed (check server logs if available).
- The agent's model doesn't support tool/function calling (use GPT-4 or Claude 3+).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Prompt-based servers don't work">
Emergent does not yet support MCP *prompts*. If your server exposes only prompts (no tools or resources), it will not function. Check the server's documentation for a tools-based alternative.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Credentials are rejected">
- Verify the credential format (e.g., `postgresql://` vs `postgres://`).
- Ensure the credential has the necessary permissions (read/write, scopes, etc.).
- Test the credential outside Emergent (e.g., with `psql`, `curl`) to confirm validity.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Examples

### PostgreSQL database

**Endpoint:**  
```
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres
```

**Configuration JSON:**
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb"
  }
}
```

### Git operations

**Endpoint:**  
```
uvx mcp-server-git
```

**Configuration JSON:**
```json
{
  "env": {
    "GIT_REPO_PATH": "/workspace/repo"
  },
  "args": ["--read-only"]
}
```

### Custom HTTP MCP server

**Endpoint:**  
```
https://api.example.com/mcp
```

**Configuration JSON:**
```json
{
  "env": {
    "API_KEY": "your-secret-key"
  },
  "timeout": 60000
}
```

---

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Custom agents" icon="robot" href="/custom-agents">
    Build agents with specialized instructions and tool access
  </Card>
  <Card title="Database (MongoDB)" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
    Connect your workspace to a MongoDB instance
  </Card>
  <Card title="The Universal LLM Key" icon="key" href="/the-universal-llm-key">
    Manage API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers
  </Card>
  <Card title="Glossary of Emergent terms" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
    Definitions of workspace, agent, MCP, and more
  </Card>
</CardGroup>
