missing-functionality.title: Missing functionality
missing-functionality.content:
## Overview

When a feature you described doesn't appear in your app—or doesn't work as expected—it's usually due to one of a few common causes. This page walks you through diagnosing the issue and requesting a rebuild or clarification.

<Note>
Most missing functionality is resolved by rephrasing your request or explicitly calling out the feature in a follow-up chat message.
</Note>

---

## Common reasons features go missing

**The agent misunderstood the scope**  
Natural language can be ambiguous. If you said "add user profiles," the agent might have built a basic profile page but skipped avatar uploads, bio fields, or edit functionality.

**The feature was deprioritized**  
Emergent's agents prioritize core flows first. Secondary features—like admin dashboards, analytics, or "nice-to-have" UI polish—may be deferred or omitted if the initial build focused on MVP functionality.

**A dependency wasn't clear**  
Some features require scaffolding. For example, "send email notifications" needs an email service integrated, and "save preferences" needs a database schema. If you didn't mention the underlying requirement, the agent may have skipped the feature.

**The feature exists but isn't visible**  
Check that you're testing the right screen, user role, or device form factor. A feature built for mobile may not render on desktop, or an admin-only button may be hidden for regular users.

---

## Step-by-step diagnosis

<Steps>

<Step title="Verify the feature was in scope">
Re-read your original chat prompt and any follow-up messages. Did you explicitly request the feature, or was it implied? Agents work best with direct, specific instructions.
</Step>

<Step title="Check the current build">
Open the live preview or deployed app and navigate to where the feature should appear. Test all relevant user roles, screen sizes, and edge cases (e.g., empty states, logged-out views).
</Step>

<Step title="Review the build log (if available)">
Some workspaces surface build summaries or agent notes in the chat history. Look for messages like "skipped X due to Y" or "deferred Z for next iteration."
</Step>

<Step title="Search the codebase">
Use the workspace file tree or search to look for related code. If the feature is partially implemented—like a backend route without a UI—you'll find clues in `api/`, `components/`, or `pages/` directories.
</Step>

</Steps>

---

## Requesting a fix or rebuild

Once you've confirmed the feature is missing or incomplete, ask the agent to build it in a new chat message. Use clear, actionable language:

<CodeGroup>

```plaintext Good example
Add a "Save Draft" button to the blog post editor. 
It should save the current title and body to the 
database without publishing. Show a success toast 
when saved.
```

```plaintext Avoid vague requests
The editor is missing stuff. Fix it.
```

</CodeGroup>

**Be explicit about acceptance criteria:**

- Where should the feature appear? (e.g., "in the top-right of the editor header")
- What should it do? (e.g., "POST to `/api/drafts`, store in MongoDB")
- What should the user see? (e.g., "a green checkmark icon and 'Draft saved' message")

<Tip>
If the feature depends on a database collection, API endpoint, or third-party service, mention it up front. For example: "Use the `drafts` collection in MongoDB" or "Integrate Stripe for payment processing."
</Tip>

---

## When functionality is partially built

Sometimes a feature exists in the backend but lacks a UI, or vice versa. Here's how to complete it:

| Situation | Next step |
|-----------|-----------|
| Backend route exists, no UI | "Create a form in `components/DraftEditor.tsx` that calls `POST /api/drafts` and shows a success message." |
| UI exists, no backend | "Implement the `/api/drafts` endpoint: accept title and body, save to MongoDB `drafts` collection, return 201." |
| Feature works on web, missing on mobile | "Add the Save Draft button to the mobile layout in `DraftEditor.tsx`. It should match the web behavior." |

---

## Common gotchas

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Feature was removed in a later iteration">
If you asked the agent to "simplify" or "redesign" the app, it may have removed features you wanted to keep. Check the chat history for messages like "removed X to streamline Y."  

**Fix:** Explicitly ask to restore it: "Bring back the Save Draft button and keep the new design for the rest of the editor."
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Feature is hidden behind a feature flag or env var">
Some functionality—like admin panels or payment flows—may be gated by environment variables or user roles. Check your `.env` file and any role-checking logic in the code.

**Fix:** Update the relevant env var or user role in your database. See [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) for how to modify user records.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Third-party service not configured">
Features like email, payments, or SMS require API keys and service setup. If the agent built the integration but you haven't added credentials, the feature will fail silently.

**Fix:** Add the missing API key to your `.env` file or workspace secrets. See [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) for an example of secret configuration.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Escalation

If you've followed the steps above and the feature still doesn't work:

1. **Describe the exact behavior** you're seeing (e.g., "clicking Save Draft shows a 500 error in the console").
2. **Share the expected behavior** (e.g., "it should save to MongoDB and show a success toast").
3. **Ask the agent to debug:** "Check the `/api/drafts` endpoint and the `DraftEditor` component. The save button isn't working."

<Warning>
If the agent repeatedly misunderstands or skips the same feature, try breaking the request into smaller, sequential steps. For example: "First, create the database schema for drafts. Then, build the API endpoint. Finally, add the UI button."
</Warning>

---

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>

<Card title="Glossary" icon="book" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
Definitions of workspace, agent, build, and other platform terms
</Card>

<Card title="Tour of the workspace" icon="map" href="/a-tour-of-the-workspace">
Understand where code, logs, and builds live in your project
</Card>

</CardGroup>

plans-the-free-tier.title: Plans & the free tier
plans-the-free-tier.content:
## Overview

Emergent offers a tiered pricing model designed to match your development needs and budget. Whether you're exploring the platform for the first time, building personal projects, or scaling production applications, there's a plan that fits.

Every plan is **credit-based**: building, testing, and deploying your apps consumes credits. The main difference between plans is your monthly credit allocation, deployment capability, and access to advanced features.

## Plan comparison

<Callout type="info" title="Credit-based usage">
All plans use credits to power AI agents that write, test, and deploy your code. Higher tiers give you more credits per month and unlock additional capabilities.
</Callout>

| Feature | Free | Standard | Pro |
|---------|------|----------|-----|
| **Monthly credits** | 10 | Higher allocation | Highest allocation |
| **Deploy to production** | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Custom domains** | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Advanced features** | Limited | Full access | Full access + priority |
| **Support** | Community | Standard | Priority |
| **Best for** | Exploration & learning | Personal projects & prototypes | Production apps & teams |

<Note>
Free tier credits reset monthly but **do not roll over**. Unused credits expire at the end of each billing cycle.
</Note>

## Free tier

The Free tier gives you **10 credits per month** to explore Emergent and understand how vibe-coding works. You can:

- Chat with AI agents to build and iterate on apps
- Test features and workflows in the workspace
- Learn the platform's capabilities hands-on

**What you cannot do:**

- Deploy apps to production (deployment requires a paid plan)
- Use [custom domains](/custom-domain)
- Access priority support or advanced agent customization

The Free tier is perfect for evaluating Emergent, experimenting with ideas, or learning how agentic development works before committing to a paid plan.

<Tip>
If you run out of free credits mid-month, you can upgrade to Standard or Pro immediately—your new credit allocation becomes available right away.
</Tip>

## Standard plan

The Standard plan is designed for **developers building personal projects, side projects, and production-ready prototypes**. You get:

- A larger monthly credit allocation
- Full deployment capability (your apps go live at `yourapp.emergent.run`)
- Support for [custom domains](/custom-domain)
- Access to all core platform features

Standard is the right choice when you're ready to ship real applications, need your work publicly accessible, or want consistent monthly credits for ongoing development.

## Pro plan

The Pro plan is built for **teams, businesses, and power users** who need maximum capacity and priority treatment. It includes:

- The highest monthly credit allocation
- Priority support with faster response times
- Early access to new features and capabilities
- All Standard features, plus advanced configurations

Choose Pro when you're scaling production apps, running a development team, or need guaranteed availability and support.

<Info>
Both Standard and Pro support [custom agents](/custom-agents) and [AI media generation](/ai-media-generation-image-video-audio). Credit usage varies by job complexity—see [What is a Job?](/what-is-a-job) for details.
</Info>

## Choosing the right plan

<Steps>
<Step title="Evaluate your deployment needs">
If you need to deploy apps to production, you must choose Standard or Pro. Free tier is workspace-only.
</Step>

<Step title="Estimate your monthly credit usage">
Consider how many apps you'll build, how frequently you'll iterate, and whether you need [Wingman](/what-is-wingman) assistance. Larger, more complex jobs consume more credits.
</Step>

<Step title="Factor in team size and support requirements">
Solo developers typically do well on Standard. Teams, agencies, or businesses benefit from Pro's priority support and higher limits.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Bulk credits & custom pricing

<Callout type="tip" title="Need more credits?">
If your usage exceeds your plan's monthly allocation, you can **purchase bulk credits** with custom pricing tailored to your volume. This option is available to Standard and Pro customers—contact sales to discuss your needs.
</Callout>

Bulk credit purchases are one-time add-ons that supplement your monthly plan. They're ideal for:

- Seasonal spikes in development activity
- Large migration or refactoring projects
- Agencies managing multiple client apps

For **enterprise-scale needs**, including dedicated infrastructure, SLAs, and custom compliance requirements, see [Enterprise plan & features](/enterprise-plan-features).

## Credit management

All plans follow the same credit lifecycle rules:

- Credits recharge monthly on your billing date
- Unused credits **do not roll over**—they expire at cycle end
- You can monitor usage in real-time from your workspace dashboard

For details on expiry, top-ups, and recharge timing, see [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging).

<Warning>
Deploying, testing, and generating media with AI agents all consume credits. Plan your monthly allocation carefully, especially if you're building multiple apps or iterating frequently.
</Warning>

secrets-env-variables.title: Secrets & env variables
secrets-env-variables.content:
## Overview

Secrets and environment variables let your deployed app access API keys, database credentials, and other sensitive configuration without hardcoding them in your codebase.

Emergent provides a built-in **secrets manager** for every project. Store your secrets there, not in files committed to your repository.

<Warning title="Secrets are deployment-time only">
The secrets manager is designed for **deployed** applications. During the build phase in chat, agents use the [Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) and test credentials. Your secrets become available only after deployment.
</Warning>

---

## Where to store secrets

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the secrets manager">
In your workspace, navigate to the **Secrets** panel (usually in the left sidebar or deployment settings).
</Step>

<Step title="Add a key-value pair">
Enter the variable name (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`) and its value. The value will be masked in the UI after you save.
</Step>

<Step title="Save">
Click **Save** to store the secret. It is now encrypted and associated with your project.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
Never commit `.env` files or paste secrets directly into your code. The secrets manager keeps credentials out of version control and logs.
</Note>

---

## Accessing secrets in your app

Your application reads secrets as **environment variables** at runtime:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript Node.js / Next.js
const apiKey = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
```

```python Python / Flask
import os
api_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
```

```bash Shell / Docker
echo $OPENAI_API_KEY
```
</CodeGroup>

The platform injects these variables into your app's container when it starts.

---

## Redeploying after adding or changing secrets

<Warning title="Saving alone does not update your live app">
A newly saved or updated secret **will not take effect** in a running deployment until you **redeploy**.
</Warning>

**Why?** Your deployed container was built with the secrets available at deployment time. Changing a secret in the manager updates the stored value but does not restart or reconfigure running instances.

### How to apply updated secrets

1. Save your new or modified secret in the secrets manager.
2. Trigger a **replace deploy** (redeploy) from the workspace or via chat (e.g. "redeploy the app").
3. The new container starts with the updated environment variables.

<Tip>
If your app isn't picking up a secret, confirm you've redeployed since the last save. Check the deployment timestamp in your workspace.
</Tip>

---

## Common pitfalls

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="I saved a secret but my app still can't connect to the database">
**Solution:** Redeploy the app. The running container uses the secrets from the last deployment, not the latest saved values.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I see the value of a secret after I save it?">
No. The secrets manager masks values in the UI for security. If you lose a key, delete the old entry and create a new one with the correct value, then redeploy.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Do secrets sync to GitHub?">
No. Secrets live only in the Emergent platform. If you use [Save to GitHub](/save-to-github), your repository will not contain the secret values. You must configure secrets separately in any external CI/CD or hosting environment.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Best practices

- **Use descriptive names**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is clearer than `KEY_1`.
- **Rotate credentials regularly**: Update secrets in the manager, then redeploy.
- **One secret per variable**: Avoid concatenating multiple keys into a single environment variable.
- **Test after deploy**: Confirm your app can read the secret by checking logs or a health endpoint.

---

## Related pages

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="The chat-to-deployment flow" icon="messages" href="/the-chat-to-deployment-flow">
Understand how build and deploy phases handle credentials
</Card>

<Card title="Database (MongoDB)" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
Configure your MongoDB connection string as a secret
</Card>

<Card title="The Universal LLM Key" icon="key" href="/the-universal-llm-key">
Learn how agents access LLMs during the build phase
</Card>

<Card title="App slow, crashing or cold-starting" icon="triangle-alert" href="/app-slow-crashing-or-cold-starting">
Troubleshoot runtime issues, including missing secrets
</Card>
</CardGroup>
secrets-env-variables.description: 1. Where secrets go: use the secrets manager, not files in the repo.

preview-vs-deployed-separate.title: Preview vs Deployed (separate)
preview-vs-deployed-separate.content:
## They are different environments

When you build an app in Emergent, you work with **two distinct environments**:

- **Preview** – the live sandbox inside the workspace where you test changes as you refine your app with AI agents.
- **Deployed** – the production environment serving your real users at your published URL.

Each environment runs independently with its own URL, server instance, and database. Changes you make in preview do not automatically affect the deployed app until you explicitly push them.

<Info title="Preview is your sandbox">
Preview lets you iterate freely, test new features, and fix bugs without risk to your live users. It's the safe place to experiment before committing changes to production.
</Info>

---

## Why preview changes don't appear live

A common surprise: you've refined your app in preview, the agents have updated the code and tested it successfully — but **none of those changes appear in the deployed app**.

This is by design. Emergent keeps the two environments separate so you never accidentally break a live app while iterating. Your deployed app continues to serve the last version you explicitly pushed, and it will not reflect any preview work until you take action.

<Warning title="Changes stay in preview until redeployed">
Edits, bug fixes, new features and code improvements remain in the preview environment only. To make them live, you must **Redeploy** or **Replace** the deployed app.
</Warning>

---

## Redeploy vs Replace

When you're ready to push changes from preview to production, Emergent offers two options:

| Action | What it updates | Database impact |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Redeploy** | Code, assets, dependencies | None – keeps existing DB and data |
| **Replace** | Code *and* database schema/data | Swaps or resets the DB (depending on option chosen) |

- Use **Redeploy** when you've only changed UI, logic, styling or dependencies and want to preserve all user data as-is.
- Use **Replace** when your preview has a new or modified database schema, or when you want to reset/migrate production data.

---

## Redeploy: push latest code

**Redeploy** copies your preview's code, configuration and assets into the deployed environment and restarts it — without touching the database.

- The deployed app's existing MongoDB database remains untouched; all user accounts, records and uploads persist.
- No additional charge for redeployment (you already pay a fixed monthly rate per deployed app).
- Ideal for rolling out bug fixes, UI tweaks, new pages or backend logic that don't require schema changes.

<Tip title="Safe for iterative improvements">
Redeploy as often as you like. It's the quickest, safest way to keep your live app up to date without risking data loss.
</Tip>

---

## Replace: also swaps the database

**Replace** goes further: it updates the code *and* handles the database. When you replace a deployed app, Emergent prompts you to choose what happens to the production database:

- **Keep existing data** (migrate the schema if necessary).
- **Start fresh** (new, empty database).
- **Clone preview data** into production.

Replacing is necessary when your preview introduces new collections, changes field types, or otherwise alters the database structure.

<Warning title="Database changes only happen on Replace">
If you redeploy an app with a new data model, the deployed app will run the new code but still point to the *old* schema. This can cause runtime errors. When the schema has changed, always **Replace** and choose the appropriate database option.
</Warning>

For a detailed explanation of each database option and safe migration strategies, see the [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) page.

---

## Updating a live app safely

Once real users are on your deployed app, updates require extra care:

1. **Test thoroughly in preview first** – use the preview environment to verify all changes work as expected.
2. **Choose Redeploy for code-only changes** – keeps user data intact and minimizes risk.
3. **Choose Replace + "Keep existing data" for schema changes** – when you've added new fields or collections, this migrates the structure without losing user records.
4. **Avoid "Start fresh" on a live app** – this wipes all production data and is almost never appropriate after launch.

<Info title="Handling data migrations">
If you need to transform or backfill data during a schema change, test the migration logic in preview, then replace with "Keep existing data." Emergent will preserve records and apply the new schema. For complex transformations, consider a maintenance window or phased rollout.
</Info>

For more on database options during replacement, managing user data safely, and troubleshooting schema conflicts, visit [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb).

data-privacy.title: Data privacy
data-privacy.content:
## How we handle your data

When you build on Emergent, you're trusting us with your project code, chat history, environment variables, and any data your app generates. We take that responsibility seriously.

<Callout type="success" title="Your data is private by default">
Your projects, chat logs, code, and secrets are **never** shared with other users or used to train LLMs. We isolate every workspace and encrypt data in transit and at rest.
</Callout>

## Where your data lives

All project data — including source code, build artifacts, environment variables, and chat history — is stored on secure cloud infrastructure in the United States. We use industry-standard encryption (TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest) and follow AWS best practices for storage isolation.

Your MongoDB databases are hosted in the region you select at project creation time. By default, databases are created in `us-east-1`, but you can choose other regions if data residency is a concern. See [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) for configuration details.

## Who can access your data

<Steps>
<Step title="You and your workspace members">
Anyone you invite to your workspace can view and edit project code, inspect logs, and read chat history. Manage access carefully — there is no read-only role yet.
</Step>

<Step title="Emergent platform services">
Our backend services access your data to:
- Execute builds and deployments
- Stream logs and debugging output
- Generate AI-assisted code and fixes
- Route API requests to your deployed apps

This access is **automated and scoped** — no human Emergent employee views your data as part of normal operations.
</Step>

<Step title="Emergent support (with your consent)">
If you open a support ticket and explicitly share a project link or invite support staff to your workspace, our engineers may inspect logs, environment variables, and code to diagnose issues. We will **always ask permission** before looking at sensitive data.
</Step>

<Step title="LLM providers (anonymized context only)">
When you use AI features, we send code snippets and chat context to third-party LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.). These requests are anonymized and do not include your workspace name, email, or identifiable metadata. LLM providers process the data according to their own privacy policies; we do **not** opt your data into model training.
</Step>
</Steps>

## What we don't do

- **We don't sell your data.** Ever.
- **We don't train models on your projects.** Your code and chat logs stay out of any training pipeline.
- **We don't index your projects for search** outside your own workspace.
- **We don't retain deleted data indefinitely.** When you delete a project, we purge code, logs, and build artifacts within 30 days. Database backups expire according to the retention policy you set.

## Reducing exposure

If you're working with particularly sensitive data, consider these practices:

- **Use environment variables for secrets** rather than hardcoding them in source. These are encrypted at rest and never logged in plain text.
- **Limit workspace invitations** to team members who need access.
- **Rotate API keys regularly**, especially if a team member leaves or you suspect a leak.
- **Self-host sensitive databases** and connect via secure tunnel, rather than using the built-in MongoDB for regulated data.
- **Review deployed app permissions** — a public URL means anyone with the link can access your app's endpoints. Use authentication if you need to restrict access.

For more on preventing accidental data exposure in your app's public endpoints, see [Data leakage](/data-leakage).

## Questions about ownership

You retain full ownership of your code, designs, and data. Emergent claims no IP rights to what you build. For the legal details, see [Your data & ownership](/your-data-ownership).

<Note>
If you have specific compliance requirements (GDPR data processing agreements, HIPAA, SOC 2 attestation), reach out to our enterprise team — we offer tailored agreements for regulated industries.
</Note>
data-privacy.description: Where your data is stored and who can access it; addressing privacy worries.

integrations-scheduled-tasks.title: Integrations & scheduled tasks
integrations-scheduled-tasks.content:
## Overview

Every Wingman on Emergent ships with powerful integration and automation capabilities. You can connect to 300+ external services via OAuth, leverage built-in tools for research and file processing, and schedule recurring or one-time tasks that deliver results to any supported channel.

## Third-party integrations

Wingman integrates with Composio to provide OAuth-based access to popular SaaS platforms. No additional API keys or setup is required—your Wingman can authenticate with services on your behalf and perform actions in chat or scheduled tasks.

**Supported categories include:**

- **Productivity** – Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Notion, Airtable, Asana, Trello
- **Communication** – Slack, Discord, Telegram, Gmail, Outlook
- **Developer tools** – GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Figma
- **Marketing & CRM** – HubSpot, Salesforce, Mailchimp, Intercom
- **Finance & payments** – Stripe, QuickBooks, PayPal

<Note>
The full catalog of 300+ integrations is available directly in chat. Ask your Wingman "What integrations do you support?" or "Connect to GitHub" to browse and authenticate.
</Note>

Your Wingman will request OAuth consent when first connecting to a service. Tokens are stored securely and refreshed automatically; you can revoke access at any time from the workspace settings.

## Built-in capabilities

In addition to third-party integrations, every Wingman includes native tools that run without external APIs:

| Capability | What it does |
|------------|--------------|
| **Web search** | Real-time internet search for current information, news, and research |
| **File analysis** | Read and parse uploaded documents—PDFs, spreadsheets, images, CSVs—directly in chat |
| **Code execution** | Run Python snippets, data transformations, and calculations in a sandboxed environment |
| **Memory** | Persistent context across conversations; the Wingman remembers prior discussions and preferences |

These capabilities are always available and consume credits from your workspace balance. See [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging) for pricing.

## Scheduled tasks

Wingmen can execute tasks on a schedule—daily summaries, weekly reports, periodic data syncs—and deliver the output to any [supported channel](/channels-web-telegram-whatsapp-imessage-slack).

### Creating a task

<Steps>
<Step title="Describe the task in chat">
Tell your Wingman what you need: *"Every Monday at 9 AM, pull my GitHub pull requests and send a summary to Slack."*
</Step>

<Step title="Confirm the schedule and delivery channel">
The Wingman will propose a cron expression or natural-language schedule and ask which channel to use (Web, Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, or Slack).
</Step>

<Step title="Review and approve">
Once confirmed, the task is registered. You'll see it listed in the **Tasks** panel of your workspace.
</Step>
</Steps>

### One-time vs. recurring

- **Recurring tasks** run on a fixed schedule (daily, weekly, monthly, or custom cron).
- **One-time tasks** execute once at a specified date and time, then are archived.

Both types support the same integrations, built-in capabilities, and delivery channels.

### Delivery channels

Task output is sent to the channel you choose:

- **Web** – appears in your Wingman's chat interface
- **Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage** – delivered as a message to your linked account
- **Slack** – posted to a channel or DM

<Tip>
Use the **Slack** channel for team-wide reports, and **Telegram** or **WhatsApp** for personal mobile notifications.
</Tip>

See [Channels](/channels-web-telegram-whatsapp-imessage-slack) for setup instructions.

## Credit-based execution

Scheduled tasks consume workspace credits each time they run. The cost depends on the integrations invoked, the complexity of the task, and the LLM reasoning required.

### Pausing and auto-resume

<Warning>
If your workspace credits fall below the threshold needed to execute a task, that task is **paused automatically**. You will receive a notification via your default channel.
</Warning>

- **Paused tasks** do not run or incur charges.
- When you recharge your workspace, paused tasks **auto-resume** at the next scheduled interval.
- You can also manually pause or delete tasks from the **Tasks** panel.

This failsafe ensures you never run out of credits mid-execution and always maintain control over recurring spend.

## Managing tasks

The **Tasks** panel in your workspace sidebar lists all scheduled jobs, their next run time, status, and delivery channel.

**Actions you can take:**

- **Edit** – change the schedule, delivery channel, or task logic
- **Pause / Resume** – temporarily disable a task without deleting it
- **Delete** – permanently remove the task
- **View logs** – inspect past runs, output, and any errors

<Accordion title="Can I schedule tasks for my deployed app?">
Yes. Your app's backend code can also define scheduled jobs using standard cron syntax or background workers. See [Scheduled tasks & background jobs in your app](/scheduled-tasks-background-jobs-in-your-app) for implementation details.
</Accordion>

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Channels" icon="message-square" href="/channels-web-telegram-whatsapp-imessage-slack">
Connect Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage, or Slack for task delivery
</Card>
<Card title="Credit expiry & recharging" icon="coins" href="/credit-expiry-recharging">
Understand workspace credits and how to top up
</Card>
<Card title="File storage" icon="folder" href="/file-storage-emergent-object-store">
Upload files for analysis or use in tasks
</Card>
<Card title="Glossary" icon="book-open" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
Look up platform-specific terms and concepts
</Card>
</CardGroup>
integrations-scheduled-tasks.description: 300+ OAuth integrations per Wingman (via Composio), built-in capabilities (web search, file analysis, code execution, memory), and recurring/one-time scheduled tasks with delivery

rollback-when-the-agent-goes-wrong.title: Rollback when the agent goes wrong
rollback-when-the-agent-goes-wrong.content:
## When to use rollback

Rollback lets you revert your entire app—code, configuration, and deployment—to an earlier state in its history. Use it when the agent has introduced a breaking change, removed a working feature, or left the app in an undesired state.

Common scenarios:

- The agent refactored code and broke an API endpoint that was working.
- A UI change removed navigation or critical buttons.
- The agent misunderstood your instruction and deleted files you need.
- Performance degraded after a dependency update.

<Tip title="Rollback is non-destructive">
Your current state is preserved as a new snapshot before the rollback completes, so you can always roll *forward* again if you change your mind.
</Tip>

## How to roll back

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the history panel">
In the workspace, click the **History** icon in the left sidebar. You'll see a timeline of snapshots—each represents a point after the agent stopped or you manually saved.
</Step>

<Step title="Preview the snapshot">
Click any earlier snapshot to see a diff of what changed between that point and your current state. Files added, modified, or deleted are highlighted.
</Step>

<Step title="Confirm the rollback">
Click **Rollback to this version**. The platform will restore all code, environment variables, dependencies, and configuration from that snapshot and redeploy the app. Your current state is saved as a new snapshot labeled "Before rollback."
</Step>
</Steps>

The app restarts automatically; the deployment URL remains the same.

## Rollback vs Git push/pull

Rollback operates on **the platform's internal snapshots**, which capture the full deployed state—code, env vars, runtime config, and database schema metadata. It does not interact with your GitHub repository.

| Rollback | Git push/pull |
|----------|---------------|
| Reverts to a platform snapshot instantly | Syncs code with your GitHub branch |
| Includes env vars, dependencies, runtime config | Code and `package.json` only |
| Redeploys automatically | Requires manual redeploy or agent run |
| No Git knowledge needed | Requires Git workflow familiarity |

If you've connected a GitHub repo and pushed changes to it, rolling back in Emergent **does not** rewrite your Git history. The repository remains at its current HEAD. To synchronize, you would need to manually push the rolled-back code or use [Pull from GitHub](/pull-from-github-with-caution) (with caution).

<Warning title="Pulling from GitHub can overwrite platform state">
If you roll back in Emergent and then pull from GitHub, the pull may re-introduce the broken code. Roll back *or* pull—rarely both in sequence.
</Warning>

## Rollback vs forking

Both let you explore an earlier state, but they serve different purposes:

**Rollback** reverts *this app* in place. Use it when:

- The current state is broken and you want to undo recent changes.
- You're confident the earlier version is what you need going forward.
- You want to preserve the same deployment URL and database.

**Forking** creates a *new app* branching from a snapshot. Use it when:

- You want to experiment with an alternative direction without losing your current progress.
- You're building a variant (e.g., a white-label version or feature branch).
- You want to compare two approaches side-by-side.

For full forking details, see [Forking](/forking).

<Info>
Think of rollback as "undo" and forking as "duplicate and diverge."
</Info>

## What gets rolled back

A rollback restores:

- All source code files
- `package.json` and installed dependencies
- Environment variables
- Runtime configuration (Node version, build commands)
- Database schema metadata (collection names, indexes)

**Not included:**

- Database *data* (records in MongoDB remain unchanged; rollback does not revert documents)
- External integrations or API keys stored outside the platform
- Custom domain DNS records

<Note>
If a schema change in the rolled-back code is incompatible with your current data, you may see runtime errors until you manually migrate or clean up the database. The platform does not auto-migrate data on rollback.
</Note>

## Tips for effective rollback

- **Snapshot often.** Save a manual snapshot before asking the agent to make risky changes (e.g., "refactor the entire backend").
- **Review diffs carefully.** The preview shows every file change; scan for unintended deletions.
- **Test after rollback.** The deployment is automatic, but always verify critical features work as expected.
- **Combine with forking for experiments.** If you're unsure whether to keep or discard recent work, fork from the earlier snapshot and compare the two apps.

Rollback is a safety net, not a substitute for clear instructions. The more specific you are in chat, the less you'll need to roll back.
rollback-when-the-agent-goes-wrong.description: 1. Use rollback to revert to an earlier state when the agent breaks a working feature.

what-kind-of-apps-you-can-build.title: What kind of apps you can build?
what-kind-of-apps-you-can-build.content:
## Overview

Emergent is a general-purpose platform for building production-ready applications. Whether you're prototyping an idea, shipping an internal dashboard, or deploying a customer-facing SaaS product, Emergent's agentic workflow handles the full stack—frontend, backend, database, hosting, and deployment.

You describe what you want in chat. The platform's AI agents write the code, test it, and deploy it live. No frameworks to learn, no infrastructure to configure.

<Callout type="tip" title="Not just prototypes">
Emergent apps are real, production-grade projects. You get a live URL, custom domains, database persistence, and the ability to iterate continuously as your needs evolve.
</Callout>

---

## For Individuals

Perfect for personal projects, creative experiments, and side hustles.

**Common use cases:**

- **Portfolios & personal websites** — showcase your work with a custom design and domain
- **Habit trackers & productivity tools** — build exactly the tracker you need, tailored to your workflow
- **Learning projects** — test ideas, experiment with features, iterate without setup overhead
- **Content hubs** — blogs, newsletters, link-in-bio pages
- **Micro-SaaS MVPs** — validate a product idea before committing to a full build

All apps come with built-in hosting and a live URL. Add a [custom domain](/custom-domain) to make it truly yours.

---

## For Small & Medium Businesses

Emergent helps teams ship tools faster—without hiring a dev team or waiting months for an agency.

**Common use cases:**

- **Internal dashboards** — visualize KPIs, track operations, manage workflows
- **Customer portals** — let clients view orders, book appointments, submit requests
- **CRM & lead management** — custom tools that fit your sales process
- **E-commerce storefronts** — product catalogs, checkout flows, order tracking
- **Event & booking platforms** — handle registrations, payments, scheduling
- **Marketing landing pages** — quickly spin up campaign-specific pages with forms and analytics

<Info>
Teams often start with a simple MVP in Emergent, then expand it iteratively as they learn what works. The same app can evolve from a prototype to a production workhorse without platform migration.
</Info>

Integration with third-party services (Stripe, Twilio, analytics providers) is straightforward—just describe the integration you need. See [Custom & MCP integrations](/custom-mcp-integrations) for details.

---

## For Enterprises

Emergent supports complex, multi-user applications with authentication, role-based access, and scalable architecture.

**Common use cases:**

- **Enterprise dashboards & reporting tools** — aggregate data from multiple sources, support large user bases
- **Workflow automation platforms** — custom approval chains, ticket systems, process management
- **Customer-facing SaaS products** — multi-tenant apps with user accounts, billing, analytics
- **Data collection & admin panels** — manage large datasets, moderate content, enforce compliance
- **White-label platforms** — deploy customized instances for different clients or regions

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Persistent database" icon="database">
    Every app includes a MongoDB instance for structured data persistence. See [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Custom agents" icon="wand-sparkles">
    Extend the platform's capabilities with domain-specific logic. See [Custom agents](/custom-agents).
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

<Warning title="Performance at scale">
If your app handles high traffic or compute-intensive tasks, monitor performance early. See [App slow, crashing or cold-starting](/app-slow-crashing-or-cold-starting) for optimization guidance.
</Warning>

---

## Mobile & Cross-Platform

Emergent builds both web and mobile apps. You can also convert an existing web app to mobile (or vice versa) without starting over.

- **Native mobile apps** — iOS and Android from a single codebase
- **Responsive web apps** — optimized for desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers
- **Progressive Web Apps (PWAs)** — installable, offline-capable web experiences

<Tip>
Describe "make this mobile-friendly" or "convert this to a native app" in chat, and agents will adapt the UI and interactions automatically. Learn more: [Web ↔ Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical).
</Tip>

---

## What's Next

<Steps>
  <Step title="Explore the workspace">
    Get familiar with the chat interface, preview pane, and deployment controls. See [A tour of the workspace](/a-tour-of-the-workspace).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Start building">
    Describe your first app in chat. Be as detailed or high-level as you like—agents will ask clarifying questions.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Deploy & iterate">
    Once you're happy with the preview, deploy live. You can continue refining in chat even after launch.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info">
Not sure where to start? Browse the [Glossary of Emergent terms](/glossary-of-emergent-terms) to understand key concepts, or jump straight into chat and describe what you want to build.
</Callout>
what-kind-of-apps-you-can-build.description: Full-stack web apps, mobile apps, landing pages, MVPs, dashboards, internal tools, e-commerce - projects of any scale.

clerk.title: Clerk
clerk.content:
## Overview

Clerk is a complete authentication and user management platform that integrates seamlessly with Emergent applications. It provides pre-built UI components for sign-in, sign-up, and user profiles, along with session management, multi-factor authentication, and social login providers.

When you integrate Clerk with your Emergent app, you get production-ready authentication without building forms, handling password resets, or managing session tokens yourself.

<Note>
Clerk offers a generous free tier that's perfect for prototyping and small applications. You'll need to create a Clerk account at [clerk.com](https://clerk.com) to get your API keys.
</Note>

## When to use Clerk

Clerk is ideal when your application needs:

- **User sign-up and sign-in** with email, phone, or social providers (Google, GitHub, etc.)
- **User profiles** that users can edit themselves
- **Session management** with automatic token refresh
- **Role-based access control** to restrict features by user type
- **Multi-factor authentication** for security-sensitive apps

If you only need to store data without user accounts, consider using [MongoDB](/database-mongodb) directly instead.

## Setting up Clerk

<Steps>
<Step title="Create a Clerk application">
Visit [clerk.com/dashboard](https://dashboard.clerk.com) and create a new application. Choose your preferred sign-in methods (email, social providers, etc.). Clerk will generate API keys for you.
</Step>

<Step title="Copy your API keys">
In the Clerk dashboard, navigate to **API Keys**. You'll need:

- **Publishable Key** (starts with `pk_test_` or `pk_live_`)
- **Secret Key** (starts with `sk_test_` or `sk_live_`)

Keep the Secret Key private — it grants full access to your Clerk data.
</Step>

<Step title="Tell Emergent to add Clerk">
In your Emergent chat, describe what you want:

> "Add Clerk authentication. Users should be able to sign in with email and Google. Show a sign-in button in the header when logged out, and the user's profile picture when logged in."

The AI agents will install the Clerk SDK, add the required environment variables, and build the UI components you described.
</Step>

<Step title="Add your keys as environment variables">
Once the agents scaffold the integration, you'll need to provide your Clerk keys. In your app settings or during deployment, set:

```bash
CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_...
CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
```

<Warning>
Never commit secret keys to your repository. Use Emergent's environment variable management or your deployment platform's secrets manager.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Test the authentication flow">
Preview your app and try signing up as a new user. Verify that:

- The sign-in UI appears correctly
- You can create an account and sign in
- Protected pages redirect unauthenticated users
- Sign-out works as expected
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common integration patterns

### Protecting routes

Tell Emergent which pages require authentication:

> "Make the /dashboard page require login. Redirect to sign-in if the user isn't authenticated."

The agents will wrap those routes with Clerk's authentication middleware.

### Accessing user data

You can reference the current user in your prompts:

> "On the dashboard, show a welcome message with the user's first name from Clerk."

The agents will use Clerk's API to fetch and display user information.

### Adding user roles

For apps with different user types:

> "Add a 'role' field to users in Clerk. Admins should see an extra menu item. Regular users shouldn't."

Clerk supports custom metadata on user objects. The agents will read this metadata to control UI visibility or API access.

## Frontend vs. backend authentication

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Frontend (React/Next.js)">
Clerk provides React hooks and components:

- `<SignIn />`, `<SignUp />`, `<UserButton />` — drop-in UI components
- `useUser()` — access current user data
- `useAuth()` — check authentication status

Emergent's AI agents use these automatically when you describe authentication features.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Backend (API routes)">
For server-side routes (e.g., API endpoints), Clerk validates session tokens:

- Middleware verifies the user's session
- You get access to `userId` in your route handlers
- Unauthorized requests return `401 Unauthorized`

Tell Emergent which API routes need protection, and the agents will add the necessary middleware.
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Styling and customization

Clerk's default UI components match most designs, but you can customize them:

> "Use my app's primary color (#4F46E5) for the Clerk sign-in button."

Or request fully custom UI:

> "Don't use Clerk's pre-built forms. Build a custom login form that calls Clerk's API directly."

The agents can implement either approach depending on your needs.

## Testing with development keys

<Info>
Clerk provides separate keys for development (`pk_test_...`) and production (`pk_live_...`). Use test keys while building your app in Emergent. Switch to live keys when you deploy to production.
</Info>

Development keys allow unlimited users and requests, making them perfect for iterating on your app. User data in test mode is isolated from production.

## Webhooks and advanced features

For advanced use cases, you can ask Emergent to set up:

- **Webhooks** — sync Clerk user events to your database
- **Organizations** — multi-tenant apps where users belong to teams
- **Custom session claims** — embed additional data in auth tokens

Example prompt:

> "When a user signs up in Clerk, create a MongoDB document for them with their email and a default settings object."

The agents will configure a Clerk webhook and write the handler to process new user events.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Sign-in component doesn't appear">
Check that `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` is set correctly in your environment variables. The publishable key is safe to expose in client-side code.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Users see 'Clerk: Development Instance' banner">
This banner appears when using test keys (`pk_test_...`). It disappears automatically when you switch to production keys (`pk_live_...`).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="API routes return 401 even when signed in">
Ensure your backend has access to `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`. Frontend authentication and backend authentication use different keys — both must be set.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Custom domain redirect issues">
If you've set up a [custom domain](/custom-domain), update your Clerk dashboard to allow redirects to your custom domain. Add it under **Allowed redirect URLs**.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next steps

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="MongoDB Integration" icon="database" href="/database-mongodb">
Store user-specific data alongside Clerk authentication
</Card>
<Card title="Custom Domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Configure production domains for your authenticated app
</Card>
</CardGroup>

app-takedown-content-moderation.title: App takedown & content moderation
app-takedown-content-moderation.content:
## Why apps are sometimes taken down

Emergent runs automated content-policy and phishing screening on all deployed apps to keep the platform safe and trustworthy for everyone. If an app triggers these filters—even by mistake—it may be automatically taken offline.

<Callout type="info" title="False positives happen">
Automated moderation occasionally flags legitimate apps. We provide a simple dispute and recovery path so you're never permanently locked out of your work.
</Callout>

Common triggers include:

- Phishing keywords or suspicious login flows (e.g. credential harvesting forms)
- Malicious content or content-policy violations (harassment, spam, illegal material)
- Impersonation of well-known brands or services
- Misleading or deceptive UI patterns

## What happens when your app is flagged

1. **Immediate takedown:** The live deployment is removed from public access; the public URL returns a `403 Forbidden` or takedown notice.
2. **Notification:** You receive an email and in-workspace alert explaining the reason for takedown.
3. **Source code remains safe:** Your workspace, chat history, and code are **not deleted**—only the public deployment is affected.

<Warning>
Your credits are **not** refunded for apps taken down after deployment. The deployment consumed platform resources (build, hosting), so the charge stands.
</Warning>

## How to dispute or fix the issue

<Steps>
<Step title="Review the takedown notice">
Check your email and workspace notifications for the specific policy violation cited. Many false positives stem from keywords in placeholder text, demo content, or authentication flows.
</Step>

<Step title="Submit a dispute (false positive)">
If you believe your app was flagged in error, click **Dispute takedown** in the workspace banner or reply to the notification email. Include:

- A brief description of the app's purpose
- Why the flagged content is legitimate (e.g. "auth form is for a real user login, not phishing")

Our support team reviews disputes within **24 hours** on business days. If approved, your app is restored to its original public URL.
</Step>

<Step title="Fix and redeploy (genuine violation)">
If the takedown was correct—or if you prefer to fix the issue rather than wait for review—edit your app in the workspace:

1. Ask the agent to remove or reword the problematic content
2. Test the changes in preview
3. Click **Deploy** to publish a new version

The new deployment will be re-screened automatically. If it passes, it goes live immediately.
</Step>

<Step title="Fork and replace (persistent issues)">
If a specific workspace or app keeps triggering false positives, you can **fork** the project:

1. Export your code (via **Download** in the workspace)
2. Start a new workspace and upload or describe the app again
3. Deploy from the clean slate

The new deployment gets a fresh URL and a new screening pass.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Preventing false positives

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Avoid phishing keywords" icon="shield-alert">
Words like "verify your account," "urgent action required," or fake login prompts trigger phishing filters. Use clear, honest language in forms and CTAs.
</Card>

<Card title="Label demo content clearly" icon="tag">
If your app includes placeholder or test data that resembles policy violations (e.g. fake reviews, mock scams for educational purposes), add visible labels like **"Demo only"** or **"Example content"**.
</Card>

<Card title="Use real branding sparingly" icon="palette">
Avoid using trademarked logos, brand names, or UI that mimics well-known services unless you have permission or a clear parody/educational use case.
</Card>

<Card title="Review before deploy" icon="eye">
Preview your app in the workspace before publishing. Look for anything a moderation system might misinterpret as malicious.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Appeals and repeat offenders

- **First takedown:** Dispute or fix freely; no penalty.
- **Multiple violations:** Repeated policy breaches (especially after disputes are rejected) may result in account suspension or permanent bans.
- **Malicious intent:** Apps designed to harm users, steal credentials, or violate laws result in immediate account termination with no refund.

<Tip>
Emergent's moderation is designed to be lenient for edge cases. If you're building something unconventional (satire, security research, etc.), reach out to support **before** deploying so we can whitelist or review it manually.
</Tip>

## Related topics

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="How apps work here" icon="lightbulb" href="/how-apps-work-here-mental-model">
Understand the deployment and lifecycle of Emergent apps
</Card>

<Card title="How credits work" icon="coins" href="/how-credits-work">
Why credits are consumed even if an app is taken down
</Card>

<Card title="Custom domain" icon="globe" href="/custom-domain">
Point your own domain to a deployed app
</Card>

<Card title="Glossary" icon="book-open" href="/glossary-of-emergent-terms">
Key terms like "workspace," "deployment," and "fork"
</Card>
</CardGroup>
app-takedown-content-moderation.description: Deployed apps can be taken offline by automated content-policy/phishing screening; how to dispute and remedy via fork/replace.

database-mongodb.title: Database (MongoDB)
database-mongodb.content:
## Where your database lives

Your app's database is a **MongoDB connection string** (a URL), not a file on disk. By default, Emergent hosts your database on managed infrastructure — you don't need to provision or configure anything.

The connection string is injected into your app as the `MONGO_URI` environment variable at runtime. Your backend code (Express, Next.js API routes, etc.) uses this variable to connect:

```javascript
import { MongoClient } from 'mongodb';

const client = new MongoClient(process.env.MONGO_URI);
await client.connect();
const db = client.db();
```

<Info>
MongoDB runs on Emergent's managed cloud by default. You can also bring your own connection string (MongoDB Atlas, self-hosted, etc.) by setting `MONGO_URI` in your environment variables.
</Info>

---

## Preview vs Production database

<Warning title="Separate databases — data does not auto-sync">
**Preview** (the workspace VS Code) and **Production** (the deployed app at `yourapp.emergent.app`) use **separate MongoDB databases**. Changes you make in preview — new collections, documents, schema updates — do **not** automatically flow to production.
</Warning>

This is a common gotcha: you might add test data in preview, then deploy and wonder where it went. The production database starts empty (or retains whatever data was already there from prior deployments).

For more context on the preview/production split, see [Preview vs Deployed (separate)](/preview-vs-deployed-separate).

---

## Database behavior on redeploy vs replace

When you push a new deployment, Emergent offers two options:

<Columns cols={2}>
<Card title="Redeploy" icon="rotate-cw">
Updates code and dependencies but **keeps the existing production database** unchanged. Use this for most updates.
</Card>

<Card title="Replace" icon="refresh-ccw">
Tears down the entire production environment and rebuilds it. You choose whether to:
- Keep the existing production DB, or
- Start with a **fresh copy** of the preview database (useful for schema changes or resetting data).
</Card>
</Columns>

<Tip>
If you've made schema changes or want to seed production with preview data, use **Replace** and select "Copy preview database to production."
</Tip>

---

## Inspecting & exporting your database

Emergent provides two ways to browse and export your data:

### Database Manager (web UI)

The built-in **Database Manager** lets you browse collections and documents in both preview and production databases:

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the Database Manager">
Navigate to [mongoview.emergent.host](https://mongoview.emergent.host) and sign in with your Emergent account.
</Step>

<Step title="Select your environment">
Choose **Preview** or **Production** from the environment switcher in the top bar.
</Step>

<Step title="Browse collections">
Click any collection to view documents. You can filter, sort, and inspect individual records.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
The Database Manager is read-only for production databases to prevent accidental data loss. Preview databases are fully editable.
</Note>

### Exporting the preview database (mongodump)

You can export your preview database as a `.bson` dump file using `mongodump` directly in the workspace VS Code terminal:

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the terminal">
In the VS Code workspace, press `` Ctrl+` `` (or `Cmd+` on Mac) to open the integrated terminal.
</Step>

<Step title="Run mongodump">
```bash
mongodump --uri="$MONGO_URI" --out=./dump
```
This creates a `./dump` folder with `.bson` files for each collection.
</Step>

<Step title="Download the dump">
Right-click the `dump` folder in the VS Code file explorer and select **Download**. The folder will be zipped and saved to your local machine.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
Use `mongorestore` locally to import the dump into your own MongoDB instance for offline development or backup.
</Tip>

---

## Related topics

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="File storage (Emergent Object Store)" icon="folder-open" href="/file-storage-emergent-object-store">
How to store and serve user uploads, images, and other files
</Card>

<Card title="Database & data on mobile" icon="smartphone" href="/database-data-on-mobile">
Special considerations for mobile apps (React Native, Flutter)
</Card>

<Card title="Your data & ownership" icon="shield-check" href="/your-data-ownership">
Who owns your data and how to export it
</Card>

<Card title="Data privacy" icon="lock" href="/data-privacy">
How Emergent handles your data and user privacy
</Card>
</CardGroup>
